column2: Oʻzbekcha (uz). Machine-made by Claude: please have a native speaker check it.

column1: Very easy greetings for when you meet someone for the first time and when you say goodbye.
column2: Birinchi marta tanishganda va xayrlashganda aytiladigan juda oson salomlashuvlar.

column1: When you meet, say "안녕하세요?"; when you part, say "안녕히 가세요" or "안녕히 계세요".
column2: Uchrashganda "안녕하세요?" deng; xayrlashganda "안녕히 가세요" yoki "안녕히 계세요" deng.

column1: 안녕하세요? can be used in the morning, afternoon and evening. It is like "Hello".
column2: 안녕하세요? ertalab, tushdan keyin va kechqurun ishlatilaveradi. U "Assalomu alaykum" yoki "Salom" kabi.

column1: To the person leaving, say "안녕히 가세요"; to the person staying, say "안녕히 계세요".
column2: Ketayotgan odamga "안녕히 가세요", qolayotgan odamga "안녕히 계세요" deng.

column1: I say hello with a smile.
I say hello in the morning.
I'm Sam. Nice to meet you.
How have you been? (after a long time)
Long time no see. How have you been?
to be well, to be at peace
Hello. I'm Minha. Nice to meet you.
column2: Assalomu alaykum. Men Minhaman. Tanishganimdan xursandman.

column1: Words for saying thank you and sorry, and how to answer them.
column2: Rahmat va kechirasiz deyish hamda ularga javob berish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: When you are thankful, say "감사합니다"; when you are sorry, say "죄송합니다".
To older people or people above you, use "감사합니다" and "죄송합니다".
column2: Yoshi kattalarga yoki sizdan yuqoridagilarga "감사합니다" va "죄송합니다" deb ayting.

column1: The answer to "감사합니다" is "아니에요", and the answer to "죄송합니다" is "괜찮아요".
I buy a gift for my friend.
I'm sorry. I'll do it again.

column2: Yoʻq, men sizga rahmat aytishim kerak.

column1: Excuse me. May I come in?
Excuse me. Where is the restroom?
Easy words for asking and answering about names and age.
column2: Ism va yoshni soʻrash va javob berish uchun oson soʻzlar.

column1: Ask a name with "이름이 뭐예요?" and age with "몇 살이에요?".
column2: Ismni "이름이 뭐예요?", yoshni "몇 살이에요?" deb soʻrang.

column1: 씨 goes only after other people's names. Don't use it with your own name.
column2: 씨 faqat boshqa odamlarning ismidan keyin qoʻyiladi. Oʻz ismingiz bilan ishlatmang.

column1: For age, add "살", like "스무 살 (20 years old), 서른 살 (30 years old)".
column2: Yoshni aytishda "살" qoʻshing: "스무 살 (20 yosh), 서른 살 (30 yosh)".

column1: to give (주세요 = please give me / please do)
How old is your younger brother or sister?
Easy words for saying which country you are from and which language you speak.
column2: Qaysi davlatdan ekaningizni va qaysi tilda gaplashishingizni aytish uchun oson soʻzlar.

column1: Answer "어느 나라 사람이에요?" with "미얀마 사람이에요" (I'm from Myanmar).
column2: 어느 나라 사람이에요? savoliga "미얀마 사람이에요" (Men Myanmadanman) deb javob bering.

column1: Add "사람" after a country name = a person from that country; add "어" = that country's language: 한국 사람 (Korean person), 한국어 (Korean language).
column2: Davlat nomidan keyin "사람" qoʻshsangiz = oʻsha davlatdan boʻlgan odam; "어" qoʻshsangiz = oʻsha davlat tili: 한국 사람 (koreys), 한국어 (koreys tili).

column1: It's my first time in Korea.
to try, to have done (-아/어 보다)
Words for answering and for when you didn't understand. These are the most needed words when you start somewhere new.
column2: Javob berish va tushunmay qolganda aytiladigan soʻzlar. Yangi joyda boshlaganda eng kerakli soʻzlar shular.

column1: If you don't understand, say "다시 말해 주세요"; if you understand, say "알겠습니다".
If you say "네" when you didn't understand, there can be problems in class or at your part-time job. If you don't understand, always ask again.
column2: Tushunmay turib "네" desangiz, darsda yoki ishda muammo chiqishi mumkin. Tushunmasangiz, albatta qayta soʻrang.

column1: If someone speaks fast, ask: "천천히 말해 주세요" (Please speak slowly).
column2: Kimdir tez gapirsa, "천천히 말해 주세요" (Sekinroq gapiring) deb soʻrang.

column1: to be right, to be correct
to know (알겠어요 = I understand, got it)
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
Got it. I'll do it right away.
I don't know, I don't understand
I'm sorry, but please say it again.
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
Easy words for saying how you feel in one word.
column2: Hissiyot va kayfiyatni bir soʻz bilan aytish uchun oson soʻzlar.

column1: Say your feelings in one word, like "좋아요", "피곤해요". If your voice goes up at the end, it is a question.
column2: Hissiyotingizni bir soʻz bilan ayting: "좋아요", "피곤해요". Oxirida ovozingiz koʻtarilsa, bu savol boʻladi.

column1: Put "정말 (really)", "너무 (so, too)" or "조금 (a little)" in front to say how strong the feeling is.
column2: Hissiyot qanchalik kuchli ekanini aytish uchun oldiga "정말 (rostdan)", "너무 (juda, haddan tashqari)" yoki "조금 (biroz)" qoʻying.

column1: Raise your voice at the end to make it a question: "피곤해요?" (Are you tired?), "맛있어요?" (Is it delicious?).
column2: Savol qilish uchun oxirida ovozingizni koʻtaring: "피곤해요?" (Charchadingizmi?), "맛있어요?" (Mazalimi?).

column1: Are you tired? Take a rest.
I've been hungry since the morning.
Are you cold? Shall I close the door?
Ask with "뭐 (what), 어디 (where), 누구 (who), 언제 (when), 얼마 (how much)" and give short answers.
column2: 뭐 (nima), 어디 (qayer), 누구 (kim), 언제 (qachon), 얼마 (qancha) bilan soʻrang va qisqa javob bering.

column1: Ask with "뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마" and answer briefly.
column2: 뭐, 어디, 누구, 언제, 얼마 bilan soʻrang va qisqa javob bering.

column1: Raise your voice at the end of a question. Short answers are fine: "어디 가요?" (Where are you going?) "시장이요." (To the market.)
column2: Savolning oxirida ovozingizni koʻtaring. Qisqa javob ham boʻlaveradi: "어디 가요?" (Qayerga ketyapsiz?) "시장이요." (Bozorga.)

column1: Question words do not come at the start of the sentence like in English. They usually come just before the verb: "뭐 먹어요?" (What are you eating?).
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, soʻroq soʻzlari odatda feʼldan oldin keladi: "뭐 먹어요?" (Nima yeyapsiz?).

column1: How much is it all together?
Words for family members. The words for older brother and sister change depending on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
column2: Oila aʼzolari uchun soʻzlar. Aka va opa soʻzlari gapiruvchi erkak yoki ayol ekaniga qarab oʻzgaradi.

column1: Men say 형 and 누나; women say 오빠 and 언니.
column2: Erkaklar 형 va 누나, ayollar esa 오빠 va 언니 deydi.

column1: English has only "brother" and "sister", but Korean has four words for older siblings. A man says 형, 누나; a woman says 오빠, 언니.
column2: Oʻzbek tilida "aka" va "opa" hamma uchun bir xil, lekin koreys tilida aka-opa uchun toʻrtta soʻz bor. Erkak 형, 누나, ayol esa 오빠, 언니 deydi.

column1: 동생 is used for both boys and girls. To show which, say 남동생 (younger brother) or 여동생 (younger sister).
column2: 동생 ham oʻgʻil, ham qiz uchun ishlatiladi. Aniq aytish uchun 남동생 (uka) yoki 여동생 (singil) deng.

column1: When you become close at school, you can call older seniors or friends 형, 누나, 언니 or 오빠 even if they are not family.
column2: Maktabda yaqin boʻlib qolsangiz, oila aʼzosi boʻlmasa ham katta kursdosh yoki doʻstlarni 형, 누나, 언니 yoki 오빠 deb chaqirishingiz mumkin.

column1: It was my father's birthday, so I made a video call.
column2: Otamning tugʻilgan kuni boʻlgani uchun video qoʻngʻiroq qildim.

column1: (보고 싶다 = to miss, to want to see)
My mother is a good cook.
My mother is sick, so I'm worried.
I send money to my parents.
I send living money to my parents every month.
column2: Har oy ota-onamga yashash uchun pul yuboraman.

column1: My older brother is taller than me.
My older brother wants to study in Korea too.
My older brother is a university student.
I told my older brother the dates of my vacation.
to let someone know, to tell
My older sister is a nurse.
My older sister sent me wedding photos.
I live with my older sister.
My older sister bought me clothes.
My older sister helps me a lot with life in Korea.
column2: Opam Koreyadagi hayotimda menga koʻp yordam beradi.

column1: My younger brother is a high school student.
I have two younger brothers and sisters.
I pay my younger sibling's school fees.
My grandfather is sick, so I took time off.
column2: Bobom kasal boʻlgani uchun ishdan javob oldim.

column1: I'm going to my grandmother's house.
I bought Korean ginseng for my grandmother.
How many people are in your family?
Five. I have my parents, an older sister and a younger brother.
column2: Besh kishi. Ota-onam, opam va ukam bor.

column1: Words for talking about marriage and brothers and sisters.
column2: Turmush va aka-ukalar haqida gapirish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: Ask and answer about marriage with "결혼했어요?".
column2: Turmush qurganlik haqida "결혼했어요?" bilan soʻrang va javob bering.

column1: 결혼했어요 is in the past form, but it means "I am married now". If you are not married yet, say "아직 안 했어요".
column2: 결혼했어요 oʻtgan zamon shaklida, lekin "Hozir uylanganman / turmushdaman" degan maʼnoni beradi. Hali turmush qurmagan boʻlsangiz, "아직 안 했어요" deng.

column1: Koreans often ask if you are married, even the first time they meet you. You don't need to think it is rude.
column2: Koreyslar birinchi tanishganda ham koʻpincha turmush qurganingizni soʻrashadi. Buni odobsizlik deb oʻylashingiz shart emas.

column1: When do you want to get married?
My older sister got married last year.
My older brother is getting married in our hometown next year.
My older sister came to Korea with her husband.
My older sister is preparing her husband's visa documents.
column2: Opam erining vizasi uchun hujjatlarni tayyorlayapti.

column1: My friend's wife is a good cook.
My senior's wife is in Nepal.

column2: katta kursdosh (maktab yoki ishda oldin kelgan)

column1: Someday I want to travel the world with my wife.
column2: Bir kun xotinim bilan dunyo boʻylab sayohat qilmoqchiman.

column1: I'm the youngest son in my family.
My parents have only two sons.
My aunt's daughter goes to high school.
I'm an only daughter, so my parents worry a lot.
column2: Men yolgʻiz qiz farzandman, shuning uchun ota-onam juda xavotir olishadi.

column1: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
I miss my brothers and sisters back home.
I have no brothers or sisters. I'm an only child.
to not have, to not be (there)
how many people in the family
There are four people in my family.
Write on the form how many people are in your family.
column2: Oilangiz necha kishidan iboratligini anketaga yozing.

column1: Sam, do you have any brothers or sisters?
Yes, I have one younger sister.
You must miss your younger sister.
Words for describing how people look.
column2: Odamlarning tashqi koʻrinishini tasvirlash uchun soʻzlar.

column1: For a person's height, use "크다, 작다".
In English you just say "tall", but Korean says "키가 크다", with the word "키" (height). "높다" (high) is not used for people.
column2: Koreyschada boʻy haqida "키" (boʻy) soʻzi bilan "키가 크다" deyiladi. Oʻzbekchadagi "baland" kabi "높다" (baland) soʻzi odamlarga ishlatilmaydi.

column1: 잘생겼어요 and "닮았어요" use the past form to talk about how someone looks now.
column2: 잘생겼어요 va "닮았어요" oʻtgan zamon shaklida boʻlsa ham, kimningdir hozirgi koʻrinishi haqida gapiradi.

column1: I got slimmer because I exercise these days.
column2: Hozir sport bilan shugʻullanayotganim uchun ozdim.

column1: The man in the photo is handsome.
The tall person is the teaching assistant.
The tall person tidies the top shelf.
column2: Boʻyi baland odam yuqori tokchani tartibga soladi.

column1: I'm short, so I can't reach the top of the shelf.
column2: Boʻyim past boʻlgani uchun qoʻlim tokchaning yuqorisiga yetmaydi.

column1: My older sister and I look very alike.
column2: Opam bilan men bir-birimizga juda oʻxshaymiz.

column1: My younger sibling looks a lot like me.
My older sister has long hair.
My hair is long, so I tie it up.
column2: Sochim uzun boʻlgani uchun uni bogʻlab olaman.

column1: If your hair is long, tie it up when you cook.
column2: Sochingiz uzun boʻlsa, ovqat pishirganda bogʻlab oling.

column1: What does your younger brother look like?
He is tall and has short hair. He looks like me.
column2: U baland boʻyli, sochi qisqa. Menga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Words for describing a person's character. You hear them when people introduce friends or professors at school.
column2: Odamning feʼl-atvorini tasvirlash uchun soʻzlar. Maktabda doʻstlar yoki domlalarni tanishtirganda eshitasiz.
Feʼl-atvorni bildiruvchi koʻp soʻzlar "-하다" bilan tugaydi.

column1: At Korean schools and part-time jobs, the best praise is "성실하다" and "부지런하다".
column2: Koreya maktablari va ish joylarida eng katta maqtov "성실하다" va "부지런하다" hisoblanadi.

column1: Before a noun, change it to "-ㄴ/은": 친절한 사람 (a kind person), 조용한 방 (a quiet room).
column2: Otdan oldin "-ㄴ/은" shakliga oʻzgartiring: 친절한 사람 (mehribon odam), 조용한 방 (tinch xona).

column1: In English you say "She is kind" or "She is a kind person". In Korean, say "친절해요" or "친절한 사람이에요".
column2: Oʻzbekchada "U mehribon" yoki "U mehribon odam" deymiz. Koreyschada "친절해요" yoki "친절한 사람이에요" deng.

column1: The staff at this shop are always kind.
My new roommate is nice, so I'm happy.
column2: Yangi xonadoshim yaxshi, shuning uchun xursandman.

column1: It's fun to chat with friends during the break.
The dormitory is quiet, so I sleep well.
column2: Yotoqxona tinch, shuning uchun yaxshi uxlayman.

column1: My younger brother is outgoing and has many friends.
Outgoing people are good at welcoming customers.
column2: Dilkash odamlar mijozlarni yaxshi kutib oladi.

column1: I'm hard-working, so I get up early.
I studied diligently, so I got praise.
If you are lazy, it is hard to extend your contract.
The shop owner is looking for a sincere part-timer.
column2: Xoʻjayin vijdonli yarim kunlik ishchi qidiryapti.

column1: My older sister is warm and caring.
Minha is warm to her friends.
He is very sincere and hard-working.
Words about friends, neighbors and making friends.
column2: Doʻstlar, qoʻshnilar va doʻst orttirish haqida soʻzlar.

column1: 친구 is used between people of the same age.
In Korean, "친구" usually means someone of the same age. If the age is different, even close people call each other 형, 누나, 동생.
column2: Koreys tilida "친구" odatda tengdoshni bildiradi. Yoshi farq qilsa, yaqin odamlar ham bir-birini 형, 누나, 동생 deb chaqiradi.

column1: 남자 친구 and "여자 친구" mean boyfriend and girlfriend. For a friend who is just a friend, say "남자인 친구" (a friend who is a man).
column2: 남자 친구 va "여자 친구" yigit va qiz (sevgili) degan maʼnoni beradi. Shunchaki doʻst boʻlsa, "남자인 친구" (erkak doʻst) deng.

column1: I joined this club because a friend introduced me.
column2: Doʻstim tanishtirgani uchun bu toʻgarakka qoʻshildim.

column1: I say hello to my neighbor.
My neighbor was noisy, so I couldn't sleep.
column2: Qoʻshnim shovqin qilgani uchun uxlay olmadim.

column1: The two of them are dating.
I made a lot of friends.
I made friends at a Korean language group.
I watch a movie with my boyfriend.
My boyfriend is waiting in Bangladesh.
Please help me choose a birthday present for my girlfriend.
column2: Sevgilimning tugʻilgan kuniga sovgʻa tanlashga yordam bering.

column1: I have a close friend in Korea.
I became close to my dorm roommate.
column2: Yotoqxonadagi xonadoshim bilan yaqin boʻlib qoldim.

column1: Let me introduce my friend Aisha.
Nice to meet you. Are you two close?
Yes, we are friends from the same hometown.
column2: Ha, biz bir yurtdan boʻlgan doʻstlarmiz.

column1: Korean has two sets of numbers. This set is "일, 이, 삼", used for dates, money, phone numbers, floors and minutes.
column2: Koreys tilida ikki xil sonlar bor. Bu "일, 이, 삼" sonlari sana, pul, telefon raqami, qavat va daqiqalar uchun ishlatiladi.

column1: For dates, money, numbers, floors and minutes, use "일, 이, 삼".
column2: Sana, pul, raqam, qavat va daqiqalar uchun "일, 이, 삼" ishlating.

column1: Numbers are made in a regular way: 십일 (11 = ten-one), 이십 (20 = two-ten), 삼십오 (35 = three-ten-five). Unlike English "eleven" or "twenty", every number follows the rule.
column2: Sonlar bir qoida bilan tuziladi: 십일 (11 = oʻn-bir), 이십 (20 = ikki-oʻn), 삼십오 (35 = uch-oʻn-besh). Oʻzbekchadagi "yigirma", "oʻttiz" kabi alohida soʻzlar yoʻq, hamma son qoidaga boʻysunadi.

column1: Big numbers are counted in units of "만" (10,000). 100,000 is "십만" (ten 만), 1,000,000 is "백만" (a hundred 만). This is different from English, which groups by thousands.
column2: Katta sonlar "만" (10,000) birligida sanaladi. 100,000 "십만" (oʻn 만), 1,000,000 "백만" (yuz 만) boʻladi. Bu oʻzbekchadagi minglab sanashdan farq qiladi.

column1: Read phone numbers one digit at a time, and say 0 as "공".
column2: Telefon raqamlarini bittadan raqam qilib oʻqing, 0 ni "공" deng.

column1: Please go up to the 2nd floor.
Please use the restroom on the 2nd floor.
I extend my visa in three months.
My room is room 602 on the 6th floor.
I get my part-time pay on the 7th of every month.
Bus No. 8 stops in front of the school.
There is a test in September.
The last number of the phone number is nine.
We'll give you a ten percent discount.
What floor is the department office on?
하나, 둘, 셋 are used to count things and people, and to say the hour and age.
column2: 하나, 둘, 셋 narsalar va odamlarni sanash, soat va yoshni aytish uchun ishlatiladi.

column1: Before a counter word, they change to "한, 두, 세, 네".
column2: Hisob soʻzidan oldin ular "한, 두, 세, 네" ga oʻzgaradi.

column1: Before a counter word, the form changes: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네, 스물 → 스무. 한 개, 두 명, 세 시, 네 살, 스무 살.
column2: Hisob soʻzidan oldin shakl oʻzgaradi: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네, 스물 → 스무. 한 개, 두 명, 세 시, 네 살, 스무 살.

column1: When telling the time, "시" uses native Korean numbers (하나, 둘…) and "분" uses Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이…): 세 시 십 분 (3:10).
column2: Vaqtni aytganda "시" (soat) uchun sof koreys sonlari (하나, 둘…), "분" (daqiqa) uchun xitoy-koreys sonlari (일, 이…) ishlatiladi: 세 시 십 분 (3:10).

column1: May I ask one more thing?
The two of us go together.
The two of us lift this box together.
When I say one, two, three, we lift it together.
column2: Men bir, ikki, uch deganimda birga koʻtaramiz.

column1: Four of us share our room.
Do you have a table for five?
I eat dinner at six o'clock.
I get up at seven o'clock.
You must come to the library by seven o'clock.
I start my part-time job at eight o'clock.
I sleep eight hours a day.
The bank opens at nine o'clock.
I go to bed at ten o'clock.
Please be quiet after ten o'clock.
We have to move twenty boxes.
How to say dates and days of the week. Korean goes from big to small: year, month, day.
column2: Sana va hafta kunlarini aytish. Koreys tilida kattadan kichikka qarab aytiladi: yil, oy, kun.

column1: Say dates in the order year, month, day.
column2: Sanani yil, oy, kun tartibida ayting.

column1: The order is different from English: 13 November 2026 (or November 13, 2026) = 2026년 11월 13일. Korean goes year, month, day.
column2: Koreyschada tartib har doim yil, oy, kun: 2026-yil 13-noyabr = 2026년 11월 13일.

column1: June is read as "유월", and October as "시월".
It has been one year since I came to Korea.
The contract period is three years.
I go on vacation in December.
My scholarship comes in on the 25th.
There is a class on Monday mornings.
I go to the hospital on Tuesday.
There is a group meeting on Tuesday.
We throw out recycling on Tuesdays.
column2: Seshanba kunlari qayta ishlanadigan chiqindilarni tashlaymiz.

Words for talking about time, based on today.

column1: In the same way there are "이번 달, 지난달, 다음 달" (this month, last month, next month) and "올해, 작년, 내년" (this year, last year, next year).
column2: Xuddi shunday "이번 달, 지난달, 다음 달" (shu oy, oʻtgan oy, kelasi oy) va "올해, 작년, 내년" (bu yil, oʻtgan yil, kelasi yil) bor.

column1: Did the money I sent yesterday arrive?
I'm going to Greece the day after tomorrow.

There is a health check this week.
The things I ordered last week haven't come yet.
column2: Oʻtgan hafta buyurtma qilgan narsalarim hali kelmadi.

column2: Shanba kuni qoʻshimcha ishda ishlayman, yakshanba kuni dam olaman.

column1: How to say the hour and minutes. "시" and "분" use different numbers.
column2: Soat va daqiqani aytish. "시" va "분" uchun har xil sonlar ishlatiladi.

column1: For hours use "한, 두, 세"; for minutes use "일, 이, 삼".
column2: Soat uchun "한, 두, 세", daqiqa uchun "일, 이, 삼" ishlating.

column2: 시 uchun "한, 두, 세", "분" uchun "일, 이, 삼" ishlating: 세 시 삼십 분 (3:30).

column1: Korean uses the 12-hour clock and puts "오전" (a.m.) or "오후" (p.m.) in front, like a.m./p.m. in English. Do not say "13 o'clock".
column2: Koreys tilida odatda 12 soatlik tizim ishlatiladi va oldiga "오전" (tushdan oldin) yoki "오후" (tushdan keyin) qoʻyiladi. "Soat 13" demang.

column1: Lunch time starts at twelve o'clock.
column2: Tushlik vaqti soat oʻn ikkida boshlanadi.

column2: Faqat tushdan oldin bemor qabul qilishadi.

column2: Ertalab soat 7 gacha yotoqxona oshxonasiga keling.

column2: Soat ikki yarim. Uchda dars bor.

column2: 일어나다, 씻다, 먹다, 일하다, 쉬다, 자다 — kun uchun asosiy feʼllar.

column1: Meals are called "아침, 점심, 저녁". "아침" has two meanings: "morning" and "breakfast".
column2: Ovqatlar "아침, 점심, 저녁" deyiladi. "아침" ikki maʼnoga ega: "ertalab" va "nonushta".

column1: Put "에" after a time: 여섯 시에, 아침에.
column2: Vaqtdan keyin "에" qoʻying: 여섯 시에, 아침에.

I set an alarm and get up at five o'clock.

column2: Ovqat pishirgandan keyin qoʻlingizni yaxshilab yuving.

column2: Ikki soat oʻqib, oʻn daqiqa dam olaman.

I go straight home after class.
I go to bed at eleven o'clock.
I have an early class tomorrow, so I have to go to bed early.
column2: Ertaga erta darsim bor, shuning uchun erta yotishim kerak.

column1: What time do you usually get up?
I get up at six. And I have classes from nine.
column2: Soat oltida turaman. Toʻqqizdan darslarim bor.

column1: How to count Korean money and say prices. US money is called "달러" (dollars).
column2: Koreya pulini sanash va narxni aytish. AQSh puli "달러" (dollar) deyiladi.

column1: Ask the price with "얼마예요?" and answer with the "일, 이, 삼" numbers.
column2: Narxni "얼마예요?" deb soʻrang va "일, 이, 삼" sonlari bilan javob bering.

column1: For money, use the "일, 이, 삼" numbers. 1,000 won is not "일천 원", just "천 원".
column2: Pul uchun "일, 이, 삼" sonlarini ishlating. 1,000 von "일천 원" emas, shunchaki "천 원".

column1: Big amounts are grouped by "만". 1,500,000 won is "백오십만 원". This is important when you hear about tuition or scholarships.
column2: Katta summalar "만" bilan guruhlanadi. 1,500,000 von "백오십만 원" boʻladi. Bu kontrakt toʻlovi yoki stipendiya haqida eshitganda muhim.

column1: How many US dollars is one million won?
column2: Bir million von necha AQSh dollari boʻladi?

column1: How much is the dormitory fee for one month?
to not have, there is no

Does this vending machine take bills too?
column2: Bu avtomat qogʻoz pulni ham oladimi?

column2: Koreya oshxonalari va restoranlarida koʻp uchraydigan taomlar nomlari.

column2: Koreyscha ovqat guruch, shoʻrva va qoʻshimcha taomlardan iborat.

column1: Korean rice is not sticky rice, and you eat it with a spoon. Use chopsticks to pick up side dishes.
column2: Koreys guruchi yopishqoq guruch emas, uni qoshiq bilan yeyishadi. Qoʻshimcha taomlarni choʻp bilan oling.

column1: 밥 먹었어요? (Did you eat?) can be used as a greeting, like "How are you?".
column2: 밥 먹었어요? (Ovqatlandingizmi?) "Qalaysiz?" kabi salomlashish sifatida ishlatiladi.

column1: Rice, soup and side dishes (반찬) come out together. Side dishes are shared.
column2: Guruch, shoʻrva va qoʻshimcha taomlar (반찬) birga keladi. Qoʻshimcha taomlar umumiy boʻladi.

column1: I eat ramyeon when I study for exams.
We give you more rice for free.
Please leave the meat out of the bibimbap.
to take out, to leave out
When guests come, I serve bulgogi.

One cold noodle soup and one spicy mixed cold noodles, please.
column2: Bitta sovuq ugra shoʻrva va bitta achchiq aralash sovuq ugra bering.

column1: Kimchi is self-service. Please get it over there.
column2: Kimchini oʻzingiz olasiz. Anavi yerdan oling.

column2: Tushlikka soya pastali shoʻrva buyurtma qildim.

column2: Manzil eng katta joydan boshlanadi: shahar, tuman, mahalla, bino nomi, xona raqami.

column1: At a restaurant people say "주문하다"; for delivery or in casual speech, "시키다" is common.
column2: Oshxonada "주문하다" deyiladi; yetkazib berishda yoki oddiy nutqda "시키다" koʻp ishlatiladi.

column2: Toʻrt kishi bitta tovuqni boʻlishib yedik.

column1: A live fish is "물고기", and fish as food is "생선". English uses "fish" for both.
column2: Tirik baliq "물고기", ovqat sifatidagi baliq esa "생선". Oʻzbekchada ikkalasi ham "baliq".

column1: 달걀 and "계란" mean the same thing (egg).

column2: Bir geun (600 g) choʻchqa goʻshti bering.

column2: Uy ishlari uchun koʻp soʻzlar "-하다" bilan tugaydi.

column1: In Korea, you sort your trash. General trash must go in special bags that you buy.
column2: Koreyada chiqindilar saralanadi. Umumiy chiqindi sotib olinadigan maxsus paketlarga solinishi kerak.

column1: 씻다 is for washing with water, and "닦다" is for wiping or rubbing clean. For teeth, use "이를 닦다" (to brush your teeth).
column2: 씻다 suv bilan yuvish, "닦다" esa artish yoki ishqalab tozalash uchun. Tish uchun "이를 닦다" (tish yuvmoq) ishlating.

column1: We take turns cleaning the room.
I do the laundry on Sunday.
Tidy your dorm room before you move out.
column2: Koʻchib ketishdan oldin yotoqxona xonangizni tartibga keltiring.

column1: Some water spilled. Please wipe the floor.
I wash the dishes after eating.
Wash your dishes right after you eat.
I take out the trash at night.
Food waste must be thrown away separately.
I'll clean. Aisha, please take out the trash.
Words for living with roommates and neighbors. More about dormitory life is in University Life > Housing.
column2: Xonadoshlar va qoʻshnilar bilan yashash uchun soʻzlar. Yotoqxona hayoti haqida koʻproq maʼlumot Universitet hayoti > Turar joy boʻlimida.

column1: If there's a problem, say "~이/가 안 돼요".
If there is a problem in the dormitory, tell the manager "~이/가 안 돼요" (doesn't work) or "~이/가 고장 났어요" (is broken).
column2: Yotoqxonada muammo boʻlsa, mudirga "~이/가 안 돼요" (ishlamayapti) yoki "~이/가 고장 났어요" (buzildi) deng.

column1: Korean winters go below zero. If the heating doesn't work, tell someone right away.
column2: Koreyada qishda harorat noldan pastga tushadi. Isitish ishlamasa, darhol xabar bering.

column1: Place names often end in "-실" (room): 샤워실, 세탁실, 휴게실 (break room).
column2: Joy nomlari koʻpincha "-실" (xona) bilan tugaydi: 샤워실, 세탁실, 휴게실 (dam olish xonasi).

column1: There are a lot of rules.
If you don't follow the rules, you have to leave the dormitory.
column2: Qoidalarga rioya qilmasangiz, yotoqxonadan chiqib ketishingiz kerak.

column1: I live in the university dormitory.
The dormitory is next to the library.
I pay the dormitory fee every semester.
I do my laundry in the laundry room.
The laundry room is on the first floor.
Don't leave your laundry in the laundry room for a long time.
column2: Kirlaringizni kir yuvish xonasida uzoq qoldirmang.

column1: It's warm when you turn on the heating.
If the heating breaks, tell the manager.
to come out, to happen (열이 나다 = to have a fever)
column2: chiqmoq, sodir boʻlmoq (열이 나다 = isitmasi chiqmoq)

column1: Please turn on the air conditioning.
The air conditioning is too strong.
If the air conditioning is too strong, you'll catch a cold.
column2: Konditsioner juda kuchli boʻlsa, shamollab qolasiz.

column1: Put shared things back in their place.
The shower room is at the end of the hallway.
There is no hot water in the shower room.
The shower room is crowded in the morning.
column2: Ertalab dush xonasida odam koʻp boʻladi.

column1: My roommate is sleeping, so I'm quiet.
column2: Xonadoshim uxlayapti, shuning uchun jim turaman.

column1: It's exam period, so please be quiet at night too.
column2: Imtihon davri, shuning uchun kechasi ham jim boʻling.

column1: The heating in my room doesn't work.
Words for finding a room and signing a contract. In Korea there is a large sum of money called "보증금".
column2: Xona topish va shartnoma tuzish uchun soʻzlar. Koreyada "보증금" deb ataladigan katta summa bor.

column1: When you look for a room, ask about the 보증금, 월세 and 관리비.
column2: Xona qidirganda 보증금, 월세 va 관리비 haqida soʻrang.

column1: A 보증금 is money you leave when you move in and get back when you move out. Sometimes it is more than ten times the monthly rent.
column2: 보증금 — koʻchib kirganda qoldirib, koʻchib chiqqanda qaytarib oladigan pulingiz. Baʼzan u oylik ijaradan oʻn baravardan ham koʻp boʻladi.

column1: Be sure to get a copy of the contract and keep it. If there are words you don't understand, ask before you sign.
column2: Shartnoma nusxasini albatta olib, saqlab qoʻying. Tushunmagan soʻzlaringiz boʻlsa, imzolashdan oldin soʻrang.

column1: I asked the landlord to repair it.
to look for (a room, a job)
How much is the monthly rent for a studio?
column2: Bir xonali kvartiraning oylik ijarasi qancha?

column1: Studios near the station are expensive.
column2: Bekat yaqinidagi bir xonali kvartiralar qimmat.

column1: How much is the monthly rent?
I pay the rent by the 5th of every month.
You get the deposit back when you move out.
column2: Koʻchib chiqqaningizda garov pulini qaytarib olasiz.

column1: When you move, you must report your new address.
column2: Koʻchsangiz, yangi manzilingiz haqida xabar berishingiz kerak.

column1: Be sure to see the room before you sign the contract.
column2: Shartnoma tuzishdan oldin xonani albatta koʻring.

column1: Is the internet included in the maintenance fee?
In winter, the maintenance fee is high.
How much is the monthly rent for this studio?
column2: Bu bir xonali kvartiraning oylik ijarasi qancha?

column1: The deposit is 3,000,000 won and the monthly rent is 350,000 won.
column2: Garov puli 3,000,000 von, oylik ijara 350,000 von.

column1: Is there a maintenance fee too?
Names of things you use every day. These are the first things to buy when you arrive in Korea.
column2: Har kuni ishlatiladigan narsalar nomlari. Koreyaga kelganda birinchi sotib olinadigan narsalar shular.

column1: When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요".
When something is all used up, say "떨어졌어요": 휴지가 떨어졌어요 (The toilet paper has run out).
column2: Biror narsa tugab qolsa, "떨어졌어요" deng: 휴지가 떨어졌어요 (Hojat qogʻozi tugadi).

column1: In Korea, you throw toilet paper into the toilet. People also give toilet paper as a housewarming gift.
column2: Koreyada hojat qogʻozi unitazga tashlanadi. Yangi uyga koʻchganlarga sovgʻa sifatida hojat qogʻozi ham beriladi.

column1: I dry myself with a towel.
I wash my hands with soap.
The hand soap has run out.
I bought shampoo and conditioner together.
column2: Shampun va konditsionerni birga sotib oldim.

column1: Toothpaste and toothbrushes are cheap at Daiso.
column2: Tish pastasi va tish choʻtkasi Daisoda arzon.

column1: Pack your toothbrush when you go on a business trip.
column2: Xizmat safariga ketayotganda tish choʻtkangizni olib oling.

column1: The toilet paper has run out.
There is no toilet paper in the bathroom.
Please give me one more pillow.
The pillow is hard, so my neck hurts.
column2: Yostiq qattiq, shuning uchun boʻynim ogʻriyapti.

column1: Put in only a little detergent.
The detergent in the laundry room has run out.
column2: Kir yuvish xonasidagi kir yuvish vositasi tugab qoldi.

column1: I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?
column2: Supermarketga ketyapman. Sizga biror narsa kerakmi?

column1: Please buy me some toothpaste and toilet paper.
column2: Menga tish pastasi va hojat qogʻozi sotib oling.

column1: Names of parts of the body. You need them when you are sick or hurt.
column2: Tana aʼzolari nomlari. Kasal boʻlganda yoki jarohat olganda kerak boʻladi.

column1: Say where it hurts with "body part + 이/가 아파요".
column2: Qayeringiz ogʻriyotganini "tana aʼzosi + 이/가 아파요" bilan ayting.

column1: Say where it hurts with "~이/가 아파요". The order is the same as English: "My head hurts" = 머리가 아파요.
column2: Qayeringiz ogʻriyotganini "~이/가 아파요" bilan ayting. Tartib oʻzbekchadagi kabi: "Boshim ogʻriyapti" = 머리가 아파요.

column1: 머리 has two meanings: head and hair. 머리를 감다 (to wash your hair), 머리를 자르다 (to get a haircut).
column2: 머리 ikki maʼnoga ega: bosh va soch. 머리를 감다 (sochni yuvmoq), 머리를 자르다 (soch oldirmoq).

column1: 눈 (eye, snow), 배 (stomach, boat, pear) and 다리 (leg, bridge) have more than one meaning.
column2: 눈 (koʻz, qor), 배 (qorin, qayiq, nok) va 다리 (oyoq, koʻprik) bir nechta maʼnoga ega.

column1: I got dust in my eye.
If the smell is strong, cover your nose with a mask.
column2: Hid kuchli boʻlsa, burningizni niqob bilan yoping.

column1: I have sores in my mouth, so I can't eat.
column2: Ogʻzimda yara bor, shuning uchun ovqat yeya olmayman.

column1: My roommate snores, so I wear earplugs.
column2: Xonadoshim xurrak otadi, shuning uchun quloqqa tiqin taqaman.

column1: to be dry (목이 마르다 = to be thirsty)
My throat hurts, so I can't talk.
column2: Tomogʻim ogʻriyapti, shuning uchun gapira olmayman.

column1: I put a pain relief patch on my shoulder.
I wash my hands before I eat.
I have a stomachache, so I go to the bathroom often.
column2: Qornim ogʻriyapti, shuning uchun hojatxonaga tez-tez boraman.

column1: I lifted something heavy and hurt my back.
Be careful of your back when you lift things.
My leg hurts, so I can't walk.
column2: Oyogʻim ogʻriyapti, shuning uchun yura olmayman.

column1: I stood for a long time, so my legs are swollen.
column2: Uzoq turganim uchun oyoqlarim shishib ketdi.

column1: Something heavy fell on my foot.
Expressions for saying how you feel sick.
column2: Oʻzingizni qanday kasal his qilayotganingizni aytish uchun iboralar.

column1: For symptoms, say "~이/가 나다"; for illnesses, say "~에 걸리다".
column2: Alomatlar uchun "~이/가 나다", kasalliklar uchun "~에 걸리다" deng.

column1: Symptoms often use "나다": 열이 나다, 콧물이 나다, 피가 나다. It means something comes out of the body.
column2: Alomatlarda koʻpincha "나다" ishlatiladi: 열이 나다, 콧물이 나다, 피가 나다. Bu tanadan nimadir chiqishini bildiradi.

column1: Use "걸리다" for illnesses. Even if you are still sick now, use the past form "걸렸어요".
column2: Kasalliklar uchun "걸리다" ishlating. Hozir ham kasal boʻlsangiz, oʻtgan zamon shakli "걸렸어요" ishlatiladi.

column1: If you're sick, don't put up with it. Tell your professor "몸이 안 좋아요" (I don't feel well).
column2: Kasal boʻlsangiz, chidab yurmang. Domlangizga "몸이 안 좋아요" (Mazam yoʻq) deng.

column1: If you're sick, don't just put up with it. Tell someone.
column2: Kasal boʻlsangiz, shunchaki chidab yurmang. Kimgadir ayting.

column1: to put up with, to hold back
Be careful not to catch a cold.
I caught a cold, so I can't go to class today.
column2: Shamollab qolganim uchun bugun darsga bora olmayman.

column1: I had a fever at night.
If you have a fever, don't go to school. Go to the hospital.
column2: Isitmangiz boʻlsa, maktabga bormang. Kasalxonaga boring.

column1: I studied a lot for the exam, so I'm tired.
I ate bad food and got an upset stomach.
I had an upset stomach, so I ate rice porridge.
column2: Oshqozonim buzilgani uchun guruch boʻtqa yedim.

column1: I caught a cold, so I have a runny nose.
If you have a runny nose, wear a mask.
I coughed at night, so I couldn't sleep.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
If you feel dizzy, sit down.
I walked for a long time on a hot day, so I feel dizzy.
column2: Issiq kunda uzoq yurganim uchun boshim aylanyapti.

column1: I think I'm going to throw up.
I ate bad food and threw up.
Sam, you don't look well. Are you sick?
I caught a cold. I have a fever and a cough.
column2: Shamollab qoldim. Isitmam va yoʻtalim bor.

column1: Words you hear when you check in and see a doctor at a hospital.
column2: Kasalxonada roʻyxatdan oʻtish va shifokor koʻrigida eshitiladigan soʻzlar.

column1: At the hospital, the order is: check in, see the doctor, pay.
column2: Kasalxonada tartib: roʻyxatdan oʻtish, shifokor koʻrigi, toʻlov.

column1: When you go to the hospital, take your alien registration card and health insurance card.
column2: Kasalxonaga borganingizda chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangiz va tibbiy sugʻurta kartangizni oling.

column1: In Korea, if you are not very sick, you go to a local clinic first, not a big hospital. Clinics are divided by the part that hurts, such as 내과 (internal medicine), 정형외과 (orthopedics, bones) and 치과 (dentist).
column2: Koreyada juda kasal boʻlmasangiz, katta kasalxonaga emas, avval mahalliy klinikaga borasiz. Klinikalar ogʻriyotgan joyga qarab boʻlinadi: 내과 (ichki kasalliklar), 정형외과 (ortopediya, suyaklar), 치과 (stomatolog).

column1: For shots, use "맞다": 주사를 맞다 (to get a shot).
column2: Ukol uchun "맞다" ishlating: 주사를 맞다 (ukol olmoq).

column1: I have to go to the hospital.
I saw a doctor at the hospital.
Take your alien registration card when you go to the hospital.
column2: Kasalxonaga borganingizda chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangizni oling.

column1: Show the doctor where it hurts.
The nurse checked my blood pressure.
Show your health insurance card when you check in.
column2: Roʻyxatdan oʻtayotganda tibbiy sugʻurta kartangizni koʻrsating.

column1: Don't eat anything tomorrow morning and come for the test.
column2: Ertaga ertalab hech narsa yemay tahlilga keling.

column1: I was in the hospital for three days.
to be admitted to the hospital
I have to stay in the hospital for surgery.
If you are in the hospital, give a doctor's note to the school.
column2: Kasalxonada yotsangiz, maktabga shifokor maʼlumotnomasini topshiring.

column1: You have to wait to see the doctor.
On Saturdays, the clinic is open only in the morning.
column2: Shanba kunlari klinika faqat ertalab ishlaydi.

column1: If you have health insurance, hospital bills are cheap.
column2: Tibbiy sugʻurtangiz boʻlsa, kasalxona xarajatlari arzon.

column1: I've had a fever and a sore throat since yesterday.
column2: Kechadan beri isitmam bor va tomogʻim ogʻriyapti.

column1: Please write your name here and wait.
Words for buying medicine at a pharmacy and hearing how to take it.
column2: Dorixonada dori sotib olish va uni qanday ichishni eshitish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: For medicine, listen carefully for "how many times a day, after meals".
column2: Dori haqida "kuniga necha marta, ovqatdan keyin" degan soʻzlarni diqqat bilan tinglang.

column1: You must give the prescription from the hospital to the pharmacy to get your medicine. You can buy cold medicine, headache medicine and digestive medicine without a prescription.
column2: Dori olish uchun kasalxonadan berilgan retseptni dorixonaga berishingiz kerak. Shamollash, bosh ogʻrigʻi va hazm dorilarini retseptsiz sotib olish mumkin.

column1: Use "먹다" for medicine, "바르다" for ointment and "붙이다" for patches. Even for liquid medicine, say "먹다".
column2: Dori uchun "먹다", malham uchun "바르다", plastir uchun "붙이다" ishlating. Suyuq dori uchun ham "먹다" deyiladi.

column1: 식후 means after meals, and "식전" means before meals.
column2: 식후 ovqatdan keyin, "식전" esa ovqatdan oldin degani.

column1: How many times a day do I take the headache medicine?
column2: Bosh ogʻrigʻi dorisini kuniga necha marta ichaman?

column1: I put ointment on the cut.
Do you have ointment for burns?
The pharmacy is next to the hospital.
Is there a pharmacy open on Sunday?
Take this medicine 30 minutes after meals.
column2: Bu dorini ovqatdan 30 daqiqa keyin iching.

column1: Please give me some digestive medicine.
I took digestive medicine, so I'm OK now.
I ate too much, so I bought digestive medicine.
column2: Koʻp yeb qoʻyganim uchun hazm dorisi sotib oldim.

column1: Take this medicine twice a day.
column2: Bu dorini kuniga ikki marta iching.

column1: Will this medicine make me sleepy?
Take it three times a day.
Take it three times a day after meals.
column2: Kuniga uch marta ovqatdan keyin iching.

column1: Take it three times a day for three days.
column2: Uch kun davomida kuniga uch marta iching.

column1: You can't buy this medicine without a prescription.
column2: Bu dorini retseptsiz sotib olib boʻlmaydi.

column1: Give your prescription to the pharmacy and get your medicine.
Take this medicine three times a day, after meals.
column2: Bu dorini kuniga uch marta, ovqatdan keyin iching.

column1: For how many days do I take it?
Words for saying how you got hurt. If you get hurt, you must tell someone near you right away.
column2: Qanday jarohat olganingizni aytish uchun soʻzlar. Jarohat olsangiz, yoningizdagi odamga darhol aytishingiz kerak.

column1: If you get hurt, tell someone right away. In an emergency, call 119.
column2: Jarohat olsangiz, darhol kimgadir ayting. Favqulodda holatda 119 ga qoʻngʻiroq qiling.

column1: In an emergency, call 119. Say "여기 사람이 다쳤어요" (Someone is hurt here) and give the address.
column2: Favqulodda holatda 119 ga qoʻngʻiroq qiling. "여기 사람이 다쳤어요" (Bu yerda odam jarohatlandi) deb, manzilni ayting.

column1: If you get hurt at your part-time job, tell the owner even if it's a small cut. Part-time workers can also get treatment with industrial accident insurance (산재 보험).
column2: Qoʻshimcha ishda jarohat olsangiz, kichik kesilish boʻlsa ham xoʻjayinga ayting. Yarim kunlik ishchilar ham ishlab chiqarishdagi baxtsiz hodisalar sugʻurtasi (산재 보험) bilan davolanishi mumkin.
붓다 "부었어요" ga aylanadi: ㅅ tushib qoladi.

column1: Put ice on the swollen part.
If you get hurt while exercising, go to the hospital right away.
column2: Sport bilan shugʻullanayotganda jarohat olsangiz, darhol kasalxonaga boring.

column1: If you're bleeding, press it with a clean cloth.
column2: Qon ketsa, toza mato bilan bosib turing.

column1: I have to go to the emergency room.
At night, go to the emergency room.
If I'm sick at night, I go to the emergency room.
column2: Kechasi kasal boʻlsam, tez yordam boʻlimiga boraman.

column1: I think I broke my arm.
If a bone is broken, don't move.
I cut my hand on a knife.
I cut my finger on paper.
I put a bandage on my cut hand.
I got burned by hot water.
I burned my hand, so I cooled it with cold water.
column2: Qoʻlim kuyib qolgani uchun uni sovuq suvda sovutdim.

column1: If you get burned, keep it in cold water for a long time.
column2: Kuyib qolsangiz, uzoq vaqt sovuq suvda ushlab turing.

column1: Boss, Aisha hurt her hand. She's bleeding a lot.
column2: Xoʻjayin, Aisha qoʻlini jarohatladi. Qoni koʻp ketyapti.

column1: to come out (피가 나다 = to bleed)
Hold your hand up high. Let's go to the hospital now.
column2: Qoʻlingizni baland koʻtaring. Hozir kasalxonaga boraylik.

column1: Words for opening a bank account and taking out money at the bank.
column2: Bankda hisob ochish va pul yechish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: To open a bank account, take your ID to the bank.
column2: Bank hisobini ochish uchun shaxsingizni tasdiqlovchi hujjatni bankka olib boring.

column1: To open a bank account, you need your alien registration card and passport. Your scholarship and part-time pay go into your account.
column2: Bank hisobini ochish uchun chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartasi va pasport kerak. Stipendiya va ish haqingiz hisobingizga tushadi.

column1: Putting money in is "입금", and taking it out is "출금" or "돈을 찾다".
column2: Pul qoʻyish "입금", yechish esa "출금" yoki "돈을 찾다" deyiladi.

column1: Never lend your PIN or bank account to anyone. It is against the law.
column2: PIN-kodingiz yoki bank hisobingizni hech kimga bermang. Bu qonunga zid.

column1: I want to get a debit card.
Don't tell your PIN to anyone.
There is money in my account.
I want to open a bank account.
I check if my allowance came into my account.
Sign the same way as in your bankbook.
I take out money at the ATM.
Can I use a foreign card at the ATM?
column2: Bankomatda chet el kartasidan foydalansa boʻladimi?

column1: Please send it to this account.
Tell the department office your account for the scholarship.
column2: Stipendiya uchun hisob raqamingizni kafedra idorasiga ayting.

column1: At the bank, your alien registration card is your ID.
column2: Bankda chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangiz shaxsingizni tasdiqlovchi hujjat hisoblanadi.

column1: What time does the bank open?
I go to the bank and open an account.
I check my balance on the bank app.

column2: chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartasi (ID karta)

column1: I got my alien registration card.
column2: Chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartamni oldim.

column1: Please show me your alien registration card.
column2: Chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangizni koʻrsating.

column1: You need an alien registration card to open a bank account.
column2: Bank hisobini ochish uchun chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartasi kerak.

column1: Please give me your ID. And sign here.
column2: Hujjatingizni bering. Va bu yerga imzo qoʻying.

column1: Can I get a card too?
Words for sending money home and changing money.
column2: Vatanga pul yuborish va pul almashtirish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: When you send money, always ask about the fee and the exchange rate.
column2: Pul yuborganda doim komissiya va valyuta kursini soʻrang.

column1: In some countries, it is hard to change Korean money directly into the local money. Then people usually send or change it in dollars.
column2: Baʼzi davlatlarda Koreya pulini toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri mahalliy pulga almashtirish qiyin. Shunda odatda dollarda yuboriladi yoki almashtiriladi.

column1: To send money, you need the receiver's name, bank name and account number.
column2: Pul yuborish uchun oluvchining ismi, bank nomi va hisob raqami kerak.

column1: Giving money to a person who is not a bank to send it is illegal and dangerous.
column2: Bank boʻlmagan odamga pul berib yubortirish noqonuniy va xavfli.

column1: How much is the fee for sending money abroad?
column2: Chet elga pul yuborish komissiyasi qancha?

column1: My scholarship has been paid in.
The money hasn't come in. Please check.

column2: Taklif qilinsangiz, "초대해 주셔서 감사합니다" deng va kichik sovgʻa olib boring.

column1: When you are invited to a Korean home, don't go empty-handed. Bring something like fruit, drinks or toilet paper.
column2: Koreys uyiga taklif qilinsangiz, quruq qoʻl bilan bormang. Meva, ichimlik yoki hojat qogʻozi kabi narsa olib boring.

column1: For a housewarming, people give toilet paper or detergent. It means "may everything go smoothly."
column2: Yangi uyga koʻchish bazmiga hojat qogʻozi yoki kir yuvish vositasi sovgʻa qilinadi. Bu "hamma ishlaringiz silliq ketsin" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: In Korea, people eat seaweed soup on their birthday.
column2: Koreyada tugʻilgan kunda dengiz oʻti shoʻrvasi yeyiladi.

column1: I bought detergent as a housewarming gift.
column2: Yangi uy bazmiga sovgʻa sifatida kir yuvish vositasi sotib oldim.

column1: Guests are coming, so I'm preparing food.
column2: Mehmonlar kelyapti, shuning uchun ovqat tayyorlayapman.

column1: I buy a cake for my classmate's birthday.
column2: Kursdoshimning tugʻilgan kuniga tort sotib olaman.

column2: Shanba kuni yangi uy bazmi qilaman.

column2: Yangi uy bazmiga hojat qogʻozi olib boraman.

column1: I invited my roommate and friends to my housewarming party.
column2: Yangi uy bazmimga xonadoshim va doʻstlarimni taklif qildim.

The professor invited me to dinner.
column2: Domla meni kechki ovqatga taklif qildi.

They threw me a farewell party.
We're having a housewarming at my place on Saturday. Can you come?
column2: Shanba kuni uyimda yangi uy bazmi qilyapmiz. Kela olasizmi?

column1: Yes, thank you for inviting me. What should I bring?
column2: Ha, taklif qilganingiz uchun rahmat. Nima olib kelay?

column1: Words for saying no to plans or changing them. It is important to say it softly.
column2: Rejani rad etish yoki oʻzgartirish uchun soʻzlar. Buni yumshoq aytish muhim.

column1: Say no softly with "미안하지만 + reason + 다음에".
column2: Rad etishni "미안하지만 + sabab + 다음에" bilan yumshoq ayting.

column1: In Korean, people don't say no directly, like "싫어요" or "안 가요". Start with "미안하지만" or "죄송하지만" and give a reason.
column2: Koreys tilida "싫어요" yoki "안 가요" kabi toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri yoʻq deyilmaydi. "미안하지만" yoki "죄송하지만" bilan boshlang va sababini ayting.

column1: Using "-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요" sounds softer: 못 갈 것 같아요 (I don't think I can go).
column2: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 ishlatish yumshoqroq eshitiladi: 못 갈 것 같아요 (Bora olmasam kerak).

column1: With older people or professors, use "죄송하지만" instead of "미안하지만".
column2: Yoshi kattalar yoki domlalar bilan "미안하지만" oʻrniga "죄송하지만" ishlating.

column1: I'm tired today. See you next time.
I want to cancel my reservation.

column2: Kasalxonadagi qabulimni bekor qilish uchun qoʻngʻiroq qildim.

We'll put off our plans until next week.
I put off my vacation until next month.

The library is busy during exam period.
column2: Imtihon davrida kutubxonada odam koʻp boʻladi.

column1: I think I'll be about 10 minutes late.
There's a traffic jam, so I'll be a little late.
Sorry, but could you help me?
I'm sorry, but today is not OK.
I'm sorry, but I can't come to the group meeting today.
column2: Kechirasiz, lekin bugun guruh yigʻilishiga kela olmayman.

column1: I have something to do that day.
Something came up suddenly, so I can't go.
column2: Toʻsatdan ish chiqib qoldi, shuning uchun bora olmayman.

column2: Immigratsiya idorasiga borishim kerak, shuning uchun tushdan keyingi darsimga bora olmayman.

column1: Shall we have dinner together this evening?
column2: Bugun kechqurun birga kechki ovqat qilamizmi?

column1: I'm sorry, but I have something to do today.
Yes, let's definitely go next time.
Words for happy and sad events, like weddings, first birthday parties and funerals. People also go to the events of their seniors and TAs at school.
column2: Toʻy, birinchi tugʻilgan kun va dafn marosimi kabi quvonchli va qaygʻuli tadbirlar uchun soʻzlar. Maktabda katta kursdoshlar va assistentlarning tadbirlariga ham boriladi.

column1: At a wedding, give 축의금 and say "축하합니다".
At a wedding, you put money in a white envelope and write your name on it. It is money instead of a gift.
column2: Toʻyda pulni oq konvertga solib, ustiga ismingizni yozasiz. Bu sovgʻa oʻrniga beriladigan pul.

column1: At a funeral, you must not say "축하합니다". Greet quietly and give money (조의금).
column2: Dafn marosimida "축하합니다" deyish mumkin emas. Jimgina hamdardlik bildiring va pul (조의금) bering.

column1: Korean weddings are short, about one hour. After the ceremony, guests eat and then leave.
column2: Koreys toʻylari qisqa, taxminan bir soat. Marosimdan keyin mehmonlar ovqatlanib, ketishadi.

column1: How much wedding gift money do people give?
I put the wedding gift money in an envelope.
I gave 50,000 won as gift money at my senior's wedding.
column2: Katta kursdoshimning toʻyiga 50,000 von pul berdim.

column1: I gave my friend a wedding invitation.
I got a mobile wedding invitation.
I'm going to a wedding on Saturday.
Don't wear white to a wedding.
I went to the funeral hall.
People wear black to a funeral.
I went to the funeral of our TA's father.
I was invited to my professor's baby's first birthday party.
column2: Domlamning chaqalogʻining birinchi tugʻilgan kuni bazmiga taklif qilindim.

column1: At the first birthday party, the baby picked up the money.
column2: Birinchi tugʻilgan kun bazmida chaqaloq pulni ushladi.

column1: People give a gold ring as a first birthday gift.
column2: Birinchi tugʻilgan kunga sovgʻa sifatida oltin uzuk beriladi.

column1: Our TA's wedding is next Saturday.
Can I go too? How much gift money do people give?
column2: Men ham borsam boʻladimi? Odatda qancha pul berishadi?

column1: Of course. People usually give about 50,000 won.
Manners and greetings for eating in Korea. You really need them at department dinners and MT (student retreats).
column2: Koreyada ovqatlanish odobi va salomlashuvlar. Fakultet kechki ovqatlari va MT (talabalar sayohati) da juda kerak boʻladi.

column1: Say "잘 먹겠습니다" before eating and "잘 먹었습니다" after eating.
column2: Ovqatdan oldin "잘 먹겠습니다", ovqatdan keyin "잘 먹었습니다" deng.

column1: Start eating after the oldest person picks up their spoon.
column2: Eng katta odam qoshigʻini olgandan keyin ovqatlanishni boshlang.

column1: When you pour a drink for an older person or take one from them, use both hands. When you drink, turn your head to the side.
column2: Yoshi kattaga ichimlik quyganda yoki undan olganda ikki qoʻllab oling. Ichayotganda boshingizni yon tomonga buring.

column1: If you can't drink alcohol, you can say "저는 술을 못 마십니다".
column2: Spirtli ichimlik icha olmasangiz, "저는 술을 못 마십니다" deyishingiz mumkin.

column1: Don't lift your rice bowl while eating. Don't stick your spoon upright in the rice.
column2: Ovqatlanayotganda guruch kosangizni koʻtarmang. Qoshiqni guruchga tik sanchib qoʻymang.

column1: I'll leave first. (said politely when leaving)
column2: Men oldinroq ketaman. (ketayotganda hurmat bilan aytiladi)

column1: I start eating after the professor starts eating.
column2: Domla ovqatni boshlagandan keyin men ham boshlayman.

column1: When you eat with older people, eat slowly.
to eat, to have a meal (polite)
I pour a drink for the professor.
Let me pour you a drink.
If you can't drink, you can just take the glass and put it down.
column2: Icha olmasangiz, stakanni olib, qoʻyib qoʻyishingiz mumkin.

column1: I take the glass with both hands.
Take a glass from an older person with both hands.
column2: Kattalar bergan stakanni ikki qoʻllab oling.

column1: Thank you for the food (said before eating)
Thank you for the food, professor.
Thank you for buying me this meal. (to an older student)
column2: Meni mehmon qilganingiz uchun rahmat. (katta kursdoshga)

column1: Thank you, I enjoyed the meal (said after eating)
column2: Rahmat, ovqat mazali boʻldi (ovqatdan keyin aytiladi)

column1: Thank you for the meal, Mom.
Thank you for the meal. It was delicious.
column2: Ovqat uchun rahmat. Juda mazali boʻldi.

column1: Thank you for the meal. Next time, it's my treat.
column2: Ovqat uchun rahmat. Keyingi safar men mehmon qilaman.

column1: These are manners for treating older people and people above you. Some are similar to your country and some are different.
column2: Yoshi katta va mansabi yuqori odamlarga muomala odobi. Baʼzilari sizning davlatingizga oʻxshaydi, baʼzilari farq qiladi.

column1: With senior people, bow your head to greet, give things with both hands, and use polite speech.
column2: Kattalar bilan bosh egib salomlashing, narsalarni ikki qoʻllab bering va hurmat shaklida gapiring.

column1: In Korea, instead of waving or shaking hands, people bow their head and upper body to greet. The more senior the person, the deeper you bow.
column2: Koreyada qoʻl silkitish yoki qoʻl berib koʻrishish oʻrniga bosh va gavdani egib salomlashiladi. Odam qanchalik katta boʻlsa, shunchalik chuqur egiladi.

column1: When you give or take something, use both hands, or give it with your right hand while your left hand touches your right arm.
column2: Biror narsa berganda yoki olganda ikki qoʻllab qiling yoki oʻng qoʻl bilan berib, chap qoʻlni oʻng qoʻlingizga tekkizib turing.

column1: The rule about not touching people's heads is not as strong as in Myanmar, but you don't touch an older person's body.
column2: Odamlarning boshiga tegmaslik qoidasi Myanmadagidek qatʼiy emas, lekin katta yoshli odamning tanasiga tegilmaydi.

column1: In front of senior people, "주다" becomes "드리다", "먹다" becomes "드시다", and "있다" becomes "계시다".
On New Year's Day, we bow to our elders.
At the wedding, they bow to their parents.
They bow at the 폐백 (a traditional wedding ceremony).
column2: Ular 폐백 (anʼanaviy toʻy marosimi) da taʼzim qilishadi.

column1: The senior person sits down first.
I am polite to my seniors.
When a senior person is talking, listen until the end.
I give the documents with both hands.
I give my business card with both hands.
I gave the report with both hands.
Use polite speech with older people.
Use polite speech with people you meet for the first time.
column2: Birinchi marta uchrashgan odamlar bilan hurmat shaklida gapiring.

column1: You must use polite speech with your professor.
column2: Domlangiz bilan hurmat shaklida gapirishingiz shart.

column1: I greet my professor every morning.
column2: Har kuni ertalab domlam bilan salomlashaman.

column1: When you meet an older person, greet them first.
column2: Katta odamni uchratganda birinchi boʻlib salom bering.

column1: When class is over, I say goodbye to the professor before I leave.
column2: Dars tugagach, ketishdan oldin domla bilan xayrlashaman.

column1: Good morning, professor. This is for you.
Thank you. Sam, you are very polite.
to be right, proper (예의가 바르다 = to be polite)
column2: toʻgʻri, odobli boʻlmoq (예의가 바르다 = odobli boʻlmoq)

column1: Words about Korea's big holidays, Seollal and Chuseok. Schools and shops close for a few days at these times.
column2: Koreyaning katta bayramlari — Seollal va Chuseok haqida soʻzlar. Bu paytda maktab va doʻkonlar bir necha kun yopiladi.

column1: People eat tteokguk at Seollal and songpyeon at Chuseok.
column2: Seollalda tteokguk, Chuseokda esa songpyeon yeyiladi.

column1: Seollal is the 1st day of the 1st lunar month, and Chuseok is the 15th day of the 8th lunar month. Like New Year or big holidays in many countries, the whole family gets together.
column2: Seollal oy kalendari boʻyicha 1-oyning 1-kuni, Chuseok esa 8-oyning 15-kuni. Koʻp davlatlardagi Yangi yil yoki katta bayramlar kabi butun oila yigʻiladi.

column1: The New Year greeting is "새해 복 많이 받으세요" (Happy New Year).
column2: Yangi yil tabrigi: "새해 복 많이 받으세요" (Yangi yilingiz bilan).

column1: During the holidays, there is a lot of traffic and shops close. Buy food in advance.
column2: Bayramlarda yoʻllar tirband boʻladi va doʻkonlar yopiladi. Oziq-ovqatni oldindan sotib oling.

column1: We eat tteokguk on New Year's Day.
On New Year's Day, the family gets together.
I bought a ticket home for the Lunar New Year holidays.
column2: Oy Yangi yili bayramiga uyga chipta sotib oldim.
uzoq bayram, bayram dam olish kunlari

column1: I go to my hometown for Chuseok.
At Chuseok, the department handed out songpyeon.
My neighbor shared songpyeon with me.
When I come back from my hometown, I'll bring you a gift.
column2: Yurtimdan qaytganimda sizga sovgʻa olib kelaman.

column1: We hold the memorial service in the morning.
We hold the memorial service at Chuseok too.
column2: Chuseokda ham ajdodlarni yodlash marosimini oʻtkazamiz.

column1: We made the food for the memorial service together.
I bow to my elders for the New Year.
to give a New Year's bow
When you do the New Year's bow, you get New Year's money.
column2: Yangi yil taʼzimini qilsangiz, Yangi yil pulini olasiz.

column1: I gave a New Year's bow to the professor and heard his good wishes.
column2: Domlaga Yangi yil taʼzimini qilib, uning yaxshi tilaklarini eshitdim.

column1: Please have a bowl of tteokguk.
When you eat tteokguk, you become one year older.
On New Year's morning, the dormitory cafeteria served tteokguk.
column2: Yangi yil ertalabi yotoqxona oshxonasida tteokguk berildi.

column1: to come out, to be served
What are you doing for the Chuseok holiday?
I'm resting in the dormitory. I want to go home.
column2: Yotoqxonada dam olaman. Uyga ketgim keladi.

column1: Then come to my house and eat songpyeon with us.
column2: Unda bizning uyimizga kelib, biz bilan songpyeon yeng.

column1: Rules you must follow in places that many people share. If you break them, you may have to pay a fine.
column2: Koʻp odamlar birga foydalanadigan joylarda rioya qilinishi kerak boʻlgan qoidalar. Ularni buzsangiz, jarima toʻlashingiz mumkin.

column1: No smoking, standing in line and recycling are rules everyone follows in Korea.
column2: Chekmaslik, navbatda turish va chiqindilarni saralash — Koreyada hamma rioya qiladigan qoidalar.

column1: In Korea, smoking is not allowed inside buildings, at bus stops or at subway entrances. You can smoke only in smoking areas.
column2: Koreyada binolar ichida, avtobus bekatlarida va metro kirish joylarida chekish mumkin emas. Faqat chekish joylarida chekish mumkin.

column1: Trash is sorted into paper, plastic, cans, bottles, food waste and general trash.
column2: Chiqindilar qogʻoz, plastik, banka, shisha, oziq-ovqat chiqindisi va umumiy chiqindiga saralanadi.

column1: Buses and subways have special seats for older people and pregnant women. It is better not to sit there even when they are empty.
column2: Avtobus va metroda keksalar va homilador ayollar uchun maxsus oʻrindiqlar bor. Ular boʻsh boʻlsa ham oʻtirmagan maʼqul.

column1: Please be quiet in the hospital.
Please be quiet on the subway.
In the library, talk quietly on the phone too.
Separate plastic and cans for recycling.
You have to pay a fine.
If you throw trash anywhere, you pay a fine.
column2: Chiqindini istalgan joyga tashlasangiz, jarima toʻlaysiz.

column1: Smoking is not allowed anywhere inside the school buildings.
column2: Maktab binolari ichida hech qayerda chekish mumkin emas.

column1: Bus stops are no-smoking areas too.
column2: Avtobus bekatlarida ham chekish mumkin emas.

column1: Throw your trash in the trash can.
Don't throw trash on the street.
Put your trash in a pay-as-you-throw bag.
I stand in line to get on the bus.
When you pay, line up in front of the counter.

column2: Yoʻlni notoʻgʻri joydan kesib oʻtish xavfli.

column1: If you jaywalk, you pay a fine.
column2: Yoʻlni notoʻgʻri joydan kesib oʻtsangiz, jarima toʻlaysiz.

column1: No. This is a no-smoking area. The fine is 100,000 won.
column2: Yoʻq. Bu yerda chekish mumkin emas. Jarimasi 100,000 von.

column1: Please smoke in the smoking area over there.
column2: Ana u tomondagi chekish joyida cheking.

column1: These are the six basic vowels of Hangul. When you write a vowel alone, put a silent ㅇ in front of it.
column2: Bular hangulning oltita asosiy unlisi. Unlini yolgʻiz yozganda oldiga talaffuz qilinmaydigan ㅇ qoʻying.

column1: There are six basic vowels: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ.
column2: Oltita asosiy unli bor: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ.

column1: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ are written to the right of the consonant, and ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ are written below it.
column2: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ undoshning oʻng tomoniga, ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ esa uning ostiga yoziladi.

column1: For ㅓ, open your mouth a little; for ㅗ, round your lips. English has no exact ㅓ: it is between the "o" in "hot" and the "u" in "cup". ㅗ is like the "o" in "go", but without the "w" at the end.
column2: ㅓ uchun ogʻzingizni biroz oching, ㅗ uchun lablaringizni yumaloqlang. Oʻzbek tilida ㅓ ning aniq muqobili yoʻq: u lablarni yumaloqlamasdan aytilgan "o" ga yaqin. ㅗ esa oʻzbekcha "oʻ" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: My tooth hurts. I'm going to the dentist.
It is raining. Do you have an umbrella?
These are ㅐ and ㅔ. Today, Korean people say these two sounds almost the same way.
column2: Bular ㅐ va ㅔ. Hozir koreyslar bu ikki tovushni deyarli bir xil aytishadi.

column1: ㅐ and ㅔ sound almost the same, so we tell them apart by spelling.
column2: ㅐ va ㅔ deyarli bir xil eshitiladi, shuning uchun ularni yozilishidan ajratamiz.

column1: Both sound like the "e" in "bed" (ㅐ used to be more open, like the "a" in "cat"). It is OK if you cannot hear the difference. Learn them by their spelling.
column2: Ikkalasi ham oʻzbekcha "ertaga" soʻzidagi "e" ga oʻxshaydi (ilgari ㅐ ochiqroq aytilardi). Farqni eshitmasangiz ham mayli. Ularni yozilishi bilan oʻrganing.

column1: 네 is an answer (yes), and "내" means "my".
My stomach hurts, so I take medicine.
column2: Qornim ogʻriyapti, shuning uchun dori ichaman.

column1: I learn Korean with Korean songs.
column2: Koreys tilini koreys qoʻshiqlari bilan oʻrganaman.

column1: to know (알겠어요 = I see, I understand)
I buy crabs at the market.
If you add one more stroke to a basic vowel, a [y] sound (as in "yes") comes in front.
column2: Asosiy unliga yana bitta chiziq qoʻshsangiz, oldiga [y] tovushi qoʻshiladi (oʻzbekcha "yaxshi" dagi kabi).

column1: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ are ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ with [y] in front.
column2: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ — oldiga [y] qoʻshilgan ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ.

column1: ㅏ → ㅑ, ㅓ → ㅕ, ㅗ → ㅛ, ㅜ → ㅠ: when one short stroke becomes two, a [y] sound comes in front.
column2: ㅏ → ㅑ, ㅓ → ㅕ, ㅗ → ㅛ, ㅜ → ㅠ: bitta qisqa chiziq ikkita boʻlsa, oldiga [y] tovushi qoʻshiladi.

column1: 요 at the end of a sentence makes it polite. You will hear it very often.
column2: Gap oxiridagi "요" gapni hurmatli qiladi. Uni juda koʻp eshitasiz.

column1: I saw a fox at the zoo.
The women's restroom is this way.
I am good at cooking Greek food.
The milk is in the fridge.
to know (알겠습니다 = I see, I understand)
Yes, I will come at nine o'clock tomorrow.
If you join another vowel to ㅗ or ㅜ, a [w] sound (as in "we") comes in front.
column2: ㅗ yoki ㅜ ga boshqa unli qoʻshsangiz, oldiga [w] tovushi qoʻshiladi (lablarni yumaloqlab aytiladigan qisqa "u").

column1: ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ are sounds with [w] in front.
column2: ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ — oldiga [w] qoʻshilgan tovushlar.

column1: ㅗ goes only with ㅏ ㅐ, and ㅜ goes only with ㅓ ㅔ.
column2: ㅗ faqat ㅏ ㅐ bilan, ㅜ esa faqat ㅓ ㅔ bilan birikadi.

column1: Do not read the two vowels separately. Say them together in one sound.
column2: Ikki unlini alohida oʻqimang. Ularni bitta tovush qilib birga ayting.

column1: I bought snacks at the convenience store.
A bag of apples is 5,000 won.
The bus is coming. Get on quickly.
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
What are you eating for lunch?
Thank you for showing me the way.
These are ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ. ㅚ sounds almost the same as ㅙ and ㅞ.
column2: Bular ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ. ㅚ ㅙ va ㅞ bilan deyarli bir xil eshitiladi.

column1: ㅚ sounds like [웨], ㅟ like [위], and ㅢ is [으이] said quickly.
column2: ㅚ [웨], ㅟ [위] kabi eshitiladi, ㅢ esa tez aytilgan [으이].

column1: For ㅢ, say "으" and "이" quickly together. Do not round your lips.
column2: ㅢ uchun "으" va "이" ni tez birga ayting. Lablaringizni yumaloqlamang.

column1: ㅢ changes its sound by position. At the start of a word it is [의], in other places [이], and "~의" (of, 's) is said [에].
column2: ㅢ oʻrniga qarab tovushini oʻzgartiradi. Soʻz boshida [의], boshqa joylarda [이], "~의" (-ning) esa [에] deb aytiladi.

These are the basic consonants ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ. A consonant needs a vowel to make a sound.
column2: Bular asosiy undoshlar ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ. Undosh tovush hosil qilishi uchun unli kerak.

column1: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ sound similar to English g/k, n, d/t, r/l, m.
column2: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ oʻzbekcha g/k, n, d/t, r/l, m ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: At the start of a word, ㄱ and ㄷ have a little breath, so they can sound like English "k" and "t". Between vowels they sound soft, like "g" and "d".
column2: Soʻz boshida ㄱ va ㄷ biroz nafas bilan aytiladi, shuning uchun oʻzbekcha "k" va "t" kabi eshitilishi mumkin. Unlilar orasida esa "g" va "d" kabi yumshoq eshitiladi.

column1: ㄹ is between English "r" and "l". Tap the tip of your tongue lightly once, like the "tt" in American "better".
column2: ㄹ "r" va "l" oraligʻidagi tovush. Til uchini bir marta yengil tekkizing — oʻzbekcha "r" ni titratmasdan, bir marta qisqa aytgandek.

column1: My older sister is a university student.
My older sister lives in Pakistan.
The weather in my country is hot.
I have a headache. Do you have medicine?
These are the basic consonants ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ.
column2: Bular asosiy undoshlar ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ.

column1: ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ are similar to English b/p, s, j, h, and ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable.
column2: ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ oʻzbekcha b/p, s, j, h ga oʻxshaydi, ㅇ esa boʻgʻin boshida talaffuz qilinmaydi.

column1: ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable. As a final consonant (받침), it sounds like the "ng" in "sing".
column2: ㅇ boʻgʻin boshida tovushga ega emas. Oxirgi undosh (받침) sifatida u oʻzbekcha "tong", "ming" soʻzlaridagi "ng" kabi eshitiladi.

column1: ㅅ in "시" is not [s]; it is close to the English "sh" sound.
column2: 시 dagi ㅅ [s] emas; u oʻzbekcha "sh" tovushiga yaqin.

column1: Can I try on these pants?
My younger sibling likes the lion doll.
I send money to my father.
I find the way with the map on my phone.
ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ with one more stroke. Say them with a strong puff of air.
column2: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ — bitta chiziq qoʻshilgan ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ. Ularni kuchli nafas chiqarib ayting.

column1: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are sounds with a strong puff of air.
column2: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ kuchli nafas bilan aytiladigan tovushlar.

column1: At the start of a word, ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ sound almost like English "k", "t", "p" in "kit", "top", "pin" (with a puff of air).
column2: Soʻz boshida ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ oʻzbekcha "kitob", "togʻ", "pul" soʻzlaridagi "k", "t", "p" ga yaqin (kuchli nafas bilan).

column1: ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church", with a strong puff of air. In the readings it is written "ch". Do not confuse it with ㅈ (j).
column2: ㅊ oʻzbekcha "choy" dagi "ch" ga oʻxshaydi, faqat kuchli nafas bilan aytiladi. Oʻqilishida "ch" deb yoziladi. Uni ㅈ (j) bilan adashtirmang.

column1: Hold a thin piece of paper in front of your mouth and say "카, 타, 파, 차". If the paper moves a lot, you are doing it right.
column2: Ogʻzingiz oldida yupqa qogʻozni ushlab, "카, 타, 파, 차" deng. Qogʻoz kuchli qimirlasa, toʻgʻri aytyapsiz.

How much is a box of tomatoes?
I am going to buy grapes.
Please wash the grapes before you eat them.
to eat, to drink (honorific of 먹다)
Do you have this skirt in another color?
It takes three hours to Jeonju by train.
ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are the same consonant written twice. Tighten your throat and say them with no puff of air.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ — ikki marta yozilgan bir xil undosh. Tomogʻingizni tarang qilib, nafas chiqarmasdan ayting.

column1: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are sounds made with a tight throat and no puff of air.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ tomoqni tarang qilib, nafassiz aytiladigan tovushlar.

column1: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ are close to the "k", "t", "p" after "s" in English "skin", "stop", "spin" (no puff of air), but tighter.
column2: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ oʻzbek tilida yoʻq tovushlar: ular nafassiz, tomoqni tarang qilib aytilgan "k", "t", "p" ga yaqin.

column1: English speakers should also be careful with the plain sounds ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ. Say plain sounds softly, without tension.
column2: Oddiy tovushlar ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ ga ham ehtiyot boʻling. Oddiy tovushlarni zoʻriqmasdan, yumshoq ayting.

column1: I give a carrot to the rabbit.

column2: Dada, men Koreyaga eson-omon yetib keldim.

My older brother came to meet me at the airport.
column2: Akam meni kutib olish uchun aeroportga keldi.

column1: It is a little salty. Some water, please.
Yes, they are cheap. Please come again.
A consonant written under a syllable is called 받침 (final consonant). First, ㅁ and ㅇ.
column2: Boʻgʻin ostiga yozilgan undosh 받침 (oxirgi undosh) deyiladi. Avval ㅁ va ㅇ.

column1: Final ㅁ sounds "m", and final ㅇ sounds "ng".
column2: Oxirgi ㅁ "m", oxirgi ㅇ esa "ng" deb aytiladi.

column1: Final ㅁ is like the "m" at the end of English "home", and final ㅇ is like the "ng" in "sing".
column2: Oxirgi ㅁ oʻzbekcha "olam" soʻzi oxiridagi "m" ga, oxirgi ㅇ esa "tong" dagi "ng" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: ㅇ has no sound at the front. It sounds "ng" only as a final consonant. Compare "아" and "앙".
column2: ㅇ boshida tovushga ega emas. U faqat oxirgi undosh boʻlganda "ng" deb aytiladi. "아" va "앙" ni solishtiring.

column1: I have a video call with my mom.
Do not go out alone at night.
I'm going to the library to study.
These are the final consonants ㄴ and ㄹ. Final ㄹ is similar to English "l". Practice so that it does not sound like "r".
column2: Bular oxirgi undoshlar ㄴ va ㄹ. Oxirgi ㄹ oʻzbekcha "l" ga oʻxshaydi. U "r" kabi eshitilmasligi uchun mashq qiling.

column1: Final ㄹ is not "n". It is an [l] sound with the tip of the tongue held on the gum.
column2: Oxirgi ㄹ "n" emas. Bu til uchini milkka tekkizib turib aytiladigan [l] tovushi.

column1: For final ㄹ, keep the tip of your tongue on the gum behind your upper teeth. If you say it as "n", "물" sounds like "문", which is a different word.
column2: Oxirgi ㄹ uchun til uchini ustki tishlar orqasidagi milkka tekkizib turing. Uni "n" deb aytsangiz, "물" "문" kabi eshitiladi — bu boshqa soʻz.

column1: Final ㄴ is the same as the "n" at the end of English words.
column2: Oxirgi ㄴ oʻzbekcha soʻzlar oxiridagi "n" bilan bir xil.

column1: It snowed a lot, so the road is slippery.
column2: Qor koʻp yogʻgani uchun yoʻl sirpanchiq.

column1: On the weekend, I go to the mountains with my friends.
column2: Dam olish kunlari doʻstlarim bilan togʻga boraman.

column1: I have a lot of work.
Today's work ends at five o'clock.
I write my name in Hangul.
Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ are not released: stop the sound and hold it. It is like "k", "p", "t" at the end of "book", "cup", "cat" when you do not let the air out.
column2: Oxirgi ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ ochilmaydi: tovushni toʻxtatib, ushlab turing. Bu "yoʻq", "kap", "ot" soʻzlari oxiridagi "k", "p", "t" ni havo chiqarmasdan aytganga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ end with the sound held, like an unreleased "k", "p", "t".
column2: Oxirgi ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ havo chiqarilmagan "k", "p", "t" kabi ushlab qolingan tovush bilan tugaydi.

column1: Final ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ all end with a ㄷ (t) sound: 옷[옫], 낮[낟], 꽃[꼳].
column2: Oxirgi ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ hammasi ㄷ (t) tovushi bilan tugaydi: 옷[옫], 낮[낟], 꽃[꼳].

column1: Be careful not to add "으" after a final consonant, like "채그" or "바브".
column2: Oxirgi undoshdan keyin "채그" yoki "바브" kabi "으" qoʻshib yubormaslikka ehtiyot boʻling.

column1: I take my younger sibling to school.
My house is close to the school.
I change into my gym clothes.
I give flowers to my mother.

column2: Kunduzi issiq, shuning uchun koʻp suv iching.

column1: These syllables have two consonants in the 받침. When you say the word alone, you pronounce only one of them.
column2: Bu boʻgʻinlarning 받침 ida ikkita undosh bor. Soʻzni yolgʻiz aytganda ulardan faqat bittasi talaffuz qilinadi.

column1: A double final consonant: alone, only one sounds; before a vowel, both sound.
column2: Qoʻsh oxirgi undosh: yolgʻiz kelganda faqat bittasi, unlidan oldin esa ikkalasi ham eshitiladi.

column1: Only one is pronounced, as in 닭[닥], 여덟[여덜], 값[갑]. Learn which one for each word.
column2: 닭[닥], 여덟[여덜], 값[갑] dagi kabi faqat bittasi aytiladi. Har bir soʻz uchun qaysi biri ekanini oʻrganing.

column1: If a vowel comes after, the second consonant moves to the next syllable and both are pronounced: 읽어요[일거요], 앉아요[안자요].
column2: Keyin unli kelsa, ikkinchi undosh keyingi boʻgʻinga oʻtadi va ikkalasi ham aytiladi: 읽어요[일거요], 앉아요[안자요].

geun (unit of weight, 600 g for meat)
Please be sure to read the notice.
I get up at eight in the morning.
There are many customers on weekends.

In Hangul, consonants and vowels are written together in one square block. One block is one syllable.
column2: Hangulda undosh va unlilar bitta kvadrat blokda birga yoziladi. Bitta blok — bitta boʻgʻin.

column1: One syllable is consonant + vowel, or consonant + vowel + 받침.
column2: Bitta boʻgʻin — undosh + unli yoki undosh + unli + 받침.

column1: Write from left to right and from top to bottom. The 받침 goes at the very bottom.
column2: Chapdan oʻngga va yuqoridan pastga yozing. 받침 eng pastga yoziladi.

column1: English writes letters in one line, but in Hangul the vowel goes only to the right of the consonant or below it.
column2: Oʻzbek lotin yozuvida harflar bir qatorda yoziladi, hangulda esa unli faqat undoshning oʻng tomoniga yoki ostiga yoziladi.

column1: My younger sibling sleeps holding a teddy bear.
to hug, to hold in one's arms

column2: Men ham siz bilan borsam boʻladimi?

I am going to the hospital tomorrow.
When a syllable starting with ㅇ comes after a 받침, the 받침 moves over and becomes the first sound of the next syllable.
column2: 받침 dan keyin ㅇ bilan boshlanadigan boʻgʻin kelsa, 받침 oʻtib, keyingi boʻgʻinning birinchi tovushiga aylanadi.

column1: When a vowel comes after it, the 받침 moves to the next syllable.
column2: Keyin unli kelsa, 받침 keyingi boʻgʻinga oʻtadi.

column1: The spelling stays the same; only the sound changes: 한국어[한구거], 먹어요[머거요], 있어요[이써요].
column2: Yozilishi oʻzgarmaydi, faqat talaffuz oʻzgaradi: 한국어[한구거], 먹어요[머거요], 있어요[이써요].

column1: Final ㅇ does not move: 가방에[가방에].

column1: You have learned all of Hangul. Now you can read words.
column2: Siz hangulni toʻliq oʻrgandingiz. Endi soʻzlarni oʻqiy olasiz.

column1: At first, read slowly one syllable at a time. Then read them together.
column2: Avvaliga har bir boʻgʻinni sekin oʻqing. Keyin ularni qoʻshib oʻqing.

column1: 감사합니다 is pronounced [감사함니다]. You will learn why in the pronunciation rules unit later.
column2: 감사합니다 [감사함니다] deb talaffuz qilinadi. Sababini keyinroq talaffuz qoidalari boʻlimida oʻrganasiz.

column1: I want to work in Korea.
I am Sam. I am American.
ㄱ, ㅋ, ㄲ differ in the strength of the breath and the tension in the throat. English has only one "k" sound, so it is hard to hear ㄱ and ㄲ.
column2: ㄱ, ㅋ, ㄲ nafas kuchi va tomoq tarangligi bilan farqlanadi. Oʻzbek tilida "k" tovushi bitta, shuning uchun ㄱ va ㄲ ni farqlab eshitish qiyin.

column1: ㄲ is a tight "k" (as in "skin"), ㅋ is a strong "k" (as in "kit"), and ㄱ is soft and low.
column2: ㄲ — tarang "k", ㅋ — kuchli nafasli "k" (oʻzbekcha "kitob" dagi kabi), ㄱ esa yumshoq va past ohangli.

column1: ㄲ is like the "k" in "skin" but tighter, and ㅋ is like the "k" in "kit" with a puff of air. ㄱ is in between: say it relaxed and soft, with a low pitch.
column2: ㄲ nafassiz va tarang aytiladigan "k", ㅋ esa "kitob" dagi kabi nafas bilan aytiladigan "k". ㄱ ularning oʻrtasida: uni boʻsh, yumshoq va past ohangda ayting.

column1: At the start of a word, the vowel after ㄱ starts low, and the vowel after ㅋ and ㄲ starts high. Listening for high and low pitch is the easiest way.
column2: Soʻz boshida ㄱ dan keyingi unli past, ㅋ va ㄲ dan keyingisi esa baland ohangda boshlanadi. Baland va past ohangni eshitish eng oson yoʻl.

column1: Honey water is good for a cold.
I fold the laundry and put it away.

column2: Dam olish kunlari doʻstlarim bilan shirin kartoshka qazib olaman.

These are ㄷ, ㅌ, ㄸ. ㅌ is like the "t" in "top", ㄸ is like the "t" in "stop" but tighter, and ㄷ at the start of a word has a little breath.
column2: Bular ㄷ, ㅌ, ㄸ. ㅌ oʻzbekcha "tosh" dagi kabi nafas bilan aytiladigan "t", ㄸ nafassiz va tarang aytiladigan "t", soʻz boshidagi ㄷ esa biroz nafas bilan aytiladi.

column1: ㅌ is the "t" in "top", ㄸ is the "t" in "stop", and ㄷ between vowels is "d".
column2: ㅌ — nafasli "t", ㄸ — nafassiz tarang "t", unlilar orasidagi ㄷ esa "d".

column1: ㄷ between vowels sounds like English "d": 바다, 어디.
column2: Unlilar orasidagi ㄷ oʻzbekcha "d" kabi eshitiladi: 바다, 어디.

column1: If you say "딸" as "달", the meaning changes. Say ㄸ tight and strong, like the "t" in "stop".
column2: 딸 ni "달" deb aytsangiz, maʼno oʻzgaradi. ㄸ ni tarang va kuchli, nafassiz ayting.

column1: I get my allowance once a month.
column2: Choʻntak pulimni oyiga bir marta olaman.

These are ㅂ, ㅍ, ㅃ. ㅍ is like the "p" in "pin", and ㅃ is like the "p" in "spin" but tighter.
column2: Bular ㅂ, ㅍ, ㅃ. ㅍ oʻzbekcha "pul" dagi kabi nafas bilan aytiladigan "p", ㅃ esa nafassiz va tarangroq "p".

column1: ㅍ is the "p" in "pin", ㅃ is the "p" in "spin", and ㅂ between vowels is "b".
column2: ㅍ — nafasli "p", ㅃ — nafassiz tarang "p", unlilar orasidagi ㅂ esa "b".

column1: 불 (fire) and "풀" (grass) mean very different things, and mishearing them can be dangerous. ㅍ has a strong puff of air.
column2: 불 (olov) va "풀" (oʻt) juda boshqa maʼnoga ega, ularni notoʻgʻri eshitish xavfli boʻlishi mumkin. ㅍ kuchli nafas bilan aytiladi.

column1: ㅂ between vowels sounds like English "b": 아버지, 가방.
column2: Unlilar orasidagi ㅂ oʻzbekcha "b" kabi eshitiladi: 아버지, 가방.

These are ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅉ. English has only "j" and "ch", so you need to practice all three.
column2: Bular ㅈ, ㅊ, ㅉ. Oʻzbek tilida faqat "j" va "ch" bor, shuning uchun uchalasini ham mashq qilishingiz kerak.

column1: ㅉ is a tight "j", ㅊ is "ch" with a strong breath, and ㅈ is a soft "j".
column2: ㅉ — tarang "j", ㅊ — kuchli nafasli "ch", ㅈ esa yumshoq "j".

column1: ㅉ is a tight "j" with no breath. ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church" with a strong puff of air. ㅈ is a soft, low sound between "j" and "ch".
column2: ㅉ nafassiz tarang "j". ㅊ oʻzbekcha "choy" dagi "ch" ga oʻxshaydi, kuchli nafas bilan. ㅈ esa "j" va "ch" oraligʻidagi yumshoq, past tovush.

column1: Be careful not to say ㅊ as "s" or "sh". "차" is not "사".
column2: ㅊ ni "s" yoki "sh" deb aytmaslikka ehtiyot boʻling. "차" — "사" emas.
