column1: Notices at school and in the dorm, and subway announcements, almost always use this style. It is important to read and understand them.
column2: Universitet va yotoqxonadagi eʼlonlar, metrodagi xabarnomalar deyarli har doim shu uslubda boʻladi. Ularni oʻqib tushunish muhim.

column1: Please exit through the emergency exit.
Please be quiet inside the library.
Do not bring food into the reading room.
to have, to hold (가지고 = with, carrying)
Aisha, did you turn off your phone?
Used to tell someone politely not to do something. It is like "Please don't …" in English.
column2: Kimgadir biror narsani qilmaslikni muloyimlik bilan aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "Iltimos, …mang" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: If you add "-지 마세요" after a verb, it means the same as "Don't + verb" in English.
column2: Feʼldan keyin "-지 마세요" qoʻshilsa, oʻzbekchadagi "…mang" bilan bir xil maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-지 마세요". It is the same with or without a final consonant.
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-지 마세요" qoʻshing. Oxirgi undosh boʻlsa ham, boʻlmasa ham bir xil.

column1: In English, "don't" comes before the verb, but in Korean "-지 마세요" comes after the verb.
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "-ma" kabi, koreyschada ham "-지 마세요" feʼldan keyin keladi.

column1: 안 가세요? is not a command but a question (Aren't you going?). Don't use "안" to tell someone not to do something.
column2: 안 가세요? buyruq emas, balki savol (Bormaysizmi?). Kimgadir biror narsani qilmaslikni aytish uchun "안" ishlatmang.

column1: The form changes with the level of politeness. With friends or younger people, or in an emergency, use "-지 마" (만지지 마!); usually use "-지 마세요"; on signs and in announcements use "-지 마십시오".
column2: Shakl hurmat darajasiga qarab oʻzgaradi. Doʻstlar yoki yoshi kichiklar bilan yoki favqulodda vaziyatda "-지 마" (만지지 마!), odatda "-지 마세요", belgilar va eʼlonlarda "-지 마십시오" ishlatiladi.

column1: Don't run. The floor is slippery.
Can I turn on this coffee machine now?
column2: Bu kofe mashinasini hozir yoqsam boʻladimi?

column1: No, don't turn it on yet. It's being repaired.
OK, I understand. Then what shall I do?
Move that box. It's heavy, so don't lift it alone.
column2: Anavi qutini koʻchiring. Ogʻir, shuning uchun yolgʻiz koʻtarmang.

column1: Says what you must not do or what is not allowed. It is like "must not…, can't…" in English.
column2: Nima qilish mumkin emasligini yoki nimaga ruxsat berilmaganini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ish mumkin emas, …masligingiz kerak" ga oʻxshaydi.
-(으)면 안 돼요 "…ish mumkin emas" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: After a final consonant (받침) add "-으면 안 돼요"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면 안 돼요".
column2: Oxirgi undosh (받침) boʻlsa "-으면 안 돼요", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-면 안 돼요" qoʻshiladi.

column1: -지 마세요 is said directly to the listener; "-(으)면 안 돼요" explains a rule.
column2: -지 마세요 tinglovchiga toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri aytiladi; "-(으)면 안 돼요" esa qoidani tushuntiradi.

column1: As a question, "-(으)면 안 돼요?" asks for permission, like "Can't I…?": "조금 쉬면 안 돼요?" (Can't I rest a little?)
column2: Savol shaklida "-(으)면 안 돼요?" "…sam boʻlmaydimi?" kabi ruxsat soʻraydi: "조금 쉬면 안 돼요?" (Biroz dam olsam boʻlmaydimi?)

column1: You must not look at your phone during class.
column2: Dars paytida telefonga qarash mumkin emas.

column1: You must not go in without permission.
Boss, can I listen to music while I work?
No, you must not wear earphones. You can't hear the customers.
column2: Yoʻq, quloqchin taqish mumkin emas. Mijozlarni eshitmay qolasiz.

column1: to put on, wear (gloves, a ring)
Then what about during break time?
Shows permission: you may do it. As a question, it asks for permission. It is like "may…, can…, Can I…?" in English.
column2: Ruxsatni bildiradi: qilsangiz boʻladi. Savol shaklida ruxsat soʻraydi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…sa boʻladi, …sam boʻladimi?" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -아/어도 돼요 means "may…", and "-아/어도 돼요?" means "May I…?".
column2: -아/어도 돼요 "…sa boʻladi", "-아/어도 돼요?" esa "…sam boʻladimi?" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "-도 돼요".
In English "Can I…?" comes at the start, but Korean "-아/어도 돼요?" comes at the end: "Can I go first?" = "먼저 가도 돼요?"
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, koreyschada ham ruxsat soʻrash feʼl oxirida keladi: "Oldinroq ketsam boʻladimi?" = "먼저 가도 돼요?"

column1: The answer is "네, 돼요" or "네, 그러세요"; if not allowed, "아니요, 안 돼요" or "-(으)면 안 돼요".
column2: Javob "네, 돼요" yoki "네, 그러세요"; ruxsat berilmasa, "아니요, 안 돼요" yoki "-(으)면 안 돼요".

column1: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요? asks if you are able to; "-아/어도 돼요?" asks for permission.
column2: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요? qila olasizmi deb soʻraydi; "-아/어도 돼요?" esa ruxsat soʻraydi.

column1: May I go to the restroom?
Boss, may I go home a little early today?
column2: Xoʻjayin, bugun biroz erta uyga ketsam boʻladimi?

column1: Because I have to go to the bank.
Yes, you may go at five o'clock.
Says what you must do. It is like "must, have to" in English.
column2: Nima qilish kerakligini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ishim kerak, …shim shart" ga oʻxshaydi.
-아/어야 해요/돼요 "…ish kerak, …ish shart" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "-야 해요" or "-야 돼요". Both mean the same.
column2: -아요/어요 shaklidan "요" ni olib, "-야 해요" yoki "-야 돼요" qoʻshing. Ikkalasi bir xil maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: English "have to" comes before the verb, but in Korean it is added after the verb: "have to go" = "가야 해요".
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "kerak" kabi, koreyschada ham u feʼldan keyin qoʻshiladi: "borish kerak" = "가야 해요".

column1: In speaking, "-야 돼요" is used a lot; in writing and formal speech, "-야 합니다" is common.
column2: Ogʻzaki nutqda "-야 돼요" koʻp ishlatiladi; yozuvda va rasmiy nutqda "-야 합니다" keng tarqalgan.

column1: Don't have to is "안 -아/어도 돼요", not "-지 않아야 해요".
column2: …ish shart emas — "-지 않아야 해요" emas, balki "안 -아/어도 돼요".

column1: I have to hand in the assignment by tomorrow.
I have to get up early tomorrow.
You have to take the medicine three times a day.
column2: Dorini kuniga uch marta ichishingiz kerak.

column1: You must carry your residence card with you.
column2: Chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangiz (ID karta) doim yoningizda boʻlishi kerak.
chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartasi (ID karta)

column1: I have to put them on
Sam, when you do the practice class, you must wear an apron.
column2: Sam, amaliy mashgʻulot qilganingizda albatta fartuk taqishingiz kerak.

column1: Do I have to wear a hat too?
Yes, we are making food, so you have to wear a hat too.
column2: Ha, ovqat tayyorlayapmiz, shuning uchun bosh kiyim ham kiyishingiz kerak.

column1: Means doing just that is enough. Used when explaining how to do something. It is like "you just need to…, all you have to do is…" in English.
column2: Faqat shuni qilish yetarli ekanini bildiradi. Biror narsani qanday qilishni tushuntirganda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "faqat …sangiz boʻldi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으면 돼요"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면 돼요".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으면 돼요", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-면 돼요" qoʻshiladi.

column1: To ask how to do something, say "어떻게 하면 돼요?" (What should I do? / How do I do it?). It is the most useful question when learning a job.
column2: Biror narsani qanday qilishni soʻrash uchun "어떻게 하면 돼요?" (Nima qilishim kerak? / Qanday qilaman?) deng. Bu ishni oʻrganayotganda eng foydali savol.

column1: -아/어야 돼요 is something you must do; "-(으)면 돼요" means doing only that is enough.
column2: -아/어야 돼요 — qilishingiz shart boʻlgan narsa; "-(으)면 돼요" esa faqat shuni qilish yetarli degani.

column1: You just need to press this button.
You only need to write your name here.
column2: Faqat shu yerga ismingizni yozsangiz boʻldi.

column1: By what time should I come?
You just need to press it
You just need to put it in
You just need to do it
How do I use this washing machine?
column2: Bu kir yuvish mashinasidan qanday foydalaniladi?

column1: First tap your student ID card, then just press the start button.
column2: Avval talaba ID kartangizni tekkizing, keyin start tugmasini bossangiz boʻldi.

column1: And when I want to stop it?
It is used in two ways: ① "-도록 하세요" is a polite instruction. ② "-도록" means "so that…, so as not to…".
column2: U ikki xil ishlatiladi: ① "-도록 하세요" — muloyim koʻrsatma. ② "-도록" — "…sin deb, …masin deb".

column1: -도록 하세요 is a polite instruction, and "-지 않도록" means "so as not to…".
column2: -도록 하세요 — muloyim koʻrsatma, "-지 않도록" esa "…masin deb" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-도록". It does not depend on 받침. For "so as not to", use "-지 않도록".
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-도록" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas. "…masin deb" uchun "-지 않도록" ishlating.

column1: Seniors often use it when telling juniors what to do. The answer is "네, 그렇게 하겠습니다" or "-도록 하겠습니다".
column2: Katta kursdoshlar kichiklarga nima qilishni aytganda koʻp ishlatadi. Javob "네, 그렇게 하겠습니다" yoki "-도록 하겠습니다".

column1: In school notices and dorm rules you often see "-지 않도록 주의하십시오": "물건을 잃어버리지 않도록 주의하십시오." (Be careful not to lose your things.)
column2: Universitet eʼlonlari va yotoqxona qoidalarida "-지 않도록 주의하십시오" ni tez-tez uchratasiz: "물건을 잃어버리지 않도록 주의하십시오." (Narsalaringizni yoʻqotib qoʻymaslikka ehtiyot boʻling.)

column1: Be careful not to get hurt.
Tomorrow, please come by eight o'clock.
I left early so as not to be late.
I will be careful from now on.
Please make sure to do it
so as not to get hurt
so as not to be late
I will make sure to do it
Sam, you were late again today.
I'm sorry. I will make sure not to be late again.
From the next class, please come ten minutes early.
column2: Keyingi darsdan boshlab oʻn daqiqa erta keling.

column1: Joins two sentences with "and". Used to list two similar actions or qualities side by side.
column2: Ikki gapni "va" bilan bogʻlaydi. Ikkita oʻxshash harakat yoki xususiyatni yonma-yon sanash uchun ishlatiladi.

column1: Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-고". It does not depend on 받침. For nouns, use "(이)고".
column2: Feʼl yoki sifatdan "-다" ni olib, "-고" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas. Otlar uchun "(이)고" ishlating.

column1: Join a noun and a noun with "하고", and a sentence and a sentence with "-고": "밥하고 김치", "싸고 맛있어요".
column2: Ot bilan otni "하고" bilan, gap bilan gapni "-고" bilan bogʻlang: "밥하고 김치", "싸고 맛있어요".

column1: For the past, keep the first part as it is and change only the end: "싸고 맛있었어요."
column2: Oʻtgan zamon uchun birinchi qismni oʻzgartirmay, faqat oxirini oʻzgartiring: "싸고 맛있었어요."

column1: To split it into two sentences, use "그리고": "싸요. 그리고 맛있어요."
column2: Ikki gapga ajratish uchun "그리고" ishlating: "싸요. 그리고 맛있어요."

column1: This restaurant is cheap and tasty.
The room is big and clean.
I study business administration, and my younger sibling works.
column2: Men biznes boshqaruvini oʻqiyman, ukam esa ishlaydi.

column1: Sam is American, and Minha is Korean.
The room is spacious and clean.
Is it close to the school?
Means you finish the first action and then do the next one. It is like "…and then…, after…ing" in English.
column2: Birinchi harakatni tugatib, keyin keyingisini qilishni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "-ib, …gandan keyin" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -고 and "-고 나서" show the order of actions.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-고" or "-고 나서". "-고 나서" makes it clearer that the first action is fully finished.
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-고" yoki "-고 나서" qoʻshing. "-고 나서" birinchi harakat toʻliq tugaganini aniqroq koʻrsatadi.

column1: It is used very often when explaining steps: "신청서를 쓰고, 사진을 붙이고, 학과 사무실에 냅니다." (Write the application, attach a photo, and hand it in at the department office.)
column2: Bosqichlarni tushuntirganda juda koʻp ishlatiladi: "신청서를 쓰고, 사진을 붙이고, 학과 사무실에 냅니다." (Arizani yozib, rasm yopishtirib, kafedra idorasiga topshirasiz.)

column1: Verbs of wearing and riding use "-고": "모자를 쓰고 나가요" (put on a hat and go out), "버스를 타고 가요" (go by bus).
column2: Kiyish va minish feʼllarida "-고" ishlatiladi: "모자를 쓰고 나가요" (shapka kiyib chiqaman), "버스를 타고 가요" (avtobusda boraman).

column1: After "가다, 오다, 일어나다, 앉다, 만나다", use "-아서/어서", not "-고". You will learn this in the next set.
column2: 가다, 오다, 일어나다, 앉다, 만나다 dan keyin "-고" emas, "-아서/어서" ishlatiladi. Buni keyingi toʻplamda oʻrganasiz.

column1: I finish my assignment and then rest.
Turn off the computer and then go out.
What did you do after dinner?
What do you do when work is finished?
I turn off the coffee machine and then wipe the tables.
column2: Kofe mashinasini oʻchirib, keyin stollarni artaman.

column1: I put away the cups and then go to the dorm.
to tidy up, to put away
Used when the first action and the next action are linked. You do the next action in the place of the first action, or in that state.
column2: Birinchi harakat bilan keyingi harakat bogʻliq boʻlganda ishlatiladi. Keyingi harakat birinchi harakat joyida yoki oʻsha holatda bajariladi.

column1: -아서/어서 tells two linked actions in order.
column2: -아서/어서 bir-biriga bogʻliq ikki harakatni ketma-ket aytadi.

column1: Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "서": 가다 → 가서, 만나다 → 만나서, 만들다 → 만들어서.
column2: -아요/어요 shaklidan "요" ni olib, "서" qoʻshing: 가다 → 가서, 만나다 → 만나서, 만들다 → 만들어서.

column1: 시장에 가서 샀어요 means you bought it at the market. If you say "시장에 가고 샀어요", it sounds like two separate actions.
column2: 시장에 가서 샀어요 uni bozorda sotib olganingizni bildiradi. "시장에 가고 샀어요" desangiz, ikkita alohida harakatdek eshitiladi.

column1: Even for the past, do not add "-았/었-". "갔어서" is wrong; "가서" is right.
column2: Oʻtgan zamonda ham "-았/었-" qoʻshmang. "갔어서" xato; "가서" toʻgʻri.

column1: I went to the market and bought apples.
I bought gimbap and ate it in the park.
column2: Gimbap sotib olib, uni bogʻda yedim.

column1: I went to Seoul and met a friend.
What did you do after you met?
We went to a Nepali restaurant and ate.
Means "before doing…". It is like "before" in English.
column2: …ishdan oldin degan maʼnoni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ishdan oldin" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-기 전에". For nouns, use "noun + 전에".
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-기 전에" qoʻshing. Otlar uchun "ot + 전에" ishlating.

column1: The order is the opposite of English "before + verb": "before eating" = "먹기 전에".
Even for the past, do not change the part before "-기 전에". "왔기 전에" is wrong.
column2: Oʻtgan zamonda ham "-기 전에" dan oldingi qismni oʻzgartirmang. "왔기 전에" xato.

column1: With time, use "time + 전에": "한 시간 전에" (an hour ago), "이 년 전에" (two years ago).
column2: Vaqt bilan "vaqt + 전에" ishlating: "한 시간 전에" (bir soat oldin), "이 년 전에" (ikki yil oldin).

column1: I wash my hands before eating.
Turn off your phone before class starts.
I learned Korean before I came to Korea.
column2: Koreyaga kelishdan oldin koreys tilini oʻrgandim.

column1: What do you have to do before the exam starts?
column2: Imtihon boshlanishidan oldin nima qilishimiz kerak?

column1: We have to put our student ID card on the desk.
column2: Talaba ID kartamizni stol ustiga qoʻyishimiz kerak.

column1: Right. And before the exam ends?
We have to check our names again.
column2: Ismlarimizni yana bir bor tekshirishimiz kerak.

column1: Means "after doing…". It is like "after" in English.
column2: …gandan keyin degan maʼnoni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…gandan keyin" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-은 후에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 후에". "-(으)ㄴ 다음에" and "-(으)ㄴ 뒤에" mean the same. For nouns, use "noun + 후에".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-은 후에", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄴ 후에" qoʻshiladi. "-(으)ㄴ 다음에" va "-(으)ㄴ 뒤에" ham shu maʼnoni bildiradi. Otlar uchun "ot + 후에" ishlating.

column1: The order is the opposite of English "after + verb": "after eating" = "먹은 후에".
With time, use "time + 후에": "삼십 분 후에 오세요." (Please come in 30 minutes.)
column2: Vaqt bilan "vaqt + 후에" ishlating: "삼십 분 후에 오세요." (30 daqiqadan keyin keling.)

column1: On a medicine bag, "식후 30분" means "30 minutes after eating".
Let's meet after class is over.
Take the medicine after you eat.
After I came to Korea, I made many Korean friends.
column2: Koreyaga kelganimdan keyin koʻplab koreys doʻstlar orttirdim.

column1: What do you do after class?
When do I take this medicine?
Take it after meals. It's three times a day.
column2: Ovqatdan keyin iching. Kuniga uch marta.

column1: Do I take it right after eating?
Means doing two things at the same time. It is like "while …ing" in English.
column2: Ikki ishni bir vaqtda qilishni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ib turib, …ar ekan" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -(으)면서 means one person does two things at the same time.
column2: -(으)면서 bir kishi ikki ishni bir vaqtda qilishini bildiradi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으면서"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면서".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으면서", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-면서" qoʻshiladi.

column1: The same person must do both actions. If the people are different, use "-는 동안".
column2: Ikkala harakatni bir kishi bajarishi kerak. Agar odamlar har xil boʻlsa, "-는 동안" ishlating.

column1: Say the more important action last: "운전하면서 전화하지 마세요." (Don't talk on the phone while driving.)
column2: Muhimroq harakatni oxirida ayting: "운전하면서 전화하지 마세요." (Mashina haydab turib telefonda gaplashmang.)

column1: 듣다 becomes "들으면서" and 걷다 becomes "걸으면서" (ㄷ irregular).
column2: 듣다 "들으면서" ga, 걷다 esa "걸으면서" ga aylanadi (ㄷ notoʻgʻri feʼli).

column1: I study while listening to music.
I learned Korean while working part-time.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ishda ishlab turib koreys tilini oʻrgandim.

column1: Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.
Isn't it hard to study while working?
Means during the time something is going on. It is like "while, during" in English.
column2: Biror narsa davom etayotgan vaqtni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ayotganda, davomida" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -는 동안 means "while…", and "time + 동안" means "for (a time)".
column2: -는 동안 "…ayotgan paytda" degani, "vaqt + 동안" esa "(vaqt) davomida" degani.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 동안". A ㄹ 받침 drops (돌다 → 도는 동안). For nouns, use "noun + 동안".
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-는 동안" qoʻshing. ㄹ 받침 tushib qoladi (돌다 → 도는 동안). Otlar uchun "ot + 동안" ishlating.

column1: The subjects of the two parts can be different: "제가 청소하는 동안 아이샤 씨가 요리했어요." (While I cleaned, Aisha cooked.)
column2: Ikki qismning egasi har xil boʻlishi mumkin: "제가 청소하는 동안 아이샤 씨가 요리했어요." (Men tozalayotganimda Aisha ovqat pishirdi.)

column1: To say how long something took, use "time + 동안": "얼마 동안 한국에 있었어요?" (How long were you in Korea?)
column2: Biror narsa qancha davom etganini aytish uchun "vaqt + 동안" ishlating: "얼마 동안 한국에 있었어요?" (Koreyada qancha vaqt boʻldingiz?)

column1: It often appears in exam rules: "시험을 보는 동안 휴대폰을 끄십시오." (Turn off your phone while taking the exam.)
column2: Bu imtihon qoidalarida tez-tez uchraydi: "시험을 보는 동안 휴대폰을 끄십시오." (Imtihon topshirayotganda telefoningizni oʻchiring.)

column1: Please be quiet while my roommate is sleeping.
I drank coffee while I waited.
I lived in Jeonju for three years.
Did anything happen while I was away?
Please wait here while the professor is in a meeting.
column2: Professor yigʻilishda boʻlgan paytda shu yerda kutib turing.

column1: Yes. How long is the meeting?
Used when the first and second parts contrast. It is like "but" in English.
column2: Birinchi va ikkinchi qismlar bir-biriga zid boʻlganda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "lekin, ammo" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -지만 means "but" and is added to the end of the first part.
column2: -지만 "lekin" degan maʼnoni bildiradi va birinchi qismning oxiriga qoʻshiladi.

column1: Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-지만". It does not depend on 받침. For the past, use "-았/었지만".
column2: Feʼl yoki sifatdan "-다" ni olib, "-지만" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었지만" ishlating.

column1: In English "but" comes at the start of the second part, but "-지만" is added to the end of the first part.
column2: Oʻzbekchada "lekin" ikkinchi qismning boshida keladi, "-지만" esa birinchi qismning oxiriga qoʻshiladi (oʻzbekchadagi "…sa-da" kabi).

column1: To split it into two sentences, use "하지만" or "그렇지만": "힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요."
column2: Ikki gapga ajratish uchun "하지만" yoki "그렇지만" ishlating: "힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요."

column1: Starting with "죄송하지만" or "실례지만" (Excuse me, but…) sounds polite.
column2: 죄송하지만 yoki "실례지만" (Kechirasiz, lekin…) bilan boshlash muloyim eshitiladi.

column1: Studying is hard, but it's fun.
Kimchi is spicy, but it's tasty.
I took medicine, but it still hurts.
column2: Dori ichdim, lekin hali ham ogʻriyapti.

column1: I miss my family, but I'm okay.
It was hard at first, but now I'm used to it.
column2: Avvaliga qiyin edi, lekin hozir oʻrganib qoldim.

column1: Used to give the background situation first, before what you say next. It is also used for contrast (but). There is no exact match in English.
column2: Keyin aytadigan gapingizdan oldin vaziyatni tushuntirish uchun ishlatiladi. Zidlik (lekin) uchun ham ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilida aniq muqobili yoʻq.

column1: -는데/(으)ㄴ데 first gives the background situation for what comes next.
column2: -는데/(으)ㄴ데 avval keyingi gap uchun vaziyatni tushuntiradi.

column1: Add "-는데" to verbs and "있다/없다"; to adjectives add "-은데" after a 받침 and "-ㄴ데" with no 받침; to nouns add "인데"; for the past add "-았/었는데".
column2: Feʼllarga va "있다/없다" ga "-는데" qoʻshiladi; sifatlarga 받침 boʻlsa "-은데", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄴ데"; otlarga "인데"; oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었는데".

column1: It is used most when you explain the situation before asking for help or asking a question: "길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요." (I don't know the way well. Could you tell me?)
column2: Ayniqsa yordam soʻrash yoki savol berishdan oldin vaziyatni tushuntirganda koʻp ishlatiladi: "길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요." (Yoʻlni yaxshi bilmayman. Koʻrsatib yubora olasizmi?)

column1: Ending a sentence with "-는데요" makes a soft answer that leaves the rest unsaid: "지금 없는데요." (He's not here right now…)
column2: Gapni "-는데요" bilan tugatish qolgan gapni aytmay qoldiradigan yumshoq javob boʻladi: "지금 없는데요." (U hozir yoʻq-da…)

column1: I'm busy now, so let's talk later.
It's raining. Do you have an umbrella?
I worked hard, but it didn't go well.
This is Sam. Is the professor there?
Professor, I have something to tell you. Do you have time?
column2: Professor, sizga aytadigan gapim bor. Vaqtingiz bormi?

column1: I have to go to the hospital next week. Could I miss class for one day?
column2: Kelasi hafta kasalxonaga borishim kerak. Bir kun darsga kelmasam boʻladimi?

column1: Used when choosing one of two actions. It is like "or" in English.
column2: Ikki harakatdan birini tanlaganda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "yoki" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-거나". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: Feʼl yoki sifatdan "-다" ni olib, "-거나" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas.

column1: Nouns use "(이)나", and verbs and adjectives use "-거나": "커피나 차" (coffee or tea), "마시거나 먹거나" (drink or eat).
column2: Otlarda "(이)나", feʼl va sifatlarda "-거나" ishlatiladi: "커피나 차" (kofe yoki choy), "마시거나 먹거나" (ichish yoki yeyish).

column1: English "or" stands alone in the middle, but "-거나" is attached to the first verb.
column2: Oʻzbekchada "yoki" oʻrtada alohida soʻz boʻlib turadi, "-거나" esa birinchi feʼlga qoʻshiladi.

column1: To split it into two sentences, use "아니면" or "또는".
column2: Ikki gapga ajratish uchun "아니면" yoki "또는" ishlating.

column1: On weekends I rest or meet friends.
column2: Dam olish kunlari dam olaman yoki doʻstlarim bilan uchrashaman.

column1: In the evening I watch TV or listen to music.
column2: Kechqurun televizor koʻraman yoki musiqa tinglayman.

column1: If you are sick or get hurt, tell us right away.
column2: Kasal boʻlsangiz yoki jarohat olsangiz, darhol bizga ayting.

column1: If you don't know something, ask or look it up in a dictionary.
column2: Biror narsani bilmasangiz, soʻrang yoki lugʻatdan qarang.

column1: What do you usually do on your day off?
column2: Dam olish kuningizda odatda nima qilasiz?

column1: I sleep at home or do the laundry.
Sometimes I go to the market or meet friends.
column2: Baʼzan bozorga boraman yoki doʻstlarim bilan uchrashaman.

column1: Used to give a reason. It is like "because…, so…" in English.
column2: Sababni aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…gani uchun, shuning uchun" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -아서/어서 shows a reason, and the second part cannot be an order.
column2: -아서/어서 sababni koʻrsatadi va ikkinchi qism buyruq boʻla olmaydi.

column1: Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "서". For nouns, use "(이)라서".
column2: -아요/어요 shaklidan "요" ni olib, "서" qoʻshing. Otlar uchun "(이)라서" ishlating.

column1: English "because" comes before the reason, but Korean adds "-아서/어서" to the end of the reason part. The reason comes first, and the result comes after.
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "…gani uchun" kabi, koreyschada ham "-아서/어서" sabab qismining oxiriga qoʻshiladi. Avval sabab, keyin natija keladi.

column1: The second part cannot be an order (-세요) or a suggestion (-ㅂ시다). In that case use "-(으)니까". "추워서 문을 닫으세요" is wrong.
column2: Ikkinchi qism buyruq (-세요) yoki taklif (-ㅂ시다) boʻla olmaydi. Bunday holda "-(으)니까" ishlating. "추워서 문을 닫으세요" xato.

column1: Before 고맙다, 미안하다, 죄송하다, 반갑다, always use "-아서/어서": "만나서 반갑습니다." (Nice to meet you.)
column2: 고맙다, 미안하다, 죄송하다, 반갑다 dan oldin doim "-아서/어서" ishlating: "만나서 반갑습니다." (Tanishganimdan xursandman.)

column1: I couldn't go because I was sick.
I was late because of the traffic.
I'm sorry. I missed the bus, so I was late.
column2: Kechirasiz. Avtobusdan qolib ketganim uchun kechikdim.

column1: From next time, please come earlier.
Yes, I'm sorry to have worried you.
Used to give a reason. Used when the second part is an order or a suggestion. It is like "because…, since…" in English.
column2: Sababni aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Ikkinchi qism buyruq yoki taklif boʻlganda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…gani uchun, …ki" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: When you give a reason before an order, use "-(으)니까".
After a 받침 add "-으니까"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-니까". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머니까). For the past, use "-았/었으니까".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으니까", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-니까" qoʻshiladi. ㄹ 받침 tushib qoladi (멀다 → 머니까). Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었으니까" ishlating.

column1: Safety warnings are almost always in the form "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요".
column2: Xavfsizlik ogohlantirishlari deyarli har doim "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요" shaklida boʻladi.

column1: When you give your own reason to a senior, "-(으)니까" can sound like you are arguing. "아파서 못 가요" is softer than "아프니까 못 가요".
column2: Kattalarga oʻz sababingizni aytganda "-(으)니까" bahslashayotgandek eshitilishi mumkin. "아파서 못 가요" "아프니까 못 가요" dan yumshoqroq.

column1: It's hot, so don't touch it.
It's raining, so take an umbrella with you.
column2: Yomgʻir yogʻyapti, shuning uchun soyabon olib keting.

column1: This pot is hot, so be sure to wear gloves.
column2: Bu qozon issiq, shuning uchun albatta qoʻlqop kiying.

column1: Yes, I understand. Should I wear an apron too?
Yes, oil splashes, so wear an apron too.
column2: Ha, yogʻ sachraydi, shuning uchun fartuk ham taqing.

column1: Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
column2: Sababni aniq aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Koʻpincha yozuvda, hisobotlarda va taqdimotlarda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "chunki, …gani sababli" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -기 때문에 is a formal way to state a reason clearly.
column2: -기 때문에 — sababni aniq aytishning rasmiy usuli.

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-기 때문에". For the past, use "-았/었기 때문에"; for nouns, use "noun + 때문에".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-기 때문에" qoʻshing. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었기 때문에", otlar uchun "ot + 때문에" ishlating.

column1: The second part cannot be an order or a suggestion.
column2: Ikkinchi qism buyruq yoki taklif boʻla olmaydi.

column1: Noun + 때문에 is usually the cause of something bad. For the cause of something good, use "덕분에".
column2: Ot + 때문에 odatda yomon narsaning sababi. Yaxshi narsaning sababi uchun "덕분에" ishlating.

column1: To ask for a reason, say "왜요?" or "무엇 때문에요?", and you can end the answer with "~기 때문입니다".
column2: Sababni soʻrash uchun "왜요?" yoki "무엇 때문에요?" deng, javobni esa "~기 때문입니다" bilan tugatish mumkin.

column1: Because it is raining, the festival was canceled.
column2: Yomgʻir yogʻayotgani sababli festival bekor qilindi.

column1: Because I have a lot of assignments, I'm going to the library.
column2: Topshiriqlarim koʻp boʻlgani sababli kutubxonaga ketyapman.

column1: I went to the hospital because of a cold.
Because the bus broke down, I was late for class.
column2: Avtobus buzilib qolgani sababli darsga kechikdim.

column1: Sam, why did you hand in the assignment late?
It's because my laptop broke down yesterday.
Yes, I had it repaired, so there is no problem.
column2: Ha, taʼmirlatdim, shuning uchun muammo yoʻq.

column1: Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
column2: Shartni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "agar …sa" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -(으)면 means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.
column2: -(으)면 "agar …sa" degan maʼnoni bildiradi va shartning oxiriga qoʻshiladi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면". For nouns, use "(이)면".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으면", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-면" qoʻshiladi. Otlar uchun "(이)면" ishlating.

column1: English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "-sa" kabi, "-(으)면" ham shartning oxiriga qoʻshiladi: "bilmasangiz" = "모르면".

column1: It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
column2: U albatta sodir boʻladigan narsalar uchun ham ishlatiladi. Unda "…ganda" degan maʼnoni bildiradi: "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (Bahor kelganda havo isiydi.)

column1: You can add "만약, 만일, 혹시" in front to make the condition clear: "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (If you are late, please contact me.)
column2: Shartni aniq qilish uchun oldiga "만약, 만일, 혹시" qoʻshish mumkin: "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (Agar kechiksangiz, xabar bering.)

column1: If you have time, let's go together.
If it hurts, don't put up with it. Tell us.
to put up with, hold back
What do you do if there is a fire in the dorm?
to break out (불이 나다 = a fire breaks out)
I go outside right away and call 119.
column2: Darhol tashqariga chiqib, 119 ga qoʻngʻiroq qilaman.

column1: Right. If the stairs are dark, turn on your phone's light.
column2: Toʻgʻri. Zinapoya qorongʻi boʻlsa, telefoningiz chirogʻini yoqing.

column1: Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
column2: …moqchi boʻlsangiz degan maʼnoni bildiradi. Maqsadga qanday erishishni aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…moqchi boʻlsangiz, …ish uchun" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -(으)려면 means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
column2: -(으)려면 "…moqchi boʻlsangiz" degani, undan keyin esa buning yoʻli aytiladi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으려면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려면". After it comes "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요" or "-(으)면 돼요".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으려면", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-려면" qoʻshiladi. Undan keyin "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요" yoki "-(으)면 돼요" keladi.

column1: It is the most useful pattern for asking the way or asking about procedures: "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (What do I have to do to…?)
column2: Bu yoʻl soʻrash yoki tartib-qoidalar haqida soʻrash uchun eng foydali qolip: "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (…ish uchun nima qilishim kerak?)

column1: To go to Korea, you have to take a test.
column2: Koreyaga borish uchun imtihon topshirishingiz kerak.

column1: To open a bank account, you need your residence card.
column2: Bankda hisob ochish uchun chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangiz (ID karta) kerak.

column1: Which bus do I have to take to go to City Hall?
column2: Shahar hokimiyatiga borish uchun qaysi avtobusga oʻtirishim kerak?

column1: If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.
column2: Koreys tilini yaxshi bilmoqchi boʻlsangiz, har kuni mashq qiling.

column1: if you want to be good at
What do I have to do to extend my period of stay?
column2: Yashash muddatimni uzaytirish uchun nima qilishim kerak?

column1: You have to apply at the immigration office.
What do I need to apply?
You need your passport, residence card and certificate of enrollment.
column2: Pasportingiz, chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangiz (ID karta) va oʻqish joyidan maʼlumotnoma kerak.

column1: Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
column2: Borish yoki kelish maqsadini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…gani bormoq/kelmoq" (yegani bormoq) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으러"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-러", then use "가다, 오다, 다니다".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으러", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-러" qoʻshiladi, keyin "가다, 오다, 다니다" ishlatiladi.

column1: In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, koreyschada ham "bormoq" oxirida keladi: "yegani boraman" = "먹으러 가요".

column1: Only verbs of movement (가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다) can come after it. With other verbs, use "-(으)려고".
column2: Undan keyin faqat harakat feʼllari (가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다) kela oladi. Boshqa feʼllar bilan "-(으)려고" ishlating.

column1: Say the place you go to with "에": "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (I'm going to a restaurant to eat.)
column2: Boradigan joyni "에" bilan ayting: "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (Ovqatlangani restoranga ketyapman.)

column1: I came to Korea to study.
Come over and visit on the weekend.
I'm going to the bank to take out money.
go out (to have fun), go on a trip
I'm going to the post office to send a package.
I have to go mail a letter too, so let's go together.
column2: Men ham xat joʻnatishim kerak, birga boraylik.

column1: Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
column2: Harakatning maqsadini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ish uchun, …moqchi boʻlib" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -(으)려고 means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.
column2: -(으)려고 "…ish uchun" degan maʼnoni bildiradi va maqsad birinchi aytiladi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으려고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려고". Any verb can come after it.
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으려고", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-려고" qoʻshiladi. Undan keyin istalgan feʼl kela oladi.

column1: In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, koreyschada ham avval maqsad, keyin harakat keladi.

column1: Orders and suggestions are not usually used after it. In that case, use "-(으)려면".
column2: Undan keyin odatda buyruq va taklif ishlatilmaydi. Bunday holda "-(으)려면" ishlating.

column1: At a counter, to say why you came, say "~(으)려고 왔어요" or "~(으)려고요".
column2: Peshtaxtada nima uchun kelganingizni aytish uchun "~(으)려고 왔어요" yoki "~(으)려고요" deng.

column1: I came to open a bank account.
I'm saving money to send to my family.
I'm learning Korean to study at a Korean university.
column2: Koreys universitetida oʻqish uchun koreys tilini oʻrganyapman.

column1: I went to bed early so I could get up early.
How can I help you? (Why did you come?)
column2: Sizga qanday yordam bera olaman? (Nima uchun keldingiz?)

column1: I came to pay my tuition.
Please give me your bankbook and ID card.
column2: Omonat daftarchangiz va ID kartangizni bering.

column1: Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
column2: Hozirgina aytgan gapingizning sababini qoʻshish uchun ishlatiladi. Tinglovchi bilmaydigan narsani aytadi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…-da, axir…" yoki "chunki…" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -거든요 adds the reason for what was said before, after it.
column2: -거든요 oldin aytilgan gapning sababini undan keyin qoʻshadi.

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-거든요". For the past, use "-았/었거든요"; for nouns, use "(이)거든요".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-거든요" qoʻshing. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었거든요", otlar uchun "(이)거든요" ishlating.

column1: The reason comes after. The order is the opposite of "-아서/어서": "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
column2: Sabab keyin keladi. Tartib "-아서/어서" ga teskari: "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."

column1: I'm leaving early today. I have plans, you see.
I won't eat. I ate a little while ago, you see.
I'm not sure. It's my first time here, you see.
column2: Aniq bilmayman. Bu yerga birinchi marta kelishim-da.

column1: I'm a little tired these days. I have a lot of assignments, you see.
column2: Keyingi paytlarda biroz charchadim. Topshiriqlarim koʻp-da.

column1: because it's (my) first time, you see
Sam, aren't you going to the club meeting today?
No, I can't go. I'm not feeling well, you see.
(몸이 안 좋다 = to not feel well)
I've had a headache since yesterday, you see.
Used to give the reason for a good result, with thanks. It is like "thanks to…" in English.
column2: Yaxshi natija sababini minnatdorlik bilan aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…tufayli, …ning sharofati bilan" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: 덕분에 gives the reason for a good result, with thanks.
column2: 덕분에 yaxshi natija sababini minnatdorlik bilan aytadi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-은 덕분에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 덕분에". For nouns, use "noun + 덕분에".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-은 덕분에", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄴ 덕분에" qoʻshiladi. Otlar uchun "ot + 덕분에" ishlating.

column1: Use it only for good things. For bad things, use "때문에" or "-는 바람에".
column2: Uni faqat yaxshi narsalar uchun ishlating. Yomon narsalar uchun "때문에" yoki "-는 바람에" ishlating.

column1: 덕분에 잘 지냈어요 and "덕분입니다" are set phrases used to answer "How have you been?"
column2: 덕분에 잘 지냈어요 va "덕분입니다" — "Qalaysiz, yaxshi yuribsizmi?" savoliga javob beradigan turgʻun iboralar.

column1: Thanks to your help, we finished quickly.
Thanks to the professor, I learned Korean well.
column2: Professor tufayli koreys tilini yaxshi oʻrgandim.

column1: I've been well, thanks to you.
Thanks to practicing hard, I passed the test.
column2: Astoydil mashq qilganim tufayli imtihondan oʻtdim.

column1: Sam, you got 100 points on this exam. Well done.
column2: Sam, bu imtihonda 100 ball oldingiz. Barakalla.

column1: Thank you. It's thanks to Jinha teaching me well.
column2: Rahmat. Bu Jinha menga yaxshi oʻrgatgani tufayli.

column1: to give (-아/어 주다 = do for someone)
Keep working hard from now on too.
column2: Bundan keyin ham astoydil harakat qiling.

column1: A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
column2: Feʼl otni tavsiflaydi. Hozir sodir boʻlayotgan yoki muntazam qilinadigan narsani koʻrsatadi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ayotgan, …adigan + ot" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off verbs and "있다/없다", add "-는", then put the noun. A ㄹ 받침 drops (살다 → 사는).
column2: Feʼllar va "있다/없다" dan "-다" ni olib, "-는" qoʻshing, keyin otni qoʻying. ㄹ 받침 tushib qoladi (살다 → 사는).

column1: In English the describing part comes after the noun (a person who works), but in Korean it comes before (일하는 사람). There is no separate word for "who, that".
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, koreyschada ham tavsiflovchi qism otdan oldin keladi (ishlaydigan odam = 일하는 사람). "Qaysiki" kabi alohida soʻz kerak emas.

column1: 맛있다, 재미있다 also end in "있다", so they use "-는": "맛있는 음식" (tasty food), "재미없는 영화" (a boring movie).
column2: 맛있다, 재미있다 ham "있다" bilan tugagani uchun "-는" ishlatadi: "맛있는 음식" (mazali taom), "재미없는 영화" (zerikarli film).

column1: What is the work you are doing now?
The person standing over there is the teaching assistant.
column2: Ana u yerda turgan odam — assistent.

column1: The place where I live is Jeonju.
If there is something you don't know, ask.
Who is the person wearing a hat over there?
column2: Ana u yerdagi shapka kiygan odam kim?

column1: That's Aisha, who studies with me.
column2: U men bilan birga oʻqiydigan Aisha.

column1: What part-time job does Aisha do?
She makes coffee at a cafe.
It is used in two ways: ① An adjective describes a noun (큰 상자, a big box). ② Added to a verb, it shows the past (어제 만난 사람, the person I met yesterday).
column2: U ikki xil ishlatiladi: ① Sifat otni tavsiflaydi (큰 상자, katta quti). ② Feʼlga qoʻshilsa, oʻtgan zamonni koʻrsatadi (어제 만난 사람, kecha uchrashgan odamim).

column1: Adjective + "-(으)ㄴ" describes; verb + "-(으)ㄴ" shows the past.
column2: Sifat + "-(으)ㄴ" tavsiflaydi; feʼl + "-(으)ㄴ" oʻtgan zamonni koʻrsatadi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-은"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ". A ㄹ 받침 drops (길다 → 긴), and ㅂ irregular becomes "-운" (덥다 → 더운).
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-은", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄴ" qoʻshiladi. ㄹ 받침 tushib qoladi (길다 → 긴), ㅂ notoʻgʻri feʼli esa "-운" ga aylanadi (덥다 → 더운).

column1: As in English "big box", the adjective comes before the noun, but in Korean the adjective changes its form (크다 → 큰 상자).
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "katta quti" kabi sifat otdan oldin keladi, lekin koreyschada sifat shaklini oʻzgartiradi (크다 → 큰 상자).

column1: It is the same "-(으)ㄴ", but with adjectives it is a present quality, and with verbs it is the past: "바쁜 사람" (a busy person), "온 사람" (a person who came).
column2: Bu bir xil "-(으)ㄴ", lekin sifatlarda hozirgi xususiyat, feʼllarda esa oʻtgan zamon: "바쁜 사람" (band odam), "온 사람" (kelgan odam).

column1: Who is the person you met yesterday?
The shoes I bought last week are small.
column2: Oʻtgan hafta sotib olgan oyoq kiyimim kichik.

column1: Sam, where are the books you borrowed yesterday?
I put them in that big box.
column2: Ularni ana u katta qutiga soldim.

column1: Did you put the small ones in too?
No, I put the small ones in the blue box.
Describes a noun with something you will do or that has not happened yet. It is like "… to do, … that (I) will…" in English.
column2: Otni qiladigan yoki hali sodir boʻlmagan narsa bilan tavsiflaydi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…adigan + ot" (qiladigan ish) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Verb + -(으)ㄹ + noun means "noun + to + verb" (work to do).
After a 받침 add "-을"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ". A ㄹ 받침 stays as it is (만들다 → 만들).
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-을", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄹ" qoʻshiladi. ㄹ 받침 oʻzgarmaydi (만들다 → 만들).

column1: Compare the three forms: 하는 일 (work I'm doing), 한 일 (work I did), 할 일 (work I will do).
column2: Uchta shaklni solishtiring: 하는 일 (qilayotgan ishim), 한 일 (qilgan ishim), 할 일 (qiladigan ishim).

column1: After "-(으)ㄹ", ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅈ become tense sounds: 갈 곳 [갈 꼳], 먹을 것 [머글 껃].
column2: -(으)ㄹ dan keyin ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅈ taranglashgan tovushga aylanadi: 갈 곳 [갈 꼳], 먹을 것 [머글 껃].

column1: -(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 all come from this form.
column2: -(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 hammasi shu shakldan kelib chiqqan.

column1: I have a lot of work to do tomorrow.
I have no time to rest.
I have something to tell you. (humble)
I'll tell you the work to do today.
This morning there are 50 cups to wash.
column2: Bugun ertalab yuvish kerak boʻlgan 50 ta stakan bor.

column1: I understand. Is there work to do in the afternoon too?
column2: Tushundim. Tushdan keyin ham qiladigan ish bormi?

column1: Lets a verb be used like a noun. It is like "…ing" (cooking) or "to…" in English.
column2: Feʼlni ot kabi ishlatishga imkon beradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ish" (pishirish) ga oʻxshaydi.
Feʼl + -는 것 "…ish" (harakat nomi) degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 것". In speech, shorten "것이 → 게", "것을 → 걸", "것은 → 건".
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-는 것" qoʻshing. Ogʻzaki nutqda "것이 → 게", "것을 → 걸", "것은 → 건" ga qisqaradi.

column1: Like English "-ing", "-는 것" comes after the verb: "learning" = "배우는 것".
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "-ish" kabi, "-는 것" feʼldan keyin keladi: "oʻrganish" = "배우는 것".

column1: It is often used before "좋아하다, 싫어하다, 잘하다, 못하다": "운전하는 것을 잘해요." (I'm good at driving.)
column2: U koʻpincha "좋아하다, 싫어하다, 잘하다, 못하다" dan oldin ishlatiladi: "운전하는 것을 잘해요." (Men mashinani yaxshi haydayman.)

column1: 것 also means "thing, one": "이것, 그것, 먹을 것, 큰 것" (this, that, something to eat, a big one).
column2: 것 yana "narsa" degan maʼnoni ham bildiradi: "이것, 그것, 먹을 것, 큰 것" (bu, u, yeydigan narsa, kattasi).

column1: Sam, what do you like to do on your days off?
column2: Sam, dam olish kunlaringizda nima qilishni yoqtirasiz?

column1: I like playing soccer. What about you, Minha?
column2: Futbol oʻynashni yaxshi koʻraman. Siz-chi, Minha?

column1: I like watching movies at home.
column2: Men uyda kino koʻrishni yaxshi koʻraman.

column1: -기 also turns a verb into a noun. Before "쉽다, 어렵다, 좋다, 편하다, 힘들다" it means "easy/hard/good… to do".
column2: -기 ham feʼlni otga aylantiradi. "쉽다, 어렵다, 좋다, 편하다, 힘들다" dan oldin "…ish oson/qiyin/yaxshi…" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-기". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-기" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas.

column1: The order is the opposite of English "hard to learn": add "-기" to the verb and put "어렵다, 쉽다" after it. "hard to learn" = "배우기 어려워요".
column2: Tartib oʻzbek tilidagidek: feʼlga "-기" qoʻshib, undan keyin "어렵다, 쉽다" qoʻying. "oʻrganish qiyin" = "배우기 어려워요".

column1: In lists, titles and notes, end with "-기": "말하기 (speaking), 듣기 (listening), 읽기 (reading), 쓰기 (writing)", "과제 내기" (hand in the assignment), "손 씻기" (wash hands).
column2: Roʻyxatlar, sarlavhalar va qaydlarda "-기" bilan tugating: "말하기 (gapirish), 듣기 (tinglash), 읽기 (oʻqish), 쓰기 (yozish)", "과제 내기" (topshiriqni topshirish), "손 씻기" (qoʻl yuvish).

column1: This laptop is easy to use.
This neighborhood is a good place to live.
column2: Bu mahalla yashash uchun yaxshi joy.

column1: It's hot today, so it's hard to study.
column2: Bugun issiq, shuning uchun oʻqish qiyin.

column1: How is your Korean study going?
Reading is easy, but speaking is hard.
ㅓ and "ㅗ" are hard to tell apart.
Turns an adjective into a word that tells "how" something is done. It is like "-ly" (safely, loudly) in English.
column2: Sifatni harakat "qanday" bajarilishini bildiradigan soʻzga aylantiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "-cha, …ib" yoki ravish (xavfsiz, baland ovozda) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Adjective + -게 + verb means "verb + -ly" (speak loudly, ride safely).
column2: Sifat + -게 + feʼl harakatning qanday bajarilishini bildiradi (baland gapirmoq, ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydamoq).

column1: Take "-다" off the adjective and add "-게". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: Sifatdan "-다" ni olib, "-게" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas.

column1: In English it often comes after the verb (wipe it clean, speak loudly), but in Korean it comes before the verb (깨끗하게 닦아요).
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, u feʼldan oldin keladi: "toza arting" = "깨끗하게 닦아요".

column1: Some words use another form instead of "-게": 많다 → 많이, 빠르다 → 빨리, 멀다 → 멀리, 깨끗하다 → 깨끗이 (깨끗하게 is also fine).
column2: Baʼzi soʻzlar "-게" oʻrniga boshqa shakl ishlatadi: 많다 → 많이, 빠르다 → 빨리, 멀다 → 멀리, 깨끗하다 → 깨끗이 (깨끗하게 ham toʻgʻri).

column1: Sam, please wipe this table cleaner.
column2: Sam, bu stolni tozaroq qilib arting.

column1: Yes. Is this okay? (Should I do it like this?)
Good. And don't stack the cups high.
column2: Yaxshi. Va stakanlarni baland qilib taxlamang.

column1: Tells the time when something happens. It is like "when" in English.
column2: Biror narsa sodir boʻladigan vaqtni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ganda" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-을 때"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ 때". For the past, use "-았/었을 때"; for nouns, use "noun + 때".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-을 때", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄹ 때" qoʻshiladi. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었을 때", otlar uchun "ot + 때" ishlating.

column1: English "when" comes first, but "-(으)ㄹ 때" is added at the end: "when eating" = "먹을 때".
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi "-ganda" kabi, "-(으)ㄹ 때" ham oxiriga qoʻshiladi: "yeyayotganda" = "먹을 때".

column1: 갈 때 is on the way there; "갔을 때" is after you get there: "집에 갈 때 샀어요" (I bought it on my way home), "집에 갔을 때 없었어요" (When I got home, it wasn't there).
column2: 갈 때 — u yerga ketayotgan yoʻlda; "갔을 때" — u yerga yetib borgandan keyin: "집에 갈 때 샀어요" (uyga ketayotib sotib oldim), "집에 갔을 때 없었어요" (uyga borganimda u yoʻq edi).

column1: It is the basic pattern of rules and notices: "~할 때는 ~하십시오." (When you…, do….)
column2: Bu qoidalar va eʼlonlarning asosiy qolipi: "~할 때는 ~하십시오." (…ganda, … qiling.)

column1: I drink a lot of water when I exercise.
column2: Sport bilan shugʻullanganda koʻp suv ichaman.

column1: When you are sick, you have to rest.
When I first came to Korea, it was very cold.
column2: Koreyaga birinchi kelganimda juda sovuq edi.

column1: Call me when you have time.
What should I do when I lift something heavy?
column2: Ogʻir narsani koʻtarganda nima qilishim kerak?

column1: Keep your back straight, bend your knees and lift.
column2: Belingizni tik tutib, tizzalaringizni bukib koʻtaring.

column1: Right. When it's hard to lift alone, be sure to ask for help.
column2: Toʻgʻri. Yolgʻiz koʻtarish qiyin boʻlganda, albatta yordam soʻrang.

column1: to ask (for something) (-아/어 달라고 = ask someone to…)
Tells your feeling about something you just found out by seeing or hearing it. It is like "Oh, …!" or "…, isn't it!" in English.
column2: Koʻrib yoki eshitib hozirgina bilib olgan narsangiz haqidagi hissiyotingizni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "Voy, …-ku!" yoki "…ekan!" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -네요 shows your feeling about something you have just found out.
column2: -네요 hozirgina bilib olgan narsangiz haqidagi hissiyotni koʻrsatadi.

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-네요". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머네요). For the past, use "-았/었네요"; for nouns, use "(이)네요".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-네요" qoʻshing. ㄹ 받침 tushib qoladi (멀다 → 머네요). Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었네요", otlar uchun "(이)네요" ishlating.

column1: The sound changes: 좋네요 [존네요], 맛있네요 [마신네요], 춥네요 [춤네요].
When you get a compliment, answer "아니에요, 아직 멀었어요" (No, I still have a long way to go) or "감사합니다".
column2: Maqtov eshitganingizda "아니에요, 아직 멀었어요" (Yoʻq, hali koʻp oʻrganishim kerak) yoki "감사합니다" deb javob bering.

column1: It is not used for things you already knew.
column2: U allaqachon bilgan narsalaringiz uchun ishlatilmaydi.

column1: Sam, you've already finished it all! You're fast!
column2: Sam, hammasini allaqachon tugatibsiz! Tez ekansiz!

column1: No. I still have a long way to go.
Your Korean has improved a lot too!
Used to check something you think the listener also knows, or to ask them to agree. It is like "…, right?" or "…, isn't it?" in English.
column2: Tinglovchi ham biladi deb oʻylagan narsangizni tekshirish yoki rozilik soʻrash uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…-a?, …-ku, toʻgʻrimi?" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -지요? is a checking question, like "…, right?".
Take "-다" off and add "-지요?". In speech it is shortened to "-죠?". For nouns, use "(이)지요?".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-지요?" qoʻshing. Ogʻzaki nutqda "-죠?" ga qisqaradi. Otlar uchun "(이)지요?" ishlating.

column1: The answer is "네, 추워요" or "네, 맞아요". If not, say "아니요, 괜찮아요".
column2: Javob "네, 추워요" yoki "네, 맞아요". Agar unday boʻlmasa, "아니요, 괜찮아요" deng.

column1: With question words it becomes a soft question: "이게 얼마지요?" (How much is this?), "화장실이 어디죠?" (Where is the restroom?)
column2: Soʻroq soʻzlari bilan u yumshoq savolga aylanadi: "이게 얼마지요?" (Bu qancha boʻldi?), "화장실이 어디죠?" (Hojatxona qayerda edi?)

column1: When a Korean says "힘들지요?", it is a greeting that shows care. You can just answer "괜찮습니다".
column2: Koreys kishi "힘들지요?" desa, bu gʻamxoʻrlik bildiruvchi salomlashish. Shunchaki "괜찮습니다" deb javob bersangiz boʻladi.

column1: There's a group meeting tomorrow, right?
Sam, this is your first Korean winter, right?
column2: Sam, bu sizning Koreyadagi birinchi qishingiz, toʻgʻrimi?

column1: Yes, it's cold, but the snow is pretty.
Tells a guess based on what you see or hear. It is like "I think…, It seems…" in English.
column2: Koʻrgan yoki eshitgan narsangizga asoslangan taxminni bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…shekilli, …ga oʻxshaydi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -는 것 같아요 means "I think…, It seems…" and tells a guess.
column2: -는 것 같아요 "…shekilli, …ga oʻxshaydi" degan maʼnoni bildiradi va taxminni aytadi.

column1: Add "-는 것 같아요" to verbs, "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요" to adjectives, "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요" for the past (verbs), and "noun + 같아요" to nouns.
column2: Feʼllarga "-는 것 같아요", sifatlarga "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요", oʻtgan zamon uchun (feʼllar) "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요", otlarga "ot + 같아요" qoʻshiladi.

column1: It is also used to give your opinion softly. "이게 더 좋은 것 같아요" (I think this is better) sounds less stiff than "이게 더 좋아요".
column2: U fikringizni yumshoq aytish uchun ham ishlatiladi. "이게 더 좋은 것 같아요" (Menimcha, bu yaxshiroq) "이게 더 좋아요" dan kamroq qatʼiy eshitiladi.

column1: It is useful for reporting problems: "소리가 이상한 것 같습니다" (The sound seems strange), "고장 난 것 같습니다" (It seems to be broken).
column2: U muammolar haqida xabar berish uchun foydali: "소리가 이상한 것 같습니다" (Ovozi gʻalati shekilli), "고장 난 것 같습니다" (Buzilib qolganga oʻxshaydi).

column1: In speech, "것" is shortened to "거": "오는 거 같아요".
column2: Ogʻzaki nutqda "것" "거" ga qisqaradi: "오는 거 같아요".

column1: It seems to be raining outside.
I think this printer is broken.
I think I've caught a cold.
Excuse me (TA), I think this printer is making a strange sound.
column2: Kechirasiz (assistent), bu printer gʻalati ovoz chiqaryapti shekilli.

column1: (a sound) to come out, be made
I think since ten minutes ago.
Turn it off for now. It seems the paper is stuck.
column2: Hozircha oʻchirib qoʻying. Qogʻoz tiqilib qolganga oʻxshaydi.

column1: A guess that something will happen. It is like "I think … will…, It looks like… will…, probably" in English.
column2: Biror narsa sodir boʻladi degan taxmin. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…sa kerak, …adiganga oʻxshaydi, ehtimol" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 means "I think … will…, probably".
column2: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 "…sa kerak, ehtimol" degan maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: After a 받침 add "-을 것 같아요"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ 것 같아요".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-을 것 같아요", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄹ 것 같아요" qoʻshiladi.

column1: It is a soft way to say no or give bad news. "못 갈 것 같아요" (I don't think I can go) is more polite than "못 가요".
column2: Bu rad etish yoki yomon xabar aytishning yumshoq usuli. "못 갈 것 같아요" (Bora olmasam kerak) "못 가요" dan muloyimroq.

column1: When you will be late, always tell them in advance: "차가 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같습니다." (There's traffic, so I think I'll be a little late.)
column2: Kechikadigan boʻlsangiz, doim oldindan xabar bering: "차가 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같습니다." (Tirbandlik, biroz kechiksam kerak.)

column1: It is also used for a guess from what you see in front of you. Seeing food, you say "맛있을 것 같아요" (It looks tasty).
column2: U koʻz oldingizda koʻrgan narsangizdan taxmin qilish uchun ham ishlatiladi. Ovqatni koʻrib, "맛있을 것 같아요" (Mazali boʻlsa kerak) deysiz.

column1: I'm sorry. I think I'll be about ten minutes late.
column2: Kechirasiz. Taxminan oʻn daqiqa kechiksam kerak.

column1: It looks like it's going to rain.
I think it will be finished today.
I don't think I can go tomorrow.
It looks like it will rain
It looks like it will be tasty
I think it will be finished
I think it will be hard
Professor, I'm sorry. The bus isn't coming, so I think I'll be a little late.
column2: Professor, kechirasiz. Avtobus kelmayapti, shuning uchun biroz kechiksam kerak.

column1: How late do you think you'll be?
I think it will take about twenty minutes.
Means it seems so from the outside. It is like "look…" (look tired) in English.
column2: Tashqi koʻrinishdan shunday tuyulishini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…koʻrinadi" (charchagan koʻrinadi) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "요" off the adjective's "-아요/어요" form and add "보여요".
It is used only with adjectives. With verbs, use "-는 것 같아요".
column2: U faqat sifatlar bilan ishlatiladi. Feʼllar bilan "-는 것 같아요" ishlating.

column1: It is only for what you see with your eyes. For what you know by hearing or tasting, use "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요".
column2: Bu faqat koʻz bilan koʻrgan narsa uchun. Eshitib yoki tatib bilgan narsangiz uchun "-(으)ㄴ 것 같아요" ishlating.

column1: When a friend says "피곤해 보여요" or "아파 보여요", they are showing they care about you.
column2: Doʻstingiz "피곤해 보여요" yoki "아파 보여요" desa, u sizga gʻamxoʻrlik qilayotgan boʻladi.

column1: You look like you're in a good mood.
You don't look well. Are you sick?
Sam, you look very tired today.
Yes, I studied for an exam until late last night, so I couldn't sleep.
column2: Ha, kecha kechgacha imtihonga tayyorlandim, shuning uchun uxlay olmadim.

column1: You don't look well either. Rest early today.
column2: Sizning ham rangingiz yaxshi emas. Bugun erta dam oling.

column1: Used to remind the listener of something they already know. It feels like "…, you know" or "As you know…".
column2: Tinglovchiga u allaqachon biladigan narsani eslatish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…-ku, bilasiz-ku" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -잖아요 reminds the other person of something they also know, and is not used with seniors.
column2: -잖아요 suhbatdoshga u ham biladigan narsani eslatadi va kattalarga nisbatan ishlatilmaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-잖아요". For the past, use "-았/었잖아요"; for nouns, use "(이)잖아요".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-잖아요" qoʻshing. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었잖아요", otlar uchun "(이)잖아요" ishlating.

column1: Used with seniors, it sounds like you are arguing. Use it only with close friends; don't use it with professors.
column2: Kattalarga ishlatilsa, bahslashayotgandek eshitiladi. Uni faqat yaqin doʻstlar bilan ishlating; professorlarga ishlatmang.

column1: 있잖아요 is also used to start talking: "저, 있잖아요…" = Um, you know…
column2: 있잖아요 gap boshlash uchun ham ishlatiladi: "저, 있잖아요…" = Hm, bilasizmi…

column1: It's cold outside, you know. Put on more clothes.
There's a test tomorrow, you know.
I told you yesterday, you know.
Sam, why aren't you going to school today?
Today is a day off, you know.
Oh, right. It's the school's founding day!
column2: Ha, toʻgʻri. Universitet tashkil topgan kun ekan!
universitet tashkil topgan kun (dam olish kuni)

column1: Shows the feeling "Oh, I see" about something you have just learned. It is like "Oh, I see. / So…!" in English.
column2: Hozirgina bilib olgan narsangiz haqida "A, shunaqami" degan hissiyotni koʻrsatadi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "A, shunaqa ekan-da. / …ekan-da!" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -군요 is a feeling about something you just realized, and "그렇군요" is a reply (Oh, I see).
column2: -군요 hozirgina anglagan narsangiz haqidagi hissiyot, "그렇군요" esa javob (A, shunaqa ekan-da).

column1: Add "-는군요" to verbs, "-군요" to adjectives, "-았/었군요" for the past, and "(이)군요" to nouns.
column2: Feʼllarga "-는군요", sifatlarga "-군요", oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었군요", otlarga "(이)군요" qoʻshiladi.

column1: 아, 그렇군요 is a reply that means you understood after hearing an explanation. It is used very often.
column2: 아, 그렇군요 tushuntirishni eshitib tushunganingizni bildiradigan javob. Juda koʻp ishlatiladi.

column1: -네요 is a feeling you have right now; "-군요" is something you realize by hearing or thinking. "-군요" is a little more polite.
column2: -네요 — hozir his qilayotgan hissiyotingiz; "-군요" — eshitib yoki oʻylab anglagan narsangiz. "-군요" biroz muloyimroq.

column1: So you've already finished it all!
Oh, so your hometown is Yangon.
column2: A, demak, tugʻilgan shahringiz Yangon ekan-da.

column1: to be so, be like that
Sam, what work did you do in the USA?
I worked part-time at a hotel for one year.
column2: Bir yil mehmonxonada qoʻshimcha ish qilganman.

column1: Oh, I see. So that's why you know hotel work well.
column2: A, shunaqa ekan-da. Shuning uchun mehmonxona ishini yaxshi bilar ekansiz-da.

column1: Used to pass on what someone else said or what you heard. It is like "(He) said that…, I heard that…" in English.
column2: Boshqa birovning aytganini yoki eshitgan narsangizni yetkazish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…di dedi, …ekan deb eshitdim" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Pass on what you heard with "-다고 했어요".
For verbs add "-는다고" after a 받침 and "-ㄴ다고" with no 받침; for adjectives "-다고"; for the past "-았/었다고"; for the future "-(으)ㄹ 거라고"; for nouns "(이)라고", then use "해요/했어요".
column2: Feʼllarga 받침 boʻlsa "-는다고", 받침 boʻlmasa "-ㄴ다고"; sifatlarga "-다고"; oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었다고"; kelasi zamon uchun "-(으)ㄹ 거라고"; otlarga "(이)라고" qoʻshiladi, keyin "해요/했어요" ishlatiladi.

column1: In English "said (that)" comes first, but in Korean the reported words come first and "-다고 했어요" comes at the end.
column2: Oʻzbek tilidagi kabi, koreyschada ham avval yetkazilayotgan gap keladi, "-다고 했어요" (…deb aytdi) esa oxirida turadi.

column1: To give your name, say "저는 샘이라고 합니다" (I'm called Sam). "이것은 한국어로 뭐라고 해요?" (What is this called in Korean?) uses the same pattern.
column2: Ismingizni aytish uchun "저는 샘이라고 합니다" (Meni Sam deyishadi) deng. "이것은 한국어로 뭐라고 해요?" (Bu koreyschada nima deyiladi?) ham shu qolipni ishlatadi.

column1: It is very important when interpreting or passing on what the professor said to friends.
column2: Bu tarjima qilganda yoki professorning aytganlarini doʻstlarga yetkazganda juda muhim.

column1: The teaching assistant said he is off tomorrow.
Aisha said she is busy today.
The weather forecast said it will rain tomorrow.
column2: Ob-havo maʼlumotida ertaga yomgʻir yogʻishini aytdi.

column1: Sam, what did the professor say?
He said the library is closed tomorrow.
column2: U ertaga kutubxona yopiq boʻlishini aytdi.

column1: He said they are checking the computers.
Used to pass on someone else's order. It is like "(He) told me to…" in English.
column2: Boshqa birovning buyrugʻini yetkazish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ing dedi, …ishimni aytdi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Pass on orders with "-(으)라고 했어요", and "don't" orders with "-지 말라고 했어요".
column2: Buyruqlarni "-(으)라고 했어요" bilan, "…mang" buyruqlarini esa "-지 말라고 했어요" bilan yetkazing.

column1: After a 받침 add "-으라고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-라고". For "not to", use "-지 말라고".
column2: 받침 boʻlsa "-으라고", 받침 boʻlmasa yoki ㄹ 받침 boʻlsa "-라고" qoʻshiladi. "…masin" uchun "-지 말라고" ishlating.

column1: To pass on "-아/어 주세요", use "-아/어 달라고 하다" (for the speaker) and "-아/어 주라고 하다" (for someone else): "도와 달라고 했어요" = He asked (me) to help him.
column2: -아/어 주세요 ni yetkazish uchun "-아/어 달라고 하다" (soʻzlovchining oʻzi uchun) va "-아/어 주라고 하다" (boshqa birov uchun) ishlating: "도와 달라고 했어요" = U (mendan) yordam berishimni soʻradi.

column1: To check an instruction again, ask "~(으)라고 하셨지요?": "세 시까지 끝내라고 하셨지요?" (You told me to finish by three, right?)
column2: Koʻrsatmani yana bir bor aniqlash uchun "~(으)라고 하셨지요?" deb soʻrang: "세 시까지 끝내라고 하셨지요?" (Soat uchgacha tugatishimni aytgandingiz, toʻgʻrimi?)

column1: The professor told me to wait.
The doctor told me to take the medicine.
The head of the department told you to come to the department office.
column2: Kafedra mudiri sizni kafedra idorasiga kelishingizni aytdi.

column1: They told us not to touch this computer.
(He) told me not to touch it
(He) asked (me) to give it to him
He told me to move this box to the department office.
column2: Bu qutini kafedra idorasiga olib borishimni aytdi.

column1: No, he told me not to touch that one.
Used to pass on a suggestion. It is like "(He) suggested…, (He) said let's…" in English.
column2: Taklifni yetkazish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…aylik dedi, …ishni taklif qildi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-자고 해요/했어요". It does not depend on 받침. For "let's not", use "-지 말자고".
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-자고 해요/했어요" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas. "…maylik" uchun "-지 말자고" ishlating.

column1: When passing on "-(으)ㅂ시다, -아요/어요 (let's), -(으)ㄹ까요?", they all become "-자고 하다".
column2: -(으)ㅂ시다, -아요/어요 (…aylik), -(으)ㄹ까요? ni yetkazganda hammasi "-자고 하다" ga aylanadi.

column1: If a senior said it, show respect with "-자고 하셨어요".
column2: Agar kattaroq kishi aytgan boʻlsa, "-자고 하셨어요" bilan hurmat koʻrsating.

column1: My senior says let's have an after-party today.
column2: Katta kursdoshim bugun ziyofatdan keyin yana davom ettiraylik deyapti.

column1: Minha suggested going hiking on the weekend.
column2: Minha dam olish kunlari togʻga sayrga borishni taklif qildi.

column1: Aisha says let's rest a little.
Aisha, the professor suggested having dinner together tonight.
column2: Aisha, professor bugun kechqurun birga kechki ovqat qilishni taklif qildi.

column1: He said to meet at six at the samgyeopsal restaurant in front of the school.
column2: Soat oltida universitet oldidagi samgyeopsal restoranida uchrashaylik dedi.

column1: Used to pass on someone else's question. It is like "(He) asked…" in English.
column2: Boshqa birovning savolini yetkazish uchun ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…mi deb soʻradi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Take "-다" off and add "-냐고 하다/묻다/물어보다". For the past, use "-았/었냐고"; for nouns, use "(이)냐고".
column2: -다 ni olib, "-냐고 하다/묻다/물어보다" qoʻshing. Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었냐고", otlar uchun "(이)냐고" ishlating.

column1: Remember the four reporting forms together: statements "-다고", orders "-(으)라고", suggestions "-자고", questions "-냐고".
column2: Toʻrtta oʻzlashtirma gap shaklini birga yodlang: darak gap "-다고", buyruq "-(으)라고", taklif "-자고", savol "-냐고".

column1: When you didn't catch it, ask again: "지금 뭐라고 하셨어요?" (What did you just say?)
column2: Eshitmay qolsangiz, qaytadan soʻrang: "지금 뭐라고 하셨어요?" (Hozir nima dedingiz?)

column1: The professor asked where I was sick.
The (shop) owner asked if I had eaten.
My friend asked how life in Korea is.
What did the professor ask you, Sam?
He asked if I would take his class next semester too.
column2: Kelasi semestrda ham uning darsiga yozilasanmi deb soʻradi.

column1: I said I really want to take it.
These are short forms of reported speech. In speaking, these short forms are used much more.
column2: Bular oʻzlashtirma gapning qisqa shakllari. Ogʻzaki nutqda bu qisqa shakllar ancha koʻp ishlatiladi.

column1: -대요 is short for "-다고 해요", and "-(으)래요" is short for "-(으)라고 해요".
column2: -대요 — "-다고 해요" ning qisqasi, "-(으)래요" esa "-(으)라고 해요" ning qisqasi.

column1: It feels like English "I heard…, They say…", passing on what you heard.
column2: Bu oʻzbek tilidagi "…emish, …ekan, deyishyapti" kabi eshitgan narsangizni yetkazadi.

column1: -(으)ㄹ래요 (your own wish) and "-(으)래요" (passing on an order) are different: "갈래요" (I'll go), "가래요" (He says to go).
column2: -(으)ㄹ래요 (oʻz xohishingiz) va "-(으)래요" (buyruqni yetkazish) farq qiladi: "갈래요" (Men boraman), "가래요" (U borishingni aytyapti).

column1: For the past, use "-았/었대요": "어제 조별 모임을 했대요." (I heard they had a group meeting yesterday.)
column2: Oʻtgan zamon uchun "-았/었대요" ishlating: "어제 조별 모임을 했대요." (Kecha guruh yigʻilishi boʻlibdi.)

column1: They say it will rain tomorrow.
The professor says to come quickly.
I heard Aisha is sick today.
Yes, I heard there is. They say there's a make-up class.
column2: Ha, bor ekan. Qoʻshimcha dars boʻlarmish.

column1: Until what time did they say it goes?
They said to stay in the classroom until six.
Added to adjectives to show something gradually changes that way. It is like "get…, become…" (get colder) in English.
column2: Sifatlarga qoʻshilib, biror narsa asta-sekin shunday oʻzgarishini koʻrsatadi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…lashmoq, …roq boʻlmoq" (sovuqlashmoq) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Adjective + -아/어지다 means it changes to that.
Take "요" off the adjective's "-아요/어요" form and add "져요". For something already changed, use "-아/어졌어요".
column2: Sifatning "-아요/어요" shaklidan "요" ni olib, "져요" qoʻshing. Allaqachon oʻzgargan narsa uchun "-아/어졌어요" ishlating.

column1: English uses "get, become" (get colder, get fewer), and Korean uses "-아/어지다" for both: "get colder" = "추워지다", "get fewer" = "적어지다".
column2: Oʻzbekchada "sovuqlashmoq", "kamaymoq" kabi turli shakllar ishlatiladi, koreyschada esa ikkalasi uchun ham "-아/어지다": "sovuqlashmoq" = "추워지다", "kamaymoq" = "적어지다".

column1: It is added only to adjectives. For change with verbs, use "-게 되다".
column2: U faqat sifatlarga qoʻshiladi. Feʼllardagi oʻzgarish uchun "-게 되다" ishlating.

column1: Your Korean skills have gotten much better.
There have been more assignments lately.
I took medicine and got better.
Is your cold a bit better?
Yes, I took medicine and it got much better.
column2: Ha, dori ichib, ancha yaxshi boʻldim.

column1: The weather suddenly got colder these days, didn't it?
column2: Keyingi kunlarda havo birdan sovuqlashib ketdi-a?

column1: Yes, so more people have caught colds.
Means things turned out that way, not by your own choice. It is like "came to…, ended up…, got to…" in English.
column2: Oʻz tanlovingiz bilan emas, ishlar shunday boʻlib chiqqanini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…adigan boʻldim, …ib qoldim" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Verb + -게 됐어요 means things came to be that way.
column2: Feʼl + -게 됐어요 ishlar shunday boʻlib chiqqanini bildiradi.

column1: Take "-다" off the verb and add "-게 됐어요". It does not depend on 받침.
column2: Feʼldan "-다" ni olib, "-게 됐어요" qoʻshing. 받침 ga bogʻliq emas.

column1: It is used to humbly announce something that has been decided: "다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." (I will be going back home next month.) It is common in farewell speeches.
column2: U qaror qilingan narsani kamtarlik bilan eʼlon qilish uchun ishlatiladi: "다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." (Kelasi oy vatanimga qaytadigan boʻldim.) Xayrlashuv nutqlarida keng tarqalgan.

column1: I came to study in Korea.
I got to know Aisha at school.
At first I couldn't eat kimchi, but now I've come to like it.
column2: Avvaliga kimchi yeya olmasdim, lekin endi yaxshi koʻrib qoldim.

column1: From next month, I will be living in the dormitory.
column2: Kelasi oydan boshlab yotoqxonada yashaydigan boʻldim.

column1: I came to know, I found out
I got to go, I ended up going
It turned out I can't go
Sam, how did you come to Korea?
I was accepted to Jeonju University, so I came.
column2: Chonju universitetiga qabul qilindim, shuning uchun keldim.

column1: How did you come to learn Korean?
I watched Korean dramas and came to like it.
column2: Koreys seriallarini koʻrib, yaxshi koʻrib qoldim.

column1: Means you do something and leave the result as it is. Used when preparing something in advance. It is like "leave it (open), do it in advance" in English.
column2: Biror narsani qilib, natijasini oʻsha holatda qoldirishni bildiradi. Biror narsani oldindan tayyorlaganda ishlatiladi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "…ib qoʻymoq" (ochib qoʻymoq) ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Verb + -아/어 놓다 means "leave it…, do it in advance".
Take "요" off the verb's "-아요/어요" form and add "놓다". "-아/어 두다" means the same.
column2: Feʼlning "-아요/어요" shaklidan "요" ni olib, "놓다" qoʻshing. "-아/어 두다" ham shu maʼnoni bildiradi.

column1: It is used much like English "leave… open, have… ready": "leave it open" = "열어 놓다".
column2: U oʻzbek tilidagi "…ib qoʻymoq" ga juda oʻxshash ishlatiladi: "ochib qoʻymoq" = "열어 놓다".

column1: In speech, "놓아" is shortened to "놔": "열어 놔요", "해 놨어요".
column2: Ogʻzaki nutqda "놓아" "놔" ga qisqaradi: "열어 놔요", "해 놨어요".

column1: You often hear it in instructions: "미리 해 놓으세요" (Do it in advance), "여기에 놓아 두세요" (Leave it here).
column2: Buni koʻrsatmalarda tez-tez eshitasiz: "미리 해 놓으세요" (Oldindan qilib qoʻying), "여기에 놓아 두세요" (Shu yerga qoʻyib qoʻying).

column1: I have the materials for tomorrow's presentation ready.
Don't leave the computer on and walk away.
Sam, did you get the chairs ready for tomorrow morning?
Yes, I stacked them in front of the lecture room.
column2: Ha, ularni maʼruza xonasi oldiga taxlab qoʻydim.

column1: Well done. When you leave, close the windows.
Means that after something is done, the state stays. It is like "is open, is sitting" in English.
column2: Biror narsa qilingandan keyin holat saqlanib qolishini bildiradi. Oʻzbek tilidagi "ochiq turibdi, oʻtiribdi" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: -아/어 있다 shows that the state after an action stays.
column2: -아/어 있다 harakatdan keyingi holat saqlanib turganini koʻrsatadi.

column1: Take "요" off the verb's "-아요/어요" form and add "있어요". It is used with verbs like "열리다, 닫히다, 켜지다, 꺼지다, 앉다, 서다, 걸리다, 놓이다, 쓰이다".
column2: Feʼlning "-아요/어요" shaklidan "요" ni olib, "있어요" qoʻshing. U "열리다, 닫히다, 켜지다, 꺼지다, 앉다, 서다, 걸리다, 놓이다, 쓰이다" kabi feʼllar bilan ishlatiladi.

column1: -고 있다 is an action in progress; "-아/어 있다" is the state after it is done: "문을 열고 있어요" (I'm opening the door), "문이 열려 있어요" (The door is open).
column2: -고 있다 — davom etayotgan harakat; "-아/어 있다" — u tugagandan keyingi holat: "문을 열고 있어요" (Eshikni ochyapman), "문이 열려 있어요" (Eshik ochiq turibdi).

column1: What someone did and left is "-아/어 놓다" (a person is the subject); the result is "-아/어 있다" (a thing is the subject): "문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요." (I left the door open. The door is open.)
column2: Kimdir qilib qoldirgan narsa "-아/어 놓다" (ega — odam); natija esa "-아/어 있다" (ega — narsa): "문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요." (Eshikni ochib qoʻydim. Eshik ochiq turibdi.)

column1: The professor is sitting over there.
Sam, did you check before leaving?
Yes, all the computers are off.
to go off, be turned off
One was open, so I closed it.
When a word's stem ends in "ㅡ", the "ㅡ" drops when "-아/어" is added.
column2: Soʻz oʻzagi "ㅡ" bilan tugasa, "-아/어" qoʻshilganda "ㅡ" tushib qoladi.

column1: A stem ending in "ㅡ" drops "ㅡ" before "-아/어".
column2: ㅡ bilan tugaydigan oʻzak "-아/어" dan oldin "ㅡ" ni tushirib qoldiradi.

column1: Drop "ㅡ". If the vowel of the syllable before it is ㅏ or ㅗ, add "-아요"; otherwise, or if there is no syllable before it, add "-어요": 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요, 쓰다 → 써요.
column2: ㅡ ni tushiring. Undan oldingi boʻgʻin unlisi ㅏ yoki ㅗ boʻlsa "-아요", aks holda yoki oldingi boʻgʻin boʻlmasa "-어요" qoʻshing: 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요, 쓰다 → 써요.

column1: It changes only before endings that start with "-아/어". It does not change before "-고, -지만, -습니다, -(으)면": 바쁘고, 바쁩니다, 바쁘면.
column2: U faqat "-아/어" bilan boshlanadigan qoʻshimchalardan oldin oʻzgaradi. "-고, -지만, -습니다, -(으)면" dan oldin oʻzgarmaydi: 바쁘고, 바쁩니다, 바쁘면.

column1: The past is the same: 바빴어요, 아팠어요, 썼어요, 컸어요.
column2: Oʻtgan zamon ham xuddi shunday: 바빴어요, 아팠어요, 썼어요, 컸어요.

column1: This rule has no exceptions, so it is called "탈락" (dropping), not "irregular".
column2: Bu qoidaning istisnolari yoʻq, shuning uchun u "notoʻgʻri" emas, "탈락" (tushib qolish) deb ataladi.

column1: I had a headache, so I took medicine.
column2: Boshim ogʻridi, shuning uchun dori ichdim.

column1: Sam, are you busy these days?
Yes, very busy. Yesterday my back hurt too.
column2: Ha, juda band. Kecha belim ham ogʻridi.

column1: When a word's stem ends in a ㄹ 받침, the ㄹ drops before endings that start with ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.
column2: Soʻz oʻzagi ㄹ 받침 bilan tugasa, ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ bilan boshlanadigan qoʻshimchalardan oldin ㄹ tushib qoladi.

column1: A ㄹ 받침 drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.
column2: ㄹ 받침 ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ dan oldin tushib qoladi.

column1: 살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다, 살다 + -세요 → 사세요, 살다 + -는 → 사는, 살다 + -니까 → 사니까. With "-(으)" endings, do not add "으" (살면, 살러, 살려고).
column2: 살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다, 살다 + -세요 → 사세요, 살다 + -는 → 사는, 살다 + -니까 → 사니까. "-(으)" qoʻshimchalarida "으" qoʻshilmaydi (살면, 살러, 살려고).

column1: It does not drop before "-아요/어요, -고, -지만": 살아요, 살고, 살지만.
column2: -아요/어요, -고, -지만 dan oldin tushmaydi: 살아요, 살고, 살지만.

column1: With "-(으)ㄹ" endings, only one ㄹ remains: 살 거예요, 만들 수 있어요, 알 때.
column2: -(으)ㄹ qoʻshimchalarida faqat bitta ㄹ qoladi: 살 거예요, 만들 수 있어요, 알 때.

column1: Common words with a ㄹ 받침: 살다, 알다, 만들다, 열다, 팔다, 놀다, 울다, 들다, 걸다, 멀다, 길다, 힘들다.
column2: ㄹ 받침 li keng tarqalgan soʻzlar: 살다, 알다, 만들다, 열다, 팔다, 놀다, 울다, 들다, 걸다, 멀다, 길다, 힘들다.

column1: I don't know a single person.
If you open the door, it gets cold.
Do you know anyone in Korea?
Yes, my older cousin lives in Jeonju.
Many adjectives whose stem ends in a ㅂ 받침 change ㅂ to "우" before a vowel.
column2: Oʻzagi ㅂ 받침 bilan tugaydigan koʻp sifatlarda unli tovushdan oldin ㅂ "우" ga aylanadi.

column1: In ㅂ irregular words, ㅂ changes to "우" before a vowel.
column2: ㅂ notoʻgʻri soʻzlarida unli tovushdan oldin ㅂ "우" ga aylanadi.

column1: 덥다 + -어요 → 더워요, 덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면, 덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운, 덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까. Only "돕다, 곱다" become "도와요, 고와요".
column2: 덥다 + -어요 → 더워요, 덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면, 덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운, 덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까. Faqat "돕다, 곱다" "도와요, 고와요" boʻladi.

column1: It does not change before endings that start with a consonant: 덥고, 덥지만, 덥습니다.
column2: Undosh bilan boshlanadigan qoʻshimchalardan oldin oʻzgarmaydi: 덥고, 덥지만, 덥습니다.

column1: Most things use "개", paper "장", books "권", computers and cars "대", clothes "벌", shoes "켤레".
column2: Koʻp narsalar uchun "개", qogʻoz uchun "장", kitob uchun "권", kompyuter va mashina uchun "대", kiyim uchun "벌", oyoq kiyim uchun "켤레".

column1: The order is different from English: "noun + number + counter". 3 apples = 사과 세 개.
column2: Tartib oʻzbekchadan farq qiladi: "ot + son + hisob soʻzi". 3 ta olma = 사과 세 개.

column1: For numbers use "하나, 둘, 셋"; before a counter they change to "한, 두, 세, 네". 스물 becomes "스무" (스무 개).
column2: Sonlar uchun "하나, 둘, 셋" ishlating; hisob soʻzidan oldin ular "한, 두, 세, 네" ga aylanadi. 스물 "스무" boʻladi (스무 개).

column1: If you don't know which counter to use, use "개". It works in most cases.
column2: Qaysi hisob soʻzini ishlatishni bilmasangiz, "개" ni ishlating. U koʻp hollarda toʻgʻri keladi.

column1: Korean also adds counting words for people and animals. The order is different from English, and the way of saying numbers is different too.
column2: Koreyschada odamlar va hayvonlar uchun ham hisob soʻzlari qoʻshiladi. Tartibi oʻzbekchadan farq qiladi, sonlarning aytilishi ham boshqacha.

column1: People use "명", "분" when polite, animals "마리", and numbers are "한, 두, 세, 네".
column2: Odamlar uchun "명", hurmat bilan "분", hayvonlar uchun "마리" ishlatiladi, sonlar esa "한, 두, 세, 네".

column1: The order is different from English: "noun + number + counter".
column2: Tartib oʻzbekchadan farq qiladi: "ot + son + hisob soʻzi".

column1: Count with "하나, 둘, 셋", not "일, 이, 삼", and the form changes before a counter: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네.
column2: 일, 이, 삼 bilan emas, "하나, 둘, 셋" bilan sanang, hisob soʻzidan oldin esa shakl oʻzgaradi: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네.

column1: Three people share our dorm room.
How many people are in your party?
Five guests are coming to our department today.
column2: Bugun kafedramizga besh nafar mehmon keladi.

column1: Come in one at a time.
Two people have to do this assignment together.
column2: Bu topshiriqni ikki kishi birga bajarishi kerak.

column1: There are fifty monkeys at the zoo.
Four. One more will come a little later.
column2: Toʻrt kishi. Yana bittasi biroz keyinroq keladi.

column1: Then five in total. Please come this way.
column2: Unda jami besh kishi. Marhamat, bu yoqqa keling.

column1: Is a whole chicken in samgyetang?
Yes, a whole chicken goes in.
Food and drinks are counted by the container they are in, like English "a glass of, a cup of, a bowl of, a plate of".
column2: Oziq-ovqat va ichimliklar oʻzbekchadagi "bir stakan, bir piyola, bir kosa, bir likopcha" kabi solingan idishiga qarab sanaladi.

column1: Things in bottles are counted with "병", in cups "잔", rice and soup "그릇", and meat "인분".
column2: Shishadagi narsalar "병", stakandagilar "잔", guruch va shoʻrva "그릇", goʻsht esa "인분" bilan sanaladi.

column1: Only "인분" is counted with "일, 이, 삼": 일 인분, 이 인분, 삼 인분. Others use "한, 두, 세".
column2: Faqat "인분" "일, 이, 삼" bilan sanaladi: 일 인분, 이 인분, 삼 인분. Boshqalari "한, 두, 세" ishlatadi.

column1: 한잔하다 means to go for a drink (alcohol): "오늘 한잔할까요?" (Shall we have a drink today?)
column2: 한잔하다 ichishga (spirtli ichimlik) bormoq degani: "오늘 한잔할까요?" (Bugun bir-ikki qadah ichamizmi?)

column1: At Korean BBQ restaurants, you usually have to order at least two servings.
column2: Koreyscha BBQ restoranlarida odatda kamida ikki porsiya buyurtma qilish kerak.

column1: Two more bottles of beer, please.
I'll drink just one bottle of soju and go home.
column2: Faqat bir shisha soju ichib, uyga ketaman.
