column2: Kuniga faqat ikki piyola kofe ichaman.

column1: Please add one more bowl of rice.
column2: Yana bir kosa guruch qoʻshib bering.

column1: There are four of us, so let's order four servings of meat.
column2: Toʻrt kishimiz, shuning uchun toʻrt porsiya goʻsht buyurtma qilaylik.

column1: One more plate of kimchi, please.
How much is a plate of dumplings?
Please wrap up a plate of dumplings to go.
column2: Bir likopcha chuchvarani olib ketishga oʻrab bering.

column1: I ate two slices of pizza.
Two servings of bulgogi and two bowls of rice, please.
column2: Ikki porsiya bulgogi va ikki kosa guruch bering.

column1: One bottle of cola and two glasses of water, please.
column2: Bir shisha kola va ikki stakan suv bering.

column1: These are words for counting things by package, not one by one. They are used in supermarkets, convenience stores and shops.
column2: Bular narsalarni bittalab emas, qadoq boʻyicha sanash uchun soʻzlar. Supermarket, doʻkoncha va doʻkonlarda ishlatiladi.

column1: Packages are counted with "상자, 봉지, 묶음, 통", and "씩" means "each, per".
column2: Qadoqlar "상자, 봉지, 묶음, 통" bilan sanaladi, "씩" esa "…tadan, har biriga" degani.

column1: 씩 means "each, per": "열 개씩" (ten at a time), "한 사람씩" (one person at a time). You often hear it in class too: "두 명씩 앉으세요." (Sit in twos.)
column2: 씩 "…tadan, har biriga" degani: "열 개씩" (oʻntadan), "한 사람씩" (bittadan odam). Buni darsda ham tez-tez eshitasiz: "두 명씩 앉으세요." (Ikki kishidan oʻtiring.)

column1: A tray of eggs is 30 eggs.
Pattern for dividing things: "(number) 개씩 한 (봉지/상자)에 넣으세요."
column2: Narsalarni boʻlish uchun qolip: "(son) 개씩 한 (봉지/상자)에 넣으세요."

column1: I bought a box of ramyeon.
When I moved, I packed five boxes of things.
How many go in one box?
I bought two bags of snacks.
Put the trash in a bag.
Garbage bags are sold at convenience stores.
Tie them in bundles of ten.
A bunch of green onions, please.
These ballpoint pens come in bundles of 10.
column2: Bu sharikli ruchkalar 10 tadan bogʻlamda keladi.

column1: I ate a roll of gimbap for lunch.
I ordered a tray of tofu.
A tray of eggs lasts me a week.
column2: Bir lotok tuxum menga bir haftaga yetadi.

column1: I bought two tubs of ice cream.
I got a tub of kimchi.
Please bring one more container of water.
column2: Yana bir idish suv olib keling.

column1: Put five of these snacks in each bag.
column2: Har bir paketga bu pechenyelardan beshtadan soling.

column1: Okay. How many bags do we need to make in total?
column2: Xoʻp. Jami nechta paket tayyorlashimiz kerak?

column1: Fifty bags. Put ten bags in each box.
column2: Ellikta paket. Har bir qutiga oʻntadan paket soling.

column1: These are units for length, weight and volume, and words for counting times and order. Korea uses the international (metric) units used in most countries.
column2: Bular uzunlik, ogʻirlik va hajm oʻlchov birliklari hamda marta va tartibni sanash soʻzlari. Koreyada koʻp mamlakatlarda ishlatiladigan xalqaro (metrik) birliklar qoʻllanadi.

column1: Measuring units are read with "일, 이, 삼"; "번" for times is read with "한, 두, 세".
column2: Oʻlchov birliklari "일, 이, 삼" bilan oʻqiladi; marta maʼnosidagi "번" esa "한, 두, 세" bilan oʻqiladi.

column1: Measuring units (미터, 킬로그램, 리터) are read with "일, 이, 삼", and "번" for times is read with "한, 두, 세".
column2: Oʻlchov birliklari (미터, 킬로그램, 리터) "일, 이, 삼" bilan, marta maʼnosidagi "번" esa "한, 두, 세" bilan oʻqiladi.

column1: 번 has two uses: "세 번" (three times) and "삼 번" (number 3): "삼 번 버스를 세 번 탔어요." (I took bus number 3 three times.)
column2: 번 ikki xil ishlatiladi: "세 번" (uch marta) va "삼 번" (3-raqam): "삼 번 버스를 세 번 탔어요." (3-avtobusga uch marta oʻtirdim.)

column1: It's 300 meters from the dorm to the library.

column2: Samolyotda topshiriladigan yuk 23 kilogrammgacha boʻlishi mumkin.

The second room on the right is my room.
column2: Oʻng tomondagi ikkinchi xona — mening xonam.

Twenty. Check the length twice for each.
column2: Yigirmata. Har birining uzunligini ikki marta tekshiring.

column1: Before a counter, the form of the number changes. English doesn't have this rule, so you need to practice it.
column2: Hisob soʻzidan oldin sonning shakli oʻzgaradi. Oʻzbek tilida bunday qoida yoʻq, shuning uchun uni mashq qilish kerak.

column1: Before a counter, 하나·둘·셋·넷·스물 become 한·두·세·네·스무.
column2: Hisob soʻzidan oldin 하나·둘·셋·넷·스물 한·두·세·네·스무 ga aylanadi.

column1: Only five numbers change: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 스물. The last part also changes, like 열하나 → 열한 개, 스물둘 → 스물두 명.
column2: Faqat beshta son oʻzgaradi: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷, 스물. Oxirgi qism ham oʻzgaradi: 열하나 → 열한 개, 스물둘 → 스물두 명.

column1: When you say only the number without a counter, use "하나, 둘": "몇 개 드릴까요?" "하나 주세요."
column2: Hisob soʻzisiz faqat sonni aytganda "하나, 둘" ishlating: "몇 개 드릴까요?" "하나 주세요."

column1: From 100, people usually use the "일, 이, 삼" numbers: "백 개, 이백 명".

to be in, to be contained

Korean has two sets of numbers. To tell the time, "시" (hour) is read with "한, 두, 세" and "분" (minute) with "일, 이, 삼".
column2: Koreyschada ikki xil sonlar tizimi bor. Vaqtni aytganda "시" (soat) "한, 두, 세" bilan, "분" (daqiqa) esa "일, 이, 삼" bilan oʻqiladi.

column1: 시 is read with 한·두·세, and "분" with 일·이·삼.
column2: 시 한·두·세 bilan, "분" esa 일·이·삼 bilan oʻqiladi.

column1: You mix the two number sets in one phrase, like "세 시 삼 분". Saying "삼 시" or "세 분" is wrong.
column2: 세 시 삼 분 kabi bitta iborada ikki sonlar tizimi aralashadi. "삼 시" yoki "세 분" deyish xato.

column1: 시 (o'clock, a point in time) and "시간" (hours, length of time) are different: "세 시에 만나요", "세 시간 공부했어요".
column2: 시 (soat, vaqt nuqtasi) va "시간" (soat, vaqt davomiyligi) farq qiladi: "세 시에 만나요", "세 시간 공부했어요".

column2: Tanaffus uchga oʻn daqiqa qolganda tugaydi.

Age is said with "살" or "세", and dates are read with "일, 이, 삼".

column1: Dates go in the order "year → month → day", which is different from English (13 November 2026 / November 13, 2026): 2026년 11월 13일.

Money and phone numbers are read with "일, 이, 삼". Unlike English, big numbers are split into units of "만" (ten thousand).
column2: Pul va telefon raqamlari "일, 이, 삼" bilan oʻqiladi. Oʻzbekchadan farqli ravishda, katta sonlar "만" (oʻn ming) birligiga boʻlinadi.

column1: Money is read in units of "만", and 0 in phone numbers is "공".
column2: Pul "만" birligida oʻqiladi, telefon raqamlaridagi 0 esa "공".

column1: Korean splits numbers every four digits (만, 억). English has "hundred thousand, million", and Korean says "십만, 백만": 백만 = one million, 십만 = one hundred thousand.
column2: Koreyschada sonlar har toʻrt raqamda boʻlinadi (만, 억). Oʻzbekchada "yuz ming, million" deyiladi, koreyschada esa "십만, 백만": 백만 = bir million, 십만 = yuz ming.

column2: 하루, 이틀, 사흘, 나흘 — kunlarni sanash uchun sof koreyscha soʻzlar. 나흘 (4 kun) dan boshlab "사 일, 오 일" koʻproq ishlatiladi.

English "older brother, older sister" becomes different words in Korean depending on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi "aka, opa" koreyschada soʻzlovchi erkak yoki ayol ekaniga qarab boshqa-boshqa soʻz boʻladi.

column1: Men say "형, 누나"; women say "오빠, 언니".
Unlike English, Korean uses "형, 오빠, 누나, 언니" for close older people who are not family. At school, too, people call close seniors "형" or "언니".
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi kabi, koreyschada ham "형, 오빠, 누나, 언니" oiladan boʻlmagan yaqin katta odamlarga ishlatiladi. Universitetda ham yaqin katta kursdoshlarni "형" yoki "언니" deb chaqirishadi.

column1: 아빠, 엄마 are used by children or between close people. When talking to others, "아버지, 어머니" sounds more polite.
column2: 아빠, 엄마 bolalar yoki yaqin odamlar orasida ishlatiladi. Boshqalarga gapirganda "아버지, 어머니" muloyimroq eshitiladi.

column1: Call younger siblings by name. Don't call "동생!". Add "아/야" after the name: "민하야", "샘아".

I send money for my younger sibling's school fees.
column2: Ukamning maktab toʻlovi uchun pul joʻnataman.

At Korean universities, people call each other by titles like "교수님" and "선배님" more than by name. This is different from English, where people often use first names.
column2: Koreys universitetlarida bir-biriga ismdan koʻra "교수님", "선배님" kabi unvonlar bilan koʻproq murojaat qilinadi.

column2: Yoshi yoki mavqei katta kishini "ism + 씨" deb chaqirish juda qoʻpollik. "임 씨" yoki "현정 씨" demang; "임 교수님" yoki "교수님" deng.

column1: In Korean names, the family name comes first. In "김민하", "김" is the family name and "민하" is the given name. Job titles go after the family name.
column2: Koreys ismlarida familiya birinchi keladi. "김민하" da "김" — familiya, "민하" — ism. Lavozim familiyadan keyin keladi.

column2: Bular notanish odamlarni chaqirish soʻzlari. Oʻzbekchadagi "amaki, xola" kabi, koreyschada ham buning uchun qarindoshlik soʻzlari ishlatiladi.

column1: Call strangers "저기요", staff in restaurants "여기요", and shop owners "사장님".
column2: Notanishlarni "저기요", restoran xodimlarini "여기요", doʻkon egalarini "사장님" deb chaqiring.

column1: The safest words are "저기요" and "여기요". You can use them with anyone. To call staff in a restaurant, say "여기요".
column2: Eng xavfsiz soʻzlar "저기요" va "여기요". Ularni har kimga ishlatish mumkin. Restoranda xodimni chaqirish uchun "여기요" deng.

column2: 아줌마 qoʻpol eshitilishi mumkin, shuning uchun "아주머니", "이모님" yoki "사장님" ishlating. Yosh ayollar "아주머니" deb chaqirilishini yoqtirmaydi.

column1: Shop owners, men or women, like being called "사장님".
column2: Doʻkon egalari, erkak boʻlsin, ayol boʻlsin, "사장님" deb chaqirilishini yoqtiradi.

An action a person does (문을 열다) and something that happens by itself (문이 열리다) use different words. English uses "open" for both, but Korean has a pair.
column2: Odam qiladigan harakat (문을 열다) va oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻladigan narsa (문이 열리다) har xil soʻzlar bilan aytiladi. Oʻzbekchadagi "ochmoq — ochilmoq" kabi, koreyschada ham juftlik bor.

column1: If a person does it, "을/를 열다"; if it happens by itself, "이/가 열리다".
column2: Odam qilsa "을/를 열다", oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻlsa "이/가 열리다".

column1: The particle shows the difference. For what a person does, use "을/를"; for what happens by itself, use "이/가": "문을 열어요", "문이 열려요".
column2: Farqni kelishik qoʻshimchasi koʻrsatadi. Odam qiladigan narsa uchun "을/를", oʻz-oʻzidan boʻladigan narsa uchun "이/가" ishlating: "문을 열어요", "문이 열려요".

column1: When you report a problem, use the "by itself" verb: "문이 안 열려요", "컴퓨터가 안 켜져요", "불이 안 꺼져요".
column2: Muammo haqida xabar berganda "oʻz-oʻzidan" feʼlini ishlating: "문이 안 열려요", "컴퓨터가 안 켜져요", "불이 안 꺼져요".

column1: It smells, so please open the window.
to open (by itself), to be opened

to close (by itself), to be closed

Don't put your hand in when the elevator door is closing.
If it's dark, turn on your phone's flashlight.
to turn on (by itself), to come on
When night comes, the streetlights come on.
Turn off the lights when you leave the lecture room.
I turn off the light before I go to sleep.
Be sure to turn off the electric blanket when you go out.
column2: Tashqariga chiqqanda elektr adyolni albatta oʻchiring.

open the door ↔ the door opens
close the door ↔ the door closes
turn on the light ↔ the light comes on
turn off the light ↔ the light goes out
When things break, snap or fall, Korean shows whether someone did it or it happened by itself.
column2: Narsalar sinsa, uzilsa yoki tushib ketsa, koreyschada buni kimdir qilganmi yoki oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻlganmi koʻrsatiladi.

column1: If you did it, "깼어요, 떨어뜨렸어요"; if it happened by itself, "깨졌어요, 떨어졌어요".
column2: Siz qilgan boʻlsangiz "깼어요, 떨어뜨렸어요"; oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻlgan boʻlsa "깨졌어요, 떨어졌어요".

column1: When you report a mistake, say it honestly: "제가 ~을/를 ~했습니다". "제가 컵을 깼습니다. 죄송합니다."
column2: Xatoingiz haqida xabar berganda rostini ayting: "제가 ~을/를 ~했습니다". "제가 컵을 깼습니다. 죄송합니다."

column1: When you don't know who did it, or it happened by itself, say "~이/가 ~졌습니다": "유리가 깨져 있었습니다." (The glass was already broken.)
column2: Kim qilganini bilmasangiz yoki oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻlgan boʻlsa, "~이/가 ~졌습니다" deng: "유리가 깨져 있었습니다." (Shisha allaqachon singan ekan.)

column1: I broke a plate. I'm sorry.
I broke a bowl while washing the dishes.
Wrap broken glass in newspaper and throw it away.
to cut, to hang up, to quit
Since I quit drinking, I'm saving money.
to break, to be cut off
The internet went down, so I can't make the call.
column2: Internet uzilib qoldi, shuning uchun qoʻngʻiroq qila olmayapman.

column1: Words for starting and ending also come in pairs: what a person does and what happens by itself.

column1: If a person does it, "시작하다, 끝내다, 바꾸다"; if it happens by itself, "시작되다, 끝나다, 바뀌다".
column2: Odam qilsa "시작하다, 끝내다, 바꾸다"; oʻz-oʻzidan sodir boʻlsa "시작되다, 끝나다, 바뀌다".

column1: Notices and announcements often use the "by itself" verbs: "수업 시간이 바뀌었습니다", "시험 날짜가 정해졌습니다". They don't say who decided.
column2: Eʼlon va xabarnomalarda koʻpincha "oʻz-oʻzidan" feʼllari ishlatiladi: "수업 시간이 바뀌었습니다", "시험 날짜가 정해졌습니다". Kim qaror qilgani aytilmaydi.

It's like English "go, come", but Korean strictly decides by where the speaker is now. "다니다" means going back and forth regularly.
column2: Bu oʻzbekchadagi "bormoq, kelmoq" ga oʻxshaydi, lekin koreyschada soʻzlovchi hozir qayerdaligiga qarab qatʼiy tanlanadi. "다니다" muntazam borib-kelib yurishni bildiradi.

column1: Moving away is "가다", coming closer is "오다", and going back and forth regularly is "다니다".
When you go to someone who is calling you, Korean says "가요": "샘 씨, 이리 와요!" "네, 지금 가요." Don't say "와요" like English "I'm coming!"
column2: Sizni chaqirayotgan odamning oldiga borayotganda koreyschada "가요" deyiladi: "샘 씨, 이리 와요!" "네, 지금 가요." Oʻzbekchadagi "Hozir boraman!" bilan bir xil. "와요" demang.

column1: About your school, "전주대학교에 다녀요" means you are a student there. "학교에 가요" means you are on your way there now.
column2: Universitetingiz haqida "전주대학교에 다녀요" desangiz, u yerda oʻqishingizni bildiradi. "학교에 가요" esa hozir u yerga ketayotganingizni bildiradi.

These are English "give" and "receive". If the receiver is someone above you, use "드리다" instead of "주다".

column2: Men bersam "주다". Mendan yuqori kishiga bersam "드리다". Men olsam "받다".

column1: Like English "do something for someone", Korean adds "give" after a verb: "-아/어 주다", "-아/어 드리다": "도와줘요", "도와드릴게요".
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi "…ib bermoq" kabi, koreyschada ham feʼldan keyin "bermoq" qoʻshiladi: "-아/어 주다", "-아/어 드리다": "도와줘요", "도와드릴게요".

column1: The giver is shown with "한테서, 에게서" (for an organization, "에서"): "학교에서 장학금을 받아요", "친구한테서 선물을 받았어요".
column2: Beruvchi "한테서, 에게서" bilan koʻrsatiladi (tashkilot uchun "에서"): "학교에서 장학금을 받아요", "친구한테서 선물을 받았어요".

column1: When you give something to or receive something from someone above you, use both hands.
column2: Sizdan yuqori kishiga biror narsa berganda yoki undan olganda ikki qoʻllab oling/bering.

Korean separates English "know" and "understand". "모르다" is a separate word that means the opposite of "알다".
column2: Koreyschada "bilmoq" va "tushunmoq" ajratiladi. "모르다" — "알다" ning teskarisini bildiradigan alohida soʻz.

column2: 알다 ning teskarisi "모르다", koʻrsatmalarga esa "알겠습니다" deb javob beriladi.

column1: When you answer an instruction, say "알겠습니다", not "알아요". "알아요" sounds like "I already know", so it's rude.
column2: Koʻrsatmaga javob berganda "알아요" emas, "알겠습니다" deng. "알아요" "Men allaqachon bilaman" kabi eshitiladi, shuning uchun qoʻpol.

column1: In "알다", the ㄹ sometimes drops: 압니다, 아세요, 아는 사람. "모르다" changes to "몰라요, 몰랐어요".
column2: 알다 da baʼzan ㄹ tushib qoladi: 압니다, 아세요, 아는 사람. "모르다" esa "몰라요, 몰랐어요" ga oʻzgaradi.

column1: 보다 has many other meanings too: 시험을 보다 (to take an exam), 장을 보다 (to shop for groceries), 면접을 보다 (to have an interview), 아이를 보다 (to look after a child).

column1: English "have" and "be (somewhere)" are both "있다" in Korean. You can tell the meaning by the particle in front.
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi "bor" kabi, koreyschadagi "있다" ham "ega boʻlmoq" va "(biror joyda) boʻlmoq" maʼnolarini bildiradi. Maʼnosini oldidagi kelishik qoʻshimchasidan bilish mumkin.

column1: 이/가 있다 is "have", "에 있다" is "be (somewhere)", and the opposite of both is "없다".
column2: 이/가 있다 — "…i bor (ega)", "에 있다" — "…da bor (joylashgan)", ikkalasining teskarisi "없다".

column1: Look at the particle to know the meaning. "이/가 있다" is "have", and "에 있다" is "be (somewhere)".
column2: Maʼnoni bilish uchun kelishik qoʻshimchasiga qarang. "이/가 있다" — "…i bor (ega)", "에 있다" esa "…da bor (joylashgan)".

column2: Ikkala maʼno uchun ham teskarisi "없다" (yoʻq). "안 있다" demang.

column1: The honorific form splits into two: "be (somewhere)" is "계시다", and "have" is "있으시다".

Listening on purpose is "듣다" (to listen), and sound coming into your ears by itself is "들리다" (to hear). "듣다" and "묻다" change to "들어요, 물어요", so they are easy to confuse.
column2: Ataylab tinglash "듣다" (tinglamoq), tovush quloqqa oʻz-oʻzidan kelishi esa "들리다" (eshitilmoq). "듣다" va "묻다" "들어요, 물어요" ga oʻzgaradi, shuning uchun ularni adashtirish oson.

column1: Listening on purpose is "듣다", hearing by itself is "들리다", and asking about what you don't know is "묻다".
column2: Ataylab tinglash "듣다", oʻz-oʻzidan eshitilish "들리다", bilmagan narsangizni soʻrash esa "묻다".

column1: In "듣다, 묻다, 걷다", ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel: 들어요, 물어요, 걸어요. But "듣고, 묻고, 걷고" stay the same.
column2: 듣다, 묻다, 걷다 da unli tovushdan oldin ㄷ ㄹ ga aylanadi: 들어요, 물어요, 걸어요. Lekin "듣고, 묻고, 걷고" oʻzgarmaydi.

This separates English "put, leave, put in". Putting on top is "놓다", leaving something where it is is "두다", and putting inside is "넣다".
column2: Bu "qoʻymoq, qoldirmoq, solmoq" ni ajratadi. Ustiga qoʻyish — "놓다", biror narsani joyida qoldirish — "두다", ichiga solish — "넣다".

column1: Tell "자주" (often) and "자꾸" (again and again, for bad things) apart: "자꾸 잊어버려요."
column2: 자주 (tez-tez) va "자꾸" (qayta-qayta, yomon narsalar uchun) ni farqlang: "자꾸 잊어버려요."

column1: Always carry your residence card with you.
column2: Chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangizni (ID karta) doim yoningizda olib yuring.

column2: ega boʻlmoq, olib kelmoq (가지고 오다 = olib kelmoq)

market (장을 보다 = to go grocery shopping)

I don't know Korean at all.
At first, I couldn't speak Korean at all.
can't do, to be bad at

column2: Har kuni ertalab sport bilan shugʻullanaman.

column2: Har kuni ertalab choʻzilish mashqlarini qilib, keyin ishni boshlaymiz.

column1: Sam, what do you usually do on weekends?
column2: Sam, dam olish kunlari odatda nima qilasiz?

column1: I usually rest in the dormitory. Sometimes I play soccer with my friends.
column2: Odatda yotoqxonada dam olaman. Baʼzan doʻstlarim bilan futbol oʻynayman.

column1: How to tell "already" and "yet / still" apart. If it is sooner than you thought, use "벌써"; if it is already finished, "이미"; if it isn't finished, "아직".
column2: Allaqachon va "hali" ni qanday farqlash mumkin. Oʻylaganingizdan tezroq boʻlsa "벌써", allaqachon tugagan boʻlsa "이미", tugamagan boʻlsa "아직" ishlating.

column1: If it's fast, "벌써"; if it's finished, "이미"; if it's not finished, "아직".
column2: Tez boʻlsa "벌써", tugagan boʻlsa "이미", tugamagan boʻlsa "아직".

column1: To answer "Not yet" to "다 했어요?", say "아직이요" or "아직 안 했어요".
column2: 다 했어요? ga "Hali yoʻq" deb javob berish uchun "아직이요" yoki "아직 안 했어요" deng.

column1: 아직 안 했어요 means "I haven't done it yet," and "아직 안 해요" is closer to "I'm not doing it." Usually use "-았/었-".
column2: 아직 안 했어요 "Hali qilmadim" degani, "아직 안 해요" esa "Qilmayapman" ga yaqinroq. Odatda "-았/었-" ishlating.

column1: The application period has already ended.
There's still a long way to go.
My scholarship hasn't come in yet.
Do you still work part-time at that cafe?
column2: Hali ham oʻsha kafeda qoʻshimcha ish qilasizmi?

column1: Now I'm used to taking the subway.
Sam, have you finished the presentation slides?
I'm not done yet. Please give me just ten more minutes.
column2: Hali tugatmadim. Yana oʻn daqiqa vaqt bering.

column1: Words for a time close to now. They show whether it was a moment ago or will be in a moment.
column2: Hozirgi vaqtga yaqin vaqtni bildiradigan soʻzlar. Ular bir lahza oldinmi yoki bir lahzadan keyinmi ekanini koʻrsatadi.

column1: A moment ago is "방금, 아까", a little later is "곧, 이따가", and quickly is "금방".
column2: Bir lahza oldin — "방금, 아까", biroz keyin — "곧, 이따가", tez — "금방".

column1: 이따가 is for later today, and "나중에" is for some later day that isn't fixed.
column2: 이따가 bugunning oʻzida keyinroq, "나중에" esa belgilanmagan keyingi bir kun uchun.

column1: 방금 is used only for the past. "방금 갈게요" is wrong; "금방 갈게요" is right.
column2: 방금 faqat oʻtgan zamon uchun ishlatiladi. "방금 갈게요" xato; "금방 갈게요" toʻgʻri.

column1: When Koreans say "금방", it is quite fast. If you said "금방 갈게요", hurry.
column2: Koreyslar "금방" desa, bu ancha tez degani. "금방 갈게요" degan boʻlsangiz, shoshiling.

column1: I just got a delivery text.
column2: Hozirgina yetkazib berish haqida SMS keldi.

column1: The teaching assistant was looking for you earlier.
Let's talk later during the break.
Let's have a meal together sometime.
I want to save money and open a shop later.
Sam, have you seen Professor Hwang Insu?
He just went to the department office. He'll be back soon.
column2: U hozirgina kafedra idorasiga ketdi. Tez orada qaytadi.

column1: Really? Then I'll come back later.
Like "fast" and "early" in English, Korean has two different words. For fast movement use "빨리"; for an early time use "일찍".
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi "tez" va "erta" kabi, koreyschada ham ikki xil soʻz bor. Tez harakat uchun "빨리", erta vaqt uchun "일찍" ishlating.

column1: For movement use "빨리·천천히", and for time use "일찍·늦게".
The same goes for "slowly" and "late". For slow movement use "천천히"; for a late time use "늦게".
column2: Sekin va "kech" uchun ham xuddi shunday. Sekin harakat uchun "천천히", kech vaqt uchun "늦게" ishlating.

column1: 빨리 일어나세요 means get up quickly right now, and "일찍 일어나세요" means get up at an early time.
column2: 빨리 일어나세요 hozir tez turing degani, "일찍 일어나세요" esa erta vaqtda turing degani.

column1: In Korea you often hear "빨리빨리". But it's better to do assignments slowly and carefully: "천천히 정확하게 하겠습니다."
column2: Koreyada "빨리빨리" ni koʻp eshitasiz. Lekin topshiriqlarni sekin va ehtiyotkorlik bilan bajarish yaxshiroq: "천천히 정확하게 하겠습니다."

column1: Someone is hurt. Please come quickly!
Go to bed early so you won't be tired tomorrow.
It's okay to go slowly, so do it correctly.
column2: Sekin boʻlsa ham mayli, toʻgʻri qiling.

column1: My part-time job finishes late today.
If you come back late from the library, the dormitory cafeteria is closed.
column2: Kutubxonadan kech qaytsangiz, yotoqxona oshxonasi yopiq boʻladi.

column1: If you think you'll be late, email the professor.
column2: Kechikadigan boʻlsangiz, professorga elektron xat yozing.

column1: Deliveries in Korea are really fast.
We'll have a lot of customers tomorrow, so come in thirty minutes early.
column2: Ertaga mijozlar koʻp boʻladi, shuning uchun oʻttiz daqiqa erta keling.

column1: Okay, I'll be here by seven thirty.
column2: Xoʻp, yetti yarimgacha shu yerda boʻlaman.

column1: And put these milk boxes in the fridge quickly. We open soon.
column2: Va bu sut qutilarini tezroq muzlatkichga soling. Tez orada ochamiz.

column1: Both mean "again" in English. "다시" means doing something over from the start, and "또" means the same thing happens one more time.
column2: Oʻzbekchada ular "qaytadan" va "yana" ga toʻgʻri keladi. "다시" biror narsani boshidan qaytadan qilishni, "또" esa xuddi shu narsa yana bir marta sodir boʻlishini bildiradi.

column1: For doing over use "다시", for repeating "또", and for adding "더".
column2: Qaytadan qilish uchun "다시", takrorlash uchun "또", qoʻshish uchun "더" ishlating.

column1: When you didn't understand, say "다시 한번 말씀해 주세요". "또 말해 주세요" sounds unnatural.
column2: Tushunmaganingizda "다시 한번 말씀해 주세요" deng. "또 말해 주세요" gʻayritabiiy eshitiladi.

column1: 또 often comes up when someone is scolding: "또 늦었어요?", "또 틀렸네요."
column2: 또 koʻpincha kimdir urishayotganda ishlatiladi: "또 늦었어요?", "또 틀렸네요."

column1: When you mean adding more, like "more" in English, use "더": "하나 더 주세요."
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi "yana, koʻproq" kabi qoʻshish maʼnosida "더" ishlating: "하나 더 주세요."

column1: Can I have a little more rice, please?
One more glass of water, please.
Please check the account number one more time.
column2: Hisob raqamini yana bir marta tekshiring.

column1: Contact us by phone or text.
Pay in cash or by card.
column2: Naqd pul yoki karta bilan toʻlang.

column1: Please show your passport or residence card.
column2: Pasportingiz yoki chet ellik roʻyxatdan oʻtish kartangizni (ID karta) koʻrsating.

column1: The format of this report is wrong. Write it again.
column2: Bu hisobotning shakli notoʻgʻri. Qaytadan yozing.

column1: You can't get it wrong again. Check it one more time, too.
column2: Yana xato qilish mumkin emas. Yana bir marta tekshiring ham.

column1: All of them mean "all". "다" is the most common in speech, and it also means "completely, to the end".
column2: Ularning hammasi "hammasi, barchasi" degani. "다" ogʻzaki nutqda eng keng tarqalgan va "butunlay, oxirigacha" degan maʼnoni ham bildiradi.

column1: For "to the end" use "다", for all people or things "모두", and for counting a total "전부".
column2: Oxirigacha uchun "다", barcha odamlar yoki narsalar uchun "모두", jamini sanash uchun "전부" ishlating.

column1: 다 했어요? is a question you often hear when doing group assignments. Answer "네, 다 했습니다", "거의 다 했습니다", or "아직 못 했습니다".
column2: 다 했어요? guruh topshiriqlarini bajarganda tez-tez eshitiladigan savol. "네, 다 했습니다", "거의 다 했습니다" yoki "아직 못 했습니다" deb javob bering.

column1: 모두 and "전부" can also be used like nouns: "모두가 알아요", "전부를 주세요". "다" is not used that way.
column2: 모두 va "전부" ot kabi ham ishlatilishi mumkin: "모두가 알아요", "전부를 주세요". "다" bunday ishlatilmaydi.

column1: How many people are there in total?
Everyone, gather near the emergency exit.
column2: Hamma favqulodda chiqish yoʻli yoniga yigʻilsin.

column1: How much is all my shopping in total?
I didn't understand anything in the class.
Yes, everyone is here. There are eight people in total.
column2: Ha, hamma shu yerda. Jami sakkiz kishi.

column1: Is the group assignment all finished?
Almost done. Only the presentation practice is left.
column2: Deyarli tugadi. Faqat taqdimot mashqi qoldi.

column1: Words that link one sentence to another. "그리고" adds something (and, and then), and "그래서" links a reason and a result (so, that's why).
column2: Bir gapni boshqasiga bogʻlaydigan soʻzlar. "그리고" biror narsa qoʻshadi (va, keyin), "그래서" esa sabab va natijani bogʻlaydi (shuning uchun).

column1: Use "그리고" to add something and "그래서" to say a result.
column2: Biror narsa qoʻshish uchun "그리고", natijani aytish uchun "그래서" ishlating.

column1: When you join them into one sentence, "그리고" becomes "-고", and "그래서" becomes "-아서/어서": "비가 와서 안 가요."
column2: Ularni bitta gapga birlashtirganda "그리고" "-고" ga, "그래서" esa "-아서/어서" ga aylanadi: "비가 와서 안 가요."

column1: To join two words, use "하고" rather than "그리고": "빵하고 우유".
column2: Ikki soʻzni bogʻlash uchun "그리고" emas, "하고" ishlating: "빵하고 우유".

column1: I'm Sam. And this is Aisha.
I ate. And then I had coffee.
I bought rice at the supermarket. And I bought chili peppers too.
column2: Supermarketdan guruch sotib oldim. Va qalampir ham oldim.

column1: I was sick yesterday. So I couldn't go to school.
column2: Kecha kasal edim. Shuning uchun universitetga bora olmadim.

column1: It rained. So I stayed home.
column2: Yomgʻir yogʻdi. Shuning uchun uyda qoldim.

column1: I missed the bus. So I took a taxi.
column2: Avtobusdan qolib ketdim. Shuning uchun taksiga oʻtirdim.

column1: Turn off the power. After that, clean it.
Wash your hands. Then let's eat.
First take a number ticket. Then wait.
column2: Avval navbat chiptasini oling. Keyin kuting.

column1: And then? What did the professor say?
And then? Did you go to the hospital?
I did my homework. After that, I went to bed.
column2: Uy vazifamni qildim. Shundan keyin yotdim.

column1: I took a shower. After that, I ate.
column2: Dush qabul qildim. Shundan keyin ovqatlandim.

column1: Work finished. After that, I took a shower.
column2: Ish tugadi. Shundan keyin dush qabul qildim.

column1: Sam, why did you leave early yesterday?
I had a bad headache. So I went to the hospital.
column2: Boshim qattiq ogʻridi. Shuning uchun kasalxonaga bordim.

column1: Yes, I took medicine. And I slept well.
column2: Ha, dori ichdim. Va yaxshi uxladim.

column1: All of them mean "but". "그런데" is also used to change the topic (by the way).
column2: Ularning hammasi "lekin" degani. "그런데" mavzuni oʻzgartirish uchun ham ishlatiladi (aytgancha).

column1: For a contrast use "하지만, 그렇지만", and to change the topic use "그런데".
column2: Zidlik uchun "하지만, 그렇지만", mavzuni oʻzgartirish uchun "그런데" ishlating.

column1: When you join them into one sentence, they become "-지만" or "-는데": "비싸지만 맛있어요."
column2: Ularni bitta gapga birlashtirganda "-지만" yoki "-는데" boʻladi: "비싸지만 맛있어요."

column1: Starting with "그런데" is a sign that you are bringing up something new: "그런데요, 교수님…"
column2: 그런데 bilan boshlash yangi narsa aytmoqchi ekaningizni bildiradi: "그런데요, 교수님…"

column1: If you answer an older person or boss right away with "하지만", it can sound like you are arguing. Start softly with "네, 그런데요…".
column2: Yoshi katta odam yoki xoʻjayinga darhol "하지만" bilan javob bersangiz, bahslashayotgandek eshitilishi mumkin. Yumshoq qilib "네, 그런데요…" deb boshlang.

column1: Korean is difficult. But it's fun.
Korea is cold. But the snow is pretty.
There's a lot of work. But it's okay.
The pay at my part-time job is low. But the work is easy.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ishimdagi maosh kam. Lekin ish oson.

column1: By the way, what time is it now?
By the way, who is that person?
By the way, is next semester's timetable out?
column2: Aytgancha, kelasi semestr dars jadvali chiqdimi?

column1: By the way, where are you going?
By the way, did you eat?
By the way, are you off tomorrow?
I'm tired. But I still have to go.
It's raining. But I'm still going.
It's hard. Still, when I think of my family, I feel stronger.
column2: Qiyin. Shunday boʻlsa ham, oilamni oʻylasam, kuchga kiraman.

column1: The room is small. But it's clean.
That's good. By the way, have you had dinner?
Not yet. Shall we eat together?
It means "then, in that case". "그럼" is short for "그러면", but it is also used as an answer meaning "of course".
column2: Bu "unda, shunday boʻlsa" degani. "그럼" — "그러면" ning qisqasi, lekin "albatta" maʼnosidagi javob sifatida ham ishlatiladi.

column1: When saying goodbye, start with "그럼": "그럼, 안녕히 계세요", "그럼 들어가세요".
column2: Xayrlashayotganda "그럼" bilan boshlang: "그럼, 안녕히 계세요", "그럼 들어가세요".

column1: 그럼요 is a happy "yes". With older people or bosses, "네, 물론입니다" is more polite.
column2: 그럼요 — xursandchilik bilan aytilgan "ha". Yoshi katta odamlar yoki xoʻjayinlar bilan "네, 물론입니다" muloyimroq.

column1: When you join it into one sentence, it becomes "-(으)면": "시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."
column2: Uni bitta gapga birlashtirganda "-(으)면" boʻladi: "시간이 없으면 내일 하세요."

column1: Then I'll come back tomorrow morning.
Well then, I'll be going now.
(먼저 가 보겠습니다 = I'll be leaving first)
Then I'll contact you again next week.
Can I go with you? Of course.
Of course. Ask me any time.
Can I go first? Yes, go ahead.
Oh, so that's how they do it in Korea. I see.
column2: A, Koreyada shunday qilishar ekan-da. Tushunarli.

column1: Boss, we've run out of milk today.
Really? Then let's clean up and finish early today.
column2: Shundaymi? Unda bugun yigʻishtirib, erta tugataylik.

column1: Should I come in at the usual time tomorrow?
그러니까 gives the reason first and then the result (so), and "왜냐하면" gives the result first and then the reason (because).
column2: 그러니까 avval sababni, keyin natijani aytadi (shuning uchun), "왜냐하면" esa avval natijani, keyin sababni aytadi (chunki).

column1: To give the result use "그러니까", and to give the reason use "왜냐하면".
column2: Natijani aytish uchun "그러니까", sababni aytish uchun "왜냐하면" ishlating.

column1: Before an order or a suggestion, use "그러니까", not "그래서".
column2: Buyruq yoki taklifdan oldin "그래서" emas, "그러니까" ishlating.

column1: 때문에 is for bad results, and "덕분에" is for good results: "교수님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."
column2: 때문에 yomon natijalar uchun, "덕분에" esa yaxshi natijalar uchun: "교수님 덕분에 잘 배웠습니다."

column1: We don't have time. So hurry up.
It's raining. So take an umbrella.
column2: Yomgʻir yogʻyapti. Shuning uchun soyabon oling.

column1: They say it will rain tomorrow. So bring an umbrella.
column2: Ertaga yomgʻir yogʻarmish. Shuning uchun soyabon olib keling.

column1: I can't go today. Because I have my part-time job.
column2: Bugun bora olmayman. Chunki qoʻshimcha ishim bor.

column1: I came to Korea. Because I wanted to earn money.
column2: Koreyaga keldim. Chunki pul topmoqchi edim.

column1: I'm going home next month. Because my younger brother is getting married.
column2: Kelasi oy vatanimga ketaman. Chunki ukam uylanyapti.

column1: I was late because of the rain.
The shuttle bus isn't coming because of the snow.
Thanks to you, it ended well.
I passed the exam thanks to my professor.
Thanks to my friends in my department, I got used to life in Korea quickly.
column2: Kafedramdagi doʻstlarim tufayli Koreyadagi hayotga tez moslashdim.

column1: to adjust, to get used to

column2: Aynan. Men ham shunday deb oʻylayman.

column1: It's so hot, isn't it? I know, right?
I know. Prices have gone up so much these days.
column2: Toʻgʻri. Keyingi paytlarda narxlar juda oshib ketdi.

column1: This blender's blade is sharp. So when you wash it, always turn off the power first.
column2: Bu blenderning pichogʻi oʻtkir. Shuning uchun yuvganda doim avval elektrni oʻchiring.

column1: Okay. But why do we turn off the power first?
column2: Xoʻp. Lekin nega avval elektrni oʻchiramiz?
Chunki u birdan harakatlanib ketishi mumkin.

column1: I understand. Thanks to you, I'm learning a lot.
column2: Tushundim. Sizning tufayli koʻp narsa oʻrganyapman.

column1: Question words for "what, which, what kind of". Some are used alone, and some come before a noun.
column2: Nima, qaysi, qanday soʻroq soʻzlari. Baʼzilari yolgʻiz, baʼzilari otdan oldin ishlatiladi.

column1: Use "뭐" alone, "무슨" for type, "어떤" for what something is like, and "어느" for choosing.
column2: Yolgʻiz "뭐", tur uchun "무슨", qandayligi uchun "어떤", tanlash uchun "어느" ishlating.

column1: The place of the question word is different from English. English puts it first ("What are you doing?"), but Korean puts it before the verb: "뭐 해요?"
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi kabi, koreyschada ham soʻroq soʻzi feʼldan oldin keladi: "Nima qilyapsiz?" = "뭐 해요?"

column1: 뭐 is short for "무엇". Use "뭐" when speaking, and "무엇" in writing or formal speech.
column2: 뭐 — "무엇" ning qisqasi. Gapirganda "뭐", yozuvda yoki rasmiy nutqda "무엇" ishlating.

column1: 무슨 일 있어요? is a caring question: "Is something wrong?"
column2: 무슨 일 있어요? gʻamxoʻrlik bildiruvchi savol: "Biror gap boʻldimi?"

column1: What's on the lunch menu today?
What kind of food do you like?
What kind of work have you done?
Which bank has cheap fees for sending money abroad?
column2: Qaysi bankda chet elga pul oʻtkazish komissiyasi arzon?

column1: Excuse me. What did you say?
Sorry, what? Please say it again.
column2: Kechirasiz, nima? Yana bir marta ayting.

column2: Oldidan "안전" kelsa, bu sizni jarohatdan himoya qiladigan narsa.

column1: 안전 comes first and the thing comes after: 안전 + 띠 = 안전띠, 안전 + 교육 = 안전 교육, 안전 + 수칙 = 안전 수칙.
column2: Oʻzbekchadagi kabi, "안전" birinchi, narsa keyin keladi: 안전 + 띠 = 안전띠 (xavfsizlik kamari), 안전 + 교육 = 안전 교육, 안전 + 수칙 = 안전 수칙.

column1: Other words with "안전": 안전벨트 (seat belt), 안전거리 (safe distance), 안전요원 (safety staff, lifeguard), 안전사고 (accident).
column2: 안전 li boshqa soʻzlar: 안전벨트 (xavfsizlik kamari), 안전거리 (xavfsiz masofa), 안전요원 (xavfsizlik xodimi, qutqaruvchi), 안전사고 (baxtsiz hodisa).

column1: Safety is the most important thing.
For safety, don't go around alone at night.
You have to wear a seat belt on the bus too.
column2: Avtobusda ham xavfsizlik kamarini taqishingiz kerak.

column1: When you take an express bus, be sure to fasten your seat belt.
column2: Tezyurar avtobusga oʻtirganingizda xavfsizlik kamarini albatta taqing.

An emergency alert text came because of the typhoon.
column2: Tayfun sababli favqulodda ogohlantirish SMS'i keldi.

column2: Jazirama haqida ogohlantirish SMS'i kelsa, tashqariga chiqmang.

column2: Ertaga yotoqxonada xavfsizlik boʻyicha mashgʻulot bor.

column1: After safety training, you sign a confirmation form.
column2: Xavfsizlik mashgʻulotidan keyin tasdiqlash varaqasiga imzo qoʻyasiz.

to be stuck on, to be posted
If you don't follow the safety rules, you can get hurt.
column2: Xavfsizlik qoidalariga rioya qilmasangiz, jarohat olishingiz mumkin.

There is dorm safety training at 2 p.m. today. Everyone must attend.
column2: Bugun kunduzi soat 2 da yotoqxonada xavfsizlik boʻyicha mashgʻulot bor. Hamma qatnashishi shart.

column2: Yongʻin chiqqanda qanday chiqib ketishni oʻrganamiz. Xavfsizlik qoidalarini ham albatta oʻqib chiqing.

column1: 근(勤) means to work hard. It is in words about going to and from work (like a part-time job) and about working hours.
column2: 근(勤) astoydil ishlash degani. U ishga (masalan, qoʻshimcha ishga) borish-kelish va ish soatlari haqidagi soʻzlarda bor.

column1: Words with "근" are about going to work and working hours.
column2: 근 li soʻzlar ishga borish va ish soatlari haqida.

column1: When you can't go to your part-time job, be sure to call the owner before work starts. If you don't come without telling anyone, it is "무단결근" (absence without notice) and becomes a big problem.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ishingizga bora olmasangiz, ish boshlanishidan oldin xoʻjayinga albatta qoʻngʻiroq qiling. Hech kimga aytmasdan kelmasangiz, bu "무단결근" (sababsiz ishga chiqmaslik) boʻladi va katta muammoga aylanadi.

column1: Add "하다" to all of them to make verbs: 출근하다, 퇴근하다, 결근하다, 근무하다.
column2: Hammasiga "하다" qoʻshib feʼl yasang: 출근하다, 퇴근하다, 결근하다, 근무하다.

column1: I go to work at the convenience store by eight.
The roads are jammed at rush hour.
column2: Ishga boriladigan paytda yoʻllar tirband boʻladi.

The roads are jammed when people leave work.
column2: Odamlar ishdan qaytayotganda yoʻllar tirband boʻladi.

column2: Qoʻshimcha ish smenamdan keyin topshiriqlarimni bajaraman.

You must not miss work without telling anyone.
column2: Hech kimga aytmasdan ishga chiqmaslik mumkin emas.

column2: Dam olish kunlari ish vaqti besh soat.

column2: Kutubxonada oʻqish bilan birga ishlaydigan talaba sifatida ishlayman.
stipendiyachi talaba (근로 장학생 = oʻqib ishlaydigan stipendiyachi)

If you are often late, your attendance score is low.
column2: Tez-tez kechiksangiz, davomat balingiz past boʻladi.

column1: Really? Be sure to go to the hospital. Can you come in tomorrow?
column2: Shundaymi? Albatta kasalxonaga boring. Ertaga kela olasizmi?

It's okay. Thanks for letting me know early.
column2: Hechqisi yoʻq. Erta xabar berganingiz uchun rahmat.

column1: 출(出) means to go out, "입(入)" means to go in, and "퇴(退)" means to step back or leave. If you know these three, you can read many words on signs.
column2: 출(出) chiqmoq, "입(入)" kirmoq, "퇴(退)" esa orqaga chekinmoq yoki ketmoq degani. Shu uchtasini bilsangiz, belgilardagi koʻp soʻzlarni oʻqiy olasiz.

column1: 출 means to go out, "입" means to go in, and "퇴" means to step back or leave.
column2: 출 — chiqmoq, "입" — kirmoq, "퇴" — chekinmoq yoki ketmoq.

column1: If you change one letter, you get the opposite word: 출구·입구, 출국·입국, 입원·퇴원, 입실·퇴실 (check-in, check-out), 입장·퇴장.
column2: Bitta harfni almashtirsangiz, qarama-qarshi soʻz hosil boʻladi: 출구·입구, 출국·입국, 입원·퇴원, 입실·퇴실 (joylashish, chiqib ketish), 입장·퇴장.

column1: 출입국 관리 사무소 is the office that handles going into (입) and out of (출) the country (국).
column2: 출입국 관리 사무소 mamlakatga (국) kirish (입) va chiqish (출) bilan shugʻullanadigan idora.

column1: Tell your friend the subway exit number.
column2: Doʻstingizga metro chiqish yoʻli raqamini ayting.

column1: Let's meet at the library entrance.
Tap your student ID at the dorm entrance.
column2: Yotoqxona kirish joyida talaba ID kartangizni tekkizing.

column1: Tap your card when you go in and out.
I'm leaving the country next month.
I sent my things before leaving the country.
When your departure date is set, tell the department office.
column2: Joʻnash sanangiz belgilansa, kafedra idorasiga xabar bering.

column1: to be set, to be decided
You must register as a foreigner within 90 days of the day you enter the country.
column2: Mamlakatga kirgan kundan boshlab 90 kun ichida chet ellik sifatida roʻyxatdan oʻtishingiz shart.

column1: I got hurt and was in the hospital.
My friend went into the hospital, so I went to visit.
column2: Doʻstim kasalxonaga yotdi, shuning uchun uni koʻrgani bordim.

column1: If you go into the hospital, give your professor a medical certificate.
column2: Kasalxonaga yotsangiz, professoringizga tibbiy maʼlumotnoma bering.

column2: Kasalxonadan chiqqandan keyin bir hafta dam olishingiz kerak.
Xonani boʻshatish vaqti soat oʻn bir.

column1: I packed my bags before checking out of the hotel.
During the school vacation, you have to move out of the dorm.
column2: Taʼtil paytida yotoqxonadan chiqib ketishingiz kerak.

It's over there in front of the bank. For city hall, go out of Exit 2.
column2: Ana u yerda, bank oldida. Shahar hokimiyatiga borish uchun 2-chiqish yoʻlidan chiqing.

column1: 금(禁) means "do not". If you see "금" or "금지" on a sign, you must not do that thing.
column2: 금(禁) "mumkin emas" degani. Belgida "금" yoki "금지" ni koʻrsangiz, oʻsha ishni qilish mumkin emas.

column1: If you see "금" or "금지", it is something you must not do.
column2: 금 yoki "금지" ni koʻrsangiz, bu qilish mumkin boʻlmagan ish.

column1: The order is opposite to English: "no entry" is 출입 + 금지. "금지" comes at the end.
column2: Tartib oʻzbekchadagidek: "kirish taqiqlanadi" = 출입 + 금지. "금지" oxirida keladi.

column1: When you say it, use "-지 마세요" or "-(으)면 안 돼요". "촬영 금지" is the same as "사진을 찍지 마세요".
column2: Ogʻzaki aytganda "-지 마세요" yoki "-(으)면 안 돼요" ishlating. "촬영 금지" "사진을 찍지 마세요" bilan bir xil.

column1: Other "do not" signs: 접근 금지 (keep away), 통행 금지 (no passing), 흡연 금지 (no smoking), 손대지 마시오 (do not touch).
column2: Boshqa "mumkin emas" belgilari: 접근 금지 (yaqinlashmang), 통행 금지 (oʻtish taqiqlanadi), 흡연 금지 (chekish taqiqlanadi), 손대지 마시오 (tegmang).

column2: Yotoqxonada spirtli ichimlik ichish mumkin emas.

column2: Avtobus bekatlari yaqinida ham chekish mumkin emas.
faqat xodimlar uchun, begonalarga kirish taqiqlanadi

column1: It's under construction, so no entry.
If you go into a no-entry area, you get a warning.
column2: Kirish taqiqlangan hududga kirsangiz, ogohlantirish olasiz.

column1: No cooking is allowed in dorm rooms.
column2: Yotoqxona xonalarida ovqat pishirish mumkin emas.

column1: Cooking isn't allowed, so you can't even boil ramyeon.
column2: Ovqat pishirish mumkin emas, shuning uchun hatto ramyeon ham qaynatolmaysiz.

column1: to be okay (안 돼요 = not allowed)
Inside the park is a no-cooking area.
No photos inside the concert hall.
column2: Konsert zali ichida suratga olish taqiqlanadi.

column1: No photos in the art museum.
Delete the photos you took in a no-photo area.
column2: Suratga olish taqiqlangan joyda olgan rasmlaringizni oʻchiring.

column1: Out of order. Do not use.
This restroom is closed (do not use).
Don't use a washing machine with a "사용 금지" sign.
column2: 사용 금지 belgisi osilgan kir yuvish mashinasidan foydalanmang.

column1: No outside food or drinks allowed.
column2: Tashqaridan ovqat va ichimlik olib kirish mumkin emas.

Using phones during the exam is not allowed.
column2: Imtihon paytida telefondan foydalanish mumkin emas.

column2: Yoʻq, mumkin emas. Eshikda "출입 금지" deb yozilgan.

column1: The whole building is non-smoking. There is a smoking area outside.
column2: Butun bino chekish taqiqlangan hudud. Tashqarida chekish joyi bor.

column1: -기(機, 器) means a machine or tool. It is like "-er" in English (washer, cleaner), and it also goes at the end.
column2: -기(機, 器) mashina yoki asbob degani. Oʻzbekchadagi "-gich" (changyutgich, quritgich) ga oʻxshaydi va u ham oxirida keladi.

column1: Words that end in "-기" are machines or tools that do that job.
column2: -기 bilan tugaydigan soʻzlar oʻsha ishni bajaradigan mashina yoki asboblar.

column1: The order is the same as English "washing machine": washing + machine = 세탁 + 기.
column2: Tartib oʻzbekchadagi "kir yuvish mashinasi" bilan bir xil: kir yuvish + mashina = 세탁 + 기.

column1: Other words with "-기": 계산기 (calculator), 선풍기 (electric fan), 전화기 (telephone), 자판기 (vending machine), 건조기 (clothes dryer), 비행기 (airplane).
column2: -기 li boshqa soʻzlar: 계산기 (kalkulyator), 선풍기 (ventilyator), 전화기 (telefon apparati), 자판기 (avtomat), 건조기 (kiyim quritgich), 비행기 (samolyot).

column1: Learn where the fire extinguisher is and how to use it on your first day. Pull the pin, point it at the fire, and squeeze the handle.
column2: Birinchi kuningizdayoq oʻt oʻchirgich qayerdaligini va undan qanday foydalanishni oʻrganing. Chekani sugʻuring, olovga qarating va dastani siqing.

column2: Kir yuvish mashinasidan qanday foydalanishni aytib bering.

column2: Nusxa koʻchirish mashinasiga qogʻoz tiqilib qoldi.

column2: Nusxa koʻchirish mashinasiga qogʻoz tiqilsa, kuch bilan tortib olmang.

column2: Yotoqxonaning har bir qavatida suv tozalagich bor.

I left my charger in the dormitory.
You can use a laptop charger in the library.
The fire extinguisher is next to the door.
Do you know how to use a fire extinguisher?
Learn where the fire extinguisher is in advance.
column2: Oʻt oʻchirgich qayerdaligini oldindan bilib oling.

column2: Minha, kir yuvish mashinasidan tutun chiqyapti!

column2: Tezda elektrni oʻchiring! Oʻt oʻchirgichni olib keling!

column2: 학(學) oʻrganmoq degani. Oʻzbekchadagi "oʻqish, oʻrganish" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: Other words with "학": 학년 (school year, grade), 학기 (semester), 학비 (tuition), 수학 (math), 과학 (science), and 입학, the pair of 졸업 (graduation).
column2: 학 li boshqa soʻzlar: 학년 (kurs, sinf), 학기 (semestr), 학비 (oʻqish puli), 수학 (matematika), 과학 (fan, ilm) va 졸업 (bitirish) ning jufti boʻlgan 입학.

column1: Schools in Korea: elementary school 6 years, middle school 3 years, high school 3 years, university 4 years.
column2: Koreyadagi taʼlim: boshlangʻich maktab 6 yil, oʻrta maktab 3 yil, yuqori maktab 3 yil, universitet 4 yil.

column1: 학 makes the next sound strong: 학교 [학꾜], 학생 [학쌩]. If a vowel comes next, the sound moves over: 학원 [하권].
column2: 학 keyingi tovushni kuchaytiradi: 학교 [학꾜], 학생 [학쌩]. Keyin unli kelsa, tovush oʻtadi: 학원 [하권].

Ask if there is a student discount.

column2: Oʻquv markazi toʻlovi qimmat, shuning uchun bepul darsga qatnayman.

During vacation, I travel to Seoul.

Sam, where did you learn Korean?

Do you still go to an academy?
Yes, every weekend I go to a Korean language academy in Jeonju.
column2: Ha, har dam olish kuni Chonjudagi koreys tili oʻquv markaziga boraman.

column1: 식(食) means to eat. It is in words about food and meals.
column2: 식(食) yemoq degani. U ovqat va taomlar haqidagi soʻzlarda bor.

column1: One letter of a country name + 식: 한식 (Korean food), 중식 (Chinese food), 일식 (Japanese food), 양식 (Western food).
column2: Mamlakat nomining bitta harfi + 식: 한식 (koreys taomi), 중식 (xitoy taomi), 일식 (yapon taomi), 양식 (yevropa taomi).

column1: In school cafeteria and dormitory notices, they write 조식 (breakfast), 중식 (lunch), 석식 (dinner). Here, "중식" means lunch.
column2: Universitet oshxonasi va yotoqxona eʼlonlarida 조식 (nonushta), 중식 (tushlik), 석식 (kechki ovqat) deb yoziladi. Bu yerda "중식" tushlik degani.

column1: I eat lunch at the school cafeteria.
What time does the restaurant open?
The student cafeteria menu is on the notice board.
At mealtime, we stand in line and wait.
Korean meals have many side dishes.
At first Korean food was spicy, but now I like it.
column2: Avvaliga koreys taomlari achchiq edi, lekin endi yaxshi koʻraman.

I eat fruit as a snack.
During exam period, the student council hands out snacks.

I spent a lot on food this month.
column2: Bu oy ovqatga koʻp pul sarfladim.

column2: Hali yoʻq. Hozir talabalar oshxonasiga ketmoqchi edim.

column1: Today's lunch is bibimbap. Is Korean food okay for you?
column2: Bugungi tushlik — bibimbap. Koreys taomlari sizga toʻgʻri keladimi?

column1: 회(會) means to gather. It is in words where people get together to talk and do things together.
column2: 회(會) yigʻilmoq degani. U odamlar birga gaplashish va ish qilish uchun yigʻiladigan soʻzlarda bor.

column1: Words with "회" are about people getting together.
column2: 회 li soʻzlar odamlarning yigʻilishi haqida.

column1: If you can't drink alcohol at a welcome party or a club get-together, you can say "저는 술을 못 마셔요. 음료수를 마실게요" (I can't drink alcohol. I'll have a soft drink).
column2: Xush kelibsiz kechasi yoki togʻarak yigʻilishida spirtli ichimlik icha olmasangiz, "저는 술을 못 마셔요. 음료수를 마실게요" (Men spirtli ichimlik ichmayman. Alkogolsiz ichimlik ichaman) deyishingiz mumkin.

column1: Other words: 대회 (contest), 환영회 (welcome party), 송별회 (farewell party), 동창회 (alumni meeting), 전시회 (exhibition), 국회 (National Assembly).
column2: Boshqa soʻzlar: 대회 (tanlov, musobaqa), 환영회 (xush kelibsiz kechasi), 송별회 (xayrlashuv kechasi), 동창회 (bitiruvchilar uchrashuvi), 전시회 (koʻrgazma), 국회 (Milliy Assambleya).

column1: The student council is preparing the festival.
The student council office is in Star Center.
The student council holds a welcome party for new students.
column2: Talabalar kengashi yangi talabalar uchun xush kelibsiz kechasi oʻtkazadi.

column1: There is a meeting at ten.
We have the group project meeting at the library.

I haven't paid the dues yet.
We bought snacks with the dues.
I am a member of the soccer club.
To become a member, hand in an application form.
column2: Aʼzo boʻlish uchun ariza shaklini topshiring.

column1: I want to know about Korean society.
Working life (life in society) is not easy.
In Korean society, being on time is seen as important.
column2: Koreya jamiyatida vaqtga rioya qilish muhim hisoblanadi.

column1: The student council president greeted the new students.
column2: Talabalar kengashi raisi yangi talabalarni qutladi.

column1: This evening there is a welcome party for the new club members.

After the meeting, at 6:30, at the barbecue restaurant in front of the school.
column2: Yigʻilishdan keyin, soat 6:30 da, universitet oldidagi goʻsht restoranida.

column1: 시(時) means time. It is like "time" or "o'clock" in English.
column2: 시(時) vaqt degani. Oʻzbekchadagi "vaqt" yoki "soat" ga oʻxshaydi.

column1: 시 is a time on the clock (세 시), and "시간" is a length of time (세 시간). "Three o'clock" is "세 시", and "three hours" is "세 시간".
column2: 시 — soatdagi vaqt (세 시), "시간" — vaqt davomiyligi (세 시간). "Soat uch" — "세 시", "uch soat" esa "세 시간".

column1: Other words: 동시 (at the same time), 임시 (temporary), 당시 (at that time), 시대 (era, period), 시간표 (timetable), 시차 (time difference).
column2: Boshqa soʻzlar: 동시 (bir vaqtda), 임시 (vaqtinchalik), 당시 (oʻsha paytda), 시대 (davr), 시간표 (dars jadvali), 시차 (vaqt farqi).

column1: Other words: 전선 (electric wire), 전구 (light bulb), 정전 (power outage), 감전 (electric shock), 전철 (electric train), 전자레인지 (microwave), 건전지 (battery).

column1: If you add "하다" to a noun, it becomes a verb.

column1: 하다 changes to "해요, 했어요, 할 거예요, 합니다". If you know just this, you can use all "하다" verbs.

column1: In notices and text messages, "하다" is often dropped and only the noun is used: "확인 바랍니다" (please check), "연락 주세요" (please contact us), "도착 예정" (expected to arrive).

column1: Movement words are made with a direction + "가다/오다".

column1: Ask with "-이/가 어디예요?" and "몇 층이에요?", and understand "쭉 가세요" (go straight) and "옆에 있어요" (it's next to).

column1: In room numbers, the first digit is usually the floor: Room 305 is usually on the 3rd floor. Your timetable shows the building name and room number together.
column2: Xona raqamlarida birinchi raqam odatda qavatni bildiradi: 305-xona odatda 3-qavatda. Dars jadvalingizda bino nomi va xona raqami birga koʻrsatiladi.

column2: Birinchi darsdan oldin maʼruza xonasini topib qoʻysangiz, kechikmaysiz.

column1: Jeonju University has student cafeterias in the Star Center and the student union building. These are words for ordering and eating there.
column2: Chonju universitetida Star Center va talabalar uyida talabalar oshxonalari bor. Bu u yerda buyurtma berish va ovqatlanish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: At the student cafeteria, buy a meal ticket at the kiosk and ask in advance about food you can't eat.
column2: Talabalar oshxonasida kioskdan ovqat taloni sotib oling va yey olmaydigan ovqatingiz haqida oldindan soʻrang.

column1: Jeonju University has run a "1,000-won breakfast" for students. In the 2nd semester of 2025 it was on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday mornings at the campus student cafeterias. Check the notice each semester for dates and times.
column2: Chonju universiteti talabalar uchun "1 000 vonlik nonushta" tashkil qilib keladi. 2025-yil 2-semestrida u seshanba, chorshanba va payshanba kunlari ertalab kampusdagi talabalar oshxonalarida boʻldi. Sana va vaqtni har semestr eʼlondan tekshiring.

column1: If you don't eat meat or eat only halal food, ask "돼지고기 들어 있어요?" (Is there pork in it?) or "고기 빼 주세요" (Please leave out the meat).
column2: Goʻsht yemasangiz yoki faqat halol taom yesangiz, "돼지고기 들어 있어요?" (Ichida choʻchqa goʻshti bormi?) yoki "고기 빼 주세요" (Goʻshtsiz qilib bering) deb soʻrang.

column1: I eat lunch at the student cafeteria.
The student cafeteria is cheaper than outside.
The student union cafeteria is crowded at lunchtime.
column2: Talabalar uyidagi oshxona tushlik vaqtida gavjum boʻladi.

column1: Does the menu say whether there's pork in it?
column2: Menyuda ichida choʻchqa goʻshti bor-yoʻqligi yozilganmi?

After buying a meal ticket, you line up.
column2: Ovqat talonini olgandan keyin navbatga turasiz.

column2: 1 000 vonlik nonushta tez tugaydi, shuning uchun erta boring.

to be possible to take out

column2: Pibimbap ham bor. Goʻshtsiz qilib berishni soʻrasangiz boʻldi.

column1: When you feel sick at school, you can go to the health room (보건실). If it's serious, you go to a hospital. These are the words you need.
column2: Universitetda kasal boʻlib qolsangiz, tibbiyot xonasiga (보건실) borishingiz mumkin. Jiddiy boʻlsa, kasalxonaga borasiz. Bu sizga kerak boʻladigan soʻzlar.

column1: For a mild illness go to the health room; for something serious go to a hospital. If you miss class, submit a doctor's note.
column2: Yengil kasallikda tibbiyot xonasiga, jiddiy holatda kasalxonaga boring. Darsni qoldirsangiz, shifokor maʼlumotnomasini topshiring.

column1: Say where it hurts with "-이/가 아파요": 머리가 아파요 (I have a headache), 배가 아파요 (My stomach hurts).
column2: Qayeringiz ogʻriyotganini "-이/가 아파요" bilan ayting: 머리가 아파요 (boshim ogʻriyapti), 배가 아파요 (qornim ogʻriyapti).

column1: International students in Korea must also join the national health insurance. Check details with the National Health Insurance Service or the International Office. In an emergency, call 119.
column2: Koreyadagi xorijlik talabalar ham milliy tibbiy sugʻurtaga aʼzo boʻlishi kerak. Tafsilotlarni Milliy tibbiy sugʻurta xizmati yoki Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan aniqlang. Favqulodda holatda 119 ga qoʻngʻiroq qiling.

column1: I had a headache, so I went to the health room.

column1: I got medicine at the health room.
I checked on the school website where the health room is.
column2: Tibbiyot xonasi qayerdaligini universitet veb-saytidan bilib oldim.

column1: Bring your residence card and insurance information when you go to the hospital.
column2: Kasalxonaga borganingizda ID kartangiz va sugʻurta maʼlumotlaringizni olib boring.

column1: I signed up for health insurance.
International students also need health insurance.
column2: Xorijlik talabalarga ham tibbiy sugʻurta kerak.

column1: With health insurance, hospital bills are lower.
column2: Tibbiy sugʻurta boʻlsa, davolanish xarajati kamroq boʻladi.

I was absent, so I gave the professor a doctor's note.
column2: Darsga kelmaganim uchun professorga shifokor maʼlumotnomasini berdim.

column2: Kechirasiz, boshim ogʻriyapti va isitmam bor.

Since yesterday evening. I think I caught a cold.
column2: Kecha kechqurundan beri. Shamollab qolganga oʻxshayman.

column2: Sizga dori beraman. Ertaga ham isitmangiz boʻlsa, kasalxonaga boring.

column1: These are things the professor often says in Korean class. You will also see them in this app, so learn them first.

column1: -(으)세요 is a polite way to tell someone to do something: 보세요 (look), 읽으세요 (read), 쓰세요 (write).
column2: -(으)세요 – biror narsa qilishni xushmuomalalik bilan buyurish: 보세요 (qarang), 읽으세요 (oʻqing), 쓰세요 (yozing).

column1: If you don't understand, say "모르겠어요" (I don't know) or "다시 말해 주세요" (please say it again).
column2: Tushunmasangiz, "모르겠어요" (bilmayman) yoki "다시 말해 주세요" (qaytadan ayting) deng.

column1: I write new words in my notebook.
I had a lot of work for my English-taught classes, so I couldn't do my Korean homework.

column1: English-track students also take Korean classes. These are words used in Korean class.
column2: Ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalish talabalari ham koreys tili darslariga qatnaydi. Bu koreys tili darsida ishlatiladigan soʻzlar.

column1: The person who learns is a 학생, the person who teaches is a 교수님. English-track students also study in a Korean class.
column2: Oʻrganuvchi – 학생, oʻrgatuvchi – 교수님. Ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalish talabalari ham koreys tili guruhida oʻqiydi.

column1: 한국어 and "한국말" mean the same: the Korean language.
column2: 한국어 va "한국말" bir xil maʼnoni bildiradi: koreys tili.

column1: Even in the English track, learning Korean makes campus life, part-time jobs and making friends much easier.
column2: Ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalishda boʻlsangiz ham, koreys tilini oʻrgansangiz, universitet hayoti, qoʻshimcha ish va doʻst orttirish ancha osonlashadi.

column1: 교수님 is used not only for teachers but also to politely address doctors and older people you meet for the first time.
column2: 교수님 faqat oʻqituvchilarga emas, shifokorlar va birinchi marta uchrashgan kattalarga hurmat bilan murojaat qilishda ham ishlatiladi.

column2: Imtihon uchun "보다", savollar uchun "풀다", javob tanlash uchun "고르다" ishlatiladi.

column2: 시험 (imtihon) bilan "보다" ishlatiladi: 시험을 보다 (imtihon topshirmoq). 문제 (savol) bilan "풀다" (yechmoq) ishlatiladi.

column1: Common test instructions: "다음을 듣고 맞는 것을 고르십시오" (Listen and choose the correct answer), "빈칸에 들어갈 말을 고르십시오" (Choose the word for the blank).
column2: Koʻp uchraydigan koʻrsatmalar: "다음을 듣고 맞는 것을 고르십시오" (Tinglang va toʻgʻri javobni tanlang), "빈칸에 들어갈 말을 고르십시오" (Boʻsh joyga mos soʻzni tanlang).

column2: -기 qoʻshilsa, feʼl otga aylanadi: 듣다 → 듣기 (tinglash), 읽다 → 읽기 (oʻqish), 쓰다 → 쓰기 (yozish).

Check the result on the website.

column2: Daraja testini topshirasiz va guruhga taqsimlanasiz. Agar toʻgʻri kelmasa, tezroq ayting.

column2: Har bir universitetda koreys tili guruhlari turlicha tashkil etiladi. Daraja testi va guruhga taqsimlash haqida universitet eʼlonlari yoki Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan (국제교류원) aniqlang.

column1: Levels are counted with Sino-Korean numbers: 일 단계 (level 1), 이 단계 (level 2).
column2: Darajalar xitoy-koreys sonlari bilan sanaladi: 일 단계 (1-daraja), 이 단계 (2-daraja).

column1: Your class is decided by the level test result.
column2: Guruhingiz daraja testi natijasiga qarab belgilanadi.

column1: The beginner class starts with Hangeul.
If you're learning Korean for the first time, you go into the beginner class.
column2: Koreys tilini birinchi marta oʻrganayotgan boʻlsangiz, boshlangʻich guruhga kirasiz.

column1: The intermediate class is a bit hard.

column2: Kelasi semestrda oʻrta daraja guruhiga oʻtmoqchiman.

column2: Bu har semestrda oʻqiladigan fanlarni tanlash va ularga yozilish uchun soʻzlar.

column1: Plan your timetable and register before the deadline. Also check the credits you need to graduate.

column2: Ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalish fanlari ingliz tilida oʻtiladi.

column2: Bir semestrda olinadigan kreditlar soni belgilangan.

column2: Bitirish uchun kerakli kreditlarni kafedra idorasidan aniqlang.

column2: Bir yil ikki semestrdan iborat, ular orasida taʼtil boʻladi.
