column1: At first, I use polite speech with classmates too.
column2: Avvaliga kursdoshlarim bilan ham hurmat shaklida gaplashaman.

column1: Once you get close, you use casual speech instead of polite speech.
column2: Yaqinlashgandan keyin hurmat shakli oʻrniga oddiy (sensirab) gapiriladi.

column1: Aung, I'm Minha, a third-year. Ask me if you have any questions.
column2: Aung, men uchinchi kurs talabasi Minhaman. Savolingiz boʻlsa, soʻrang.

column1: We're in the same department, so let's be relaxed with each other.
OK, then let's have a meal together next time.
column2: Xoʻp, unda keyingi safar birga ovqatlanaylik.

column1: These are expressions for visiting Professor Hwang Insu during office hours to ask questions and get advice.
column2: Bu professor Xvang Insuning qabul soatlarida borib, savol berish va maslahat olish uchun ifodalar.

column1: During office hours, say why you came, ask about what you don't understand, and end by thanking the professor.
column2: Qabul soatlarida nima uchun kelganingizni ayting, tushunmagan joyingizni soʻrang va minnatdorchilik bilan yakunlang.

column1: Office hours are times when the professor is in the office to meet students. They are often in the syllabus or on the office door.
column2: Qabul soatlari – professor talabalarni qabul qilish uchun xonasida boʻladigan vaqt. Ular koʻpincha oʻquv dasturida yoki xona eshigida yozilgan boʻladi.

column1: If office hours don't suit you, email to ask for another time. Prepare your questions before you go.
column2: Qabul soatlari sizga toʻgʻri kelmasa, elektron xat orqali boshqa vaqt soʻrang. Savollaringizni oldindan tayyorlab boring.

column1: Professor, when are your office hours?
When are office hours this week?
Office hours aren't in the syllabus. When are they?
column2: Oʻquv dasturida qabul soatlari yoʻq. Ular qachon?

column1: May I come in for a moment?
Professor, may I come in for a moment?
Knock knock. May I come in for a moment?
I came because it's office hours. May I come in?
column2: Qabul soati boʻlgani uchun keldim. Kirsam boʻladimi?

column1: I came to ask about the assignment.
I came to ask about my midterm score.
column2: Oraliq imtihon balim haqida soʻragani keldim.

column1: I came to ask about course registration for next semester.
column2: Kelasi semestrda fanlarga yozilish haqida soʻragani keldim.

column1: Professor, I don't understand this part.
I don't understand this part of the lecture materials.
I don't understand this graph. Could you explain it again?
column2: Bu grafikni tushunmayapman. Yana tushuntirib bera olasizmi?

column1: I want to improve my grade. What should I do?
I want to improve my Korean. What would you suggest?
column2: Koreys tilimni yaxshilamoqchiman. Nima maslahat berasiz?

column1: I get so nervous about presentations. What should I do?
column2: Taqdimotdan juda hayajonlanaman. Nima qilsam boʻladi?

column1: Professor, thank you for your time.
Thank you for making time when you're busy.
column2: Band boʻlsangiz ham vaqt ajratganingiz uchun rahmat.

column1: It helped a lot. Thank you for your time.
column2: Juda foydali boʻldi. Vaqt ajratganingiz uchun rahmat.

column1: Professor Hwang, may I come in for a moment?
column2: Professor Xvang, bir daqiqaga kirsam boʻladimi?

column1: I came to ask about my midterm score. I don't understand the essay question.
column2: Oraliq imtihon balim haqida soʻragani keldim. Yozma javobli savolni tushunmayapman.

column1: Look here. You need more examples to get a higher score.
column2: Mana bu yerga qarang. Ball yuqori boʻlishi uchun koʻproq misol yozish kerak.

column1: Oh, I see. Thank you for your time.
column2: A, tushundim. Vaqt ajratganingiz uchun rahmat.

column1: These words are about clubs, groups of students with the same hobbies.
column2: Bu soʻzlar toʻgaraklar – bir xil qiziqishga ega talabalar guruhlari haqida.

column1: Join a club to make Korean friends at meetings and retreats.
column2: Toʻgarakka qoʻshilsangiz, yigʻilishlar va sayohatlarda (MT) koreys doʻstlar orttirasiz.

column1: At the start of each semester, clubs recruit new members, often promoting in front of the student union building.
column2: Har semestr boshida toʻgaraklar yangi aʼzolarni qabul qiladi, koʻpincha talabalar uyi oldida targʻibot qilishadi.

column1: Clubs are a great way to make Korean friends and improve your Korean.
column2: Toʻgarak – koreys doʻstlar orttirish va koreys tilini yaxshilashning ajoyib usuli.

column1: I made a lot of Korean friends in my club.
I filled in the membership form.

column2: Xorijlik talabalar ham aʼzo boʻla oladimi?

column1: The fee is 10,000 won a month.
We buy snacks with the fees.
I can't go to the meeting today.
I introduced myself at the first meeting.
Ask the president if you have questions.
I'm going on a club retreat.
We played games on the retreat.
Retreats are usually at the start of the semester.
Would you like to join our club?
Yes. Can international students join too?
column2: Ha. Xorijlik talabalar ham qoʻshila oladimi?

column1: Of course. We meet every Wednesday, and the fee is 10,000 won a month.
column2: Albatta. Har chorshanba yigʻilamiz, badal oyiga 10 000 von.

column1: Great. I'll fill in the membership form.
These words are about university events. Jeonju University holds a spring festival called 대동제.
column2: Bu soʻzlar universitet tadbirlari haqida. Chonju universiteti bahorda 대동제 degan festival oʻtkazadi.

column1: Taking part in festivals and events makes campus life more fun.
column2: Festival va tadbirlarda qatnashsangiz, universitet hayoti yanada qiziqarli boʻladi.

column1: During the festival, departments and clubs open booths and sell food. In 2023, 대동제 was held around the main sports field and the student union building.
column2: Festival davomida kafedralar va toʻgaraklar rastalar ochib, ovqat sotadi. 2023-yilda 대동제 katta stadion va talabalar uyi atrofida oʻtdi.

column1: If someone offers you alcohol at a party or retreat and you don't drink, it's fine to say "저는 술을 못 마셔요" (I can't drink).
column2: Ziyofat yoki sayohatda sizga spirtli ichimlik taklif qilishsa va siz ichmasangiz, "저는 술을 못 마셔요" (Men ichmayman) deyishingiz mumkin.

column1: The school festival is next week.
The Jeonju University festival is called 대동제.
column2: Chonju universiteti festivali 대동제 deb ataladi.

column1: I went to the start-of-semester party.
The Hotel Management start-of-semester party is on Friday.
column2: Mehmonxona menejmenti kafedrasining semestr boshidagi ziyofati juma kuni.

column1: I met seniors at the start-of-semester party.
column2: Semestr boshidagi ziyofatda katta kursdoshlar bilan tanishdim.

column1: Our department has a sports day.
I played soccer at sports day.
Everyone wears the same clothes on sports day.
column2: Sport kunida hamma bir xil kiyim kiyadi.

column1: I danced at the international student event.
I introduced Nepal at the international student event.
There's food from many countries at international student events.
column2: Xorijlik talabalar tadbirida koʻp davlatlarning taomlari boʻladi.

column1: I took part in the festival.
If you're taking part, write your name.
We opened an Uzbek food booth.
We sold plov at the booth.
There were a lot of people in front of the booth.
Is there an international student booth at this festival?
column2: Bu festivalda xorijlik talabalar rastasi bormi?

column1: Yes, Uzbek students are selling plov.
It's rice with meat and carrots. It's delicious!
column2: Goʻsht va sabzi solingan guruch taomi. Juda mazali!

column1: I'll definitely come and eat some!
These are expressions for becoming friends with Korean students.
column2: Bu koreys talabalar bilan doʻstlashish uchun ifodalar.

column1: Suggest eating together, ask for contacts and teach each other your languages to become friends easily.
column2: Birga ovqatlanishni taklif qiling, kontaktini soʻrang va bir-biringizga tilingizni oʻrgating – shunda oson doʻstlashasiz.

column1: -(으)ㄹ래요? is a soft way to suggest something to friends.
column2: -(으)ㄹ래요? doʻstlarga biror narsani yumshoq taklif qilishda ishlatiladi.

column1: In Korea people often ask your age. If you're the same age (동갑), they may suggest switching to casual speech.
column2: Koreyada yoshingizni tez-tez soʻrashadi. Agar tengdosh (동갑) boʻlsangiz, sensirashga oʻtishni taklif qilishlari mumkin.

column1: Do you want to eat together after class?
Do you want to eat together at the student cafeteria?
Do you want to have lunch together tomorrow?
Could you give me your contact?
Could you give me your contact for the assignment?
Could you give me your KakaoTalk ID or number?
column2: KakaoTalk ID ingiz yoki raqamingizni bera olasizmi?

column1: you can speak casually with me
We're the same age, so you can speak casually.
column2: Tengdoshmiz, shuning uchun bemalol sensirab gaplashavering.

column1: We're close now, so you can speak casually.
column2: Endi yaqin boʻlib qoldik, bemalol gaplashavering.

column1: Come visit Greece during the vacation.
Food in Singapore is delicious. Come visit.
Come visit Nepal. I'll show you around.
column2: Nepalga mehmonga keling. Men sizga hamma joyni koʻrsataman.

column1: Please teach me some Korean. I'll teach you English.
column2: Menga biroz koreys tilini oʻrgating. Men sizga ingliz tilini oʻrgataman.

column1: Pronunciation is hard. Please teach me.
Aisha, do you want to eat together after class?
Sure! We're the same age, so you can speak casually.
OK, Aisha. Let's go to the student cafeteria.
Great. Give me your number on the way too.
column2: Zoʻr. Yoʻl-yoʻlakay raqamingni ham berib qoʻy.

column1: These are words for buddy activities and language exchange, where a Korean student and an international student pair up to help each other. Ask the International Office whether a program is running.
column2: Bu koreys talaba va xorijlik talaba juftlashib bir-biriga yordam beradigan "badi" faoliyati va til almashinuvi uchun soʻzlar. Bunday dastur bor-yoʻqligini Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan soʻrang.

column1: Through buddies and language exchange, you make Korean friends and learn each other's language and culture.
column2: Badi va til almashinuvi orqali koreys doʻstlar orttirasiz, bir-biringizning tili va madaniyatini oʻrganasiz.

column1: A good language exchange splits the time in half: thirty minutes in Korean, thirty minutes in English.
column2: Yaxshi til almashinuvida vaqt teng boʻlinadi: oʻttiz daqiqa koreys tilida, oʻttiz daqiqa ingliz tilida.

column1: Buddy programs and language exchange groups differ by school and semester. Check International Office notices and the school website.
column2: Badi dasturlari va til almashinuvi guruhlari universitet va semestrga qarab farq qiladi. Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimi eʼlonlari va universitet veb-saytini tekshiring.

column1: My buddy showed me around campus.
Thanks to my buddy, alien registration was easy.
column2: Badim tufayli chet ellik sifatida roʻyxatdan oʻtish oson boʻldi.

column1: I want to do a language exchange.
We practise Korean and English through language exchange.
column2: Til almashinuvi orqali koreys va ingliz tilini mashq qilamiz.

column1: We do our language exchange once a week at a café.
column2: Til almashinuvini haftasiga bir marta kafeda oʻtkazamiz.

column1: I did homework with my partner.
column2: Sherigim bilan birga uy vazifasini qildim.

column1: If your partner is busy, change to another day.
column2: Sherigingiz band boʻlsa, boshqa kunga oʻtkazing.

column1: I signed up for the buddy program.
The sign-up period is short, so watch the notices.
column2: Yozilish muddati qisqa, eʼlonlarni kuzatib boring.

column1: This month's activity is visiting Jeonju Hanok Village.
column2: Bu oyning mashgʻuloti – Chonju Hanok qishlogʻini aylanish.

column1: We take photos of our activities and put them in the report.
I want to learn about Korean culture.
I introduced Bangladeshi culture to my buddy.
Our cultures are different, so it was a bit awkward at first.
column2: Madaniyatlarimiz har xil boʻlgani uchun avvaliga biroz noqulay boʻldi.

column1: Nice to meet you! I'm from Bangladesh.
Shall we do a language exchange too? I want to learn English.
column2: Til almashinuvi ham qilamizmi? Men ingliz tilini oʻrganmoqchiman.

column1: Great. I want to learn Korean. How about once a week?
column2: Zoʻr. Men koreys tilini oʻrganmoqchiman. Haftasiga bir marta boʻlsa-chi?

column1: Good. Let's meet at the Star Center on Thursday afternoon.
column2: Yaxshi. Payshanba kuni tushdan keyin Star Centerda uchrashaylik.

column1: These are words about the tuition you pay each semester.
column2: Bu har semestr toʻlanadigan kontrakt toʻlovi haqidagi soʻzlar.

column1: Check the bill and pay tuition within the payment period. If it's hard, apply to pay in installments.
column2: Hisob-varaqni koʻrib, kontraktni toʻlov muddatida toʻlang. Qiyin boʻlsa, boʻlib toʻlashga ariza bering.

column1: You're only enrolled for the semester once you pay tuition. Missing the period can cause serious problems.
column2: Kontraktni toʻlagandagina oʻsha semestr talabasi hisoblanasiz. Muddatni oʻtkazib yuborish jiddiy muammolarga olib kelishi mumkin.

column1: Sending money from abroad takes fees and time. Send it about a week before the deadline.
column2: Chet eldan pul joʻnatish komissiya va vaqt talab qiladi. Muddatdan taxminan bir hafta oldin joʻnating.

column1: You print the bill from the school portal.
Send the money to the account on the bill.
When is the tuition payment period?
If you miss the payment period, you're not registered.
column2: Toʻlov muddatini oʻtkazib yuborsangiz, roʻyxatdan oʻtmaysiz.

column1: Can I pay tuition in installments?
How many installments can I pay in?
You must apply in advance to pay in installments.
column2: Boʻlib toʻlash uchun oldindan ariza berish kerak.

column1: Please tell me the account number.
I opened an account at a Korean bank.
My parents sent money from Pakistan to my account.
Can I get a tuition refund?
If you take a leave of absence, you may get part of it back.
column2: Akademik taʼtil olsangiz, bir qismini qaytarib olishingiz mumkin.

column1: A refund takes some time after you apply.
column2: Ariza bergandan keyin pul qaytarilishi biroz vaqt oladi.

column1: The tuition bill is out. Until when is the payment period?
column2: Kontrakt hisob-varagʻi chiqdi. Toʻlov muddati qachongacha?

column1: It's on the bill. Until the 20th of this month.

column2: Ha, shu hafta ichida ariza bering.

column1: These are words for finding out about and applying for scholarships. Jeonju University's English track also has scholarships.
column2: Bu stipendiyalar haqida bilish va ularga ariza berish uchun soʻzlar. Chonju universitetining ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalishida ham stipendiyalar bor.

column1: For scholarships, check the requirements, prepare the documents and apply within the period.
column2: Stipendiya uchun talablarni tekshiring, hujjatlarni tayyorlang va muddat ichida ariza bering.

column1: Jeonju University's English-track scholarship guide lists a TOPIK scholarship (1,000,000 won) for students who get TOPIK level 4 or higher. Amounts and conditions can change, so always check the notice.
column2: Chonju universitetining ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalishi stipendiya yoʻriqnomasida TOPIK 4-darajasi yoki undan yuqori olgan talabalar uchun TOPIK stipendiyasi (1 000 000 von) bor. Miqdor va shartlar oʻzgarishi mumkin, shuning uchun eʼlonni albatta tekshiring.

column1: 급을 따다 means to pass a test and get a level: 토픽 삼 급을 땄어요 (I got TOPIK level 3).
column2: 급을 따다 imtihondan oʻtib daraja olishni bildiradi: 토픽 삼 급을 땄어요 (TOPIK 3-darajasini oldim).

column1: There are scholarships for English-track students.
column2: Ingliz tilidagi yoʻnalish talabalari uchun stipendiyalar bor.

column1: Thanks to the scholarship, my tuition went down.
I was selected as a scholarship student.
Scholarship students must keep up their grades.
What are the requirements to apply?
Anyone who meets the requirements can apply.
column2: Shartlarga mos kelgan har kim ariza bera oladi.

column1: If you're selected, they'll let you know by text.
If your TOPIK level is high, you can get a scholarship.
column2: TOPIK darajangiz yuqori boʻlsa, stipendiya olishingiz mumkin.

column1: I wrote about my dream in my personal statement.
A senior corrected my personal statement.
column2: Motivatsion xatimni katta kursdosh tuzatib berdi.

column1: What are the requirements for the international student scholarship?
column2: Xorijlik talabalar stipendiyasiga ariza berish shartlari qanday?

column1: It depends on the scholarship. The TOPIK scholarship is for level 4 or higher.
column2: Har bir stipendiyada har xil. TOPIK stipendiyasi 4-daraja va undan yuqorilar uchun.

column1: I got TOPIK level 4 last month!
Congratulations! The application period is short, so ask the International Office soon.
column2: Tabriklayman! Ariza berish muddati qisqa, tezroq Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan soʻrang.

column1: These are the basic words international students must know before working part-time. You learn more in the "아르바이트" (part-time jobs) area.
column2: Bu xorijlik talabalar qoʻshimcha ishga kirishdan oldin bilishi shart boʻlgan asosiy soʻzlar. Batafsil maʼlumotni "아르바이트" (qoʻshimcha ish) boʻlimida oʻrganasiz.

column1: For part-time jobs, international students must check the permit, the contract, the hourly wage and working hours.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish uchun xorijlik talabalar ruxsatnoma, mehnat shartnomasi, soatbay ish haqi va ish vaqtini albatta tekshirishi kerak.

column1: International students must get a part-time work permit before working. Working without one can lead to fines or visa problems.
column2: Xorijlik talabalar ishlashdan oldin vaqtincha ishlashga ruxsatnoma olishi shart. Ruxsatnomasiz ishlash jarima yoki viza muammolariga olib kelishi mumkin.

column1: How many hours you may work depends on your degree, year and Korean level (TOPIK). Check on HiKorea and with the International Office.
column2: Necha soat ishlash mumkinligi taʼlim bosqichingiz (bakalavr, magistratura), kursingiz va koreys tili darajangizga (TOPIK) bogʻliq. HiKorea va Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan aniqlang.
Dam olish kunlari qoʻshimcha ishda ishlayman.

column1: Because of my part-time job, I don't have enough time to study.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish tufayli oʻqishga vaqtim yetmayapti.

column1: I got a part-time work permit.
You must not work without a permit.
You apply for the part-time work permit after getting confirmation from the International Office.
column2: Vaqtincha ishlashga ruxsatnomaga Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimining tasdigʻini olgandan keyin ariza beriladi.

column1: The 2026 minimum hourly wage is 10,320 won.
column2: 2026-yilda eng kam soatbay ish haqi 10 320 von.

column1: The hourly wage must not be less than the minimum wage.
column2: Soatbay ish haqi eng kam ish haqidan past boʻlmasligi kerak.

column1: International students have a fixed limit on working hours.
I cut my working hours during exam period.
Be sure to get a copy of your employment contract.
column2: Mehnat shartnomasining nusxasini albatta olib qoʻying.

column1: You need an employment contract to apply for the permit.
column2: Ruxsatnomaga ariza berish uchun mehnat shartnomasi kerak.
haftalik dam olish kuni uchun toʻlov

column1: You can also get a weekly holiday allowance.
column2: Haftalik dam olish kuni uchun toʻlov ham olishingiz mumkin.

column1: If you work 15 hours or more a week, you get a weekly holiday allowance.
column2: Haftasiga 15 soat yoki undan koʻp ishlasangiz, haftalik dam olish kuni uchun toʻlov beriladi.

column1: I asked the owner about the weekly holiday allowance.
column2: Xoʻjayindan haftalik dam olish toʻlovi haqida soʻradim.

column1: Are you an international student? Do you have a part-time work permit?
column2: Xorijlik talabamisiz? Vaqtincha ishlashga ruxsatnomangiz bormi?

column1: I'm going to apply after signing the contract. What's the hourly wage?
column2: Shartnomani imzolab, keyin ariza bermoqchiman. Soatbay ish haqi qancha?

column1: Minimum wage. Let's write the employment contract first.
column2: Eng kam ish haqi. Avval mehnat shartnomasini tuzaylik.

column1: OK. I'll start working once the permit is issued.
column2: Xoʻp. Ruxsatnoma chiqishi bilan ishni boshlayman.

column1: Words for the kinds of Jeonju University scholarships and their conditions, based on the school's scholarship guide.
column2: Chonju universiteti stipendiyalarining turlari va shartlari haqidagi soʻzlar, universitetning stipendiya yoʻriqnomasi asosida.

column1: At Jeonju University the academic excellence scholarship is 30% of tuition (12+ credits and a GPA of 3.0+ last semester), and the department top-student scholarship is 65% (GPA 3.5+). The school selects students by grades and takes it off the next semester's bill.
column2: Chonju universitetida aʼlo oʻqish stipendiyasi kontraktning 30% ini (oʻtgan semestrda 12+ kredit va 3,0+ oʻrtacha ball), kafedra birinchisi stipendiyasi esa 65% ini (3,5+ oʻrtacha ball) tashkil etadi. Universitet talabalarni baholariga qarab tanlaydi va keyingi semestr hisob-varagʻidan chegirib tashlaydi.

column1: There are also scholarships for StarT program points (3,000 won a point), ambassadors, student council officers and volunteering. All scholarships together can't be more than your tuition.
column2: StarT dasturi ballari (bir ball uchun 3 000 von), universitet elchilari, talabalar kengashi aʼzolari va koʻngillilik uchun ham stipendiyalar bor. Barcha stipendiyalar jami kontrakt summasidan oshmasligi kerak.

column1: Scholarship notices are posted on the school website (Notices › Scholarships) and on your college office board. Also ask the international office which scholarships international students can get.
column2: Stipendiya eʼlonlari universitet veb-saytida (Eʼlonlar › Stipendiyalar) va fakultet idorasi taxtasida joylanadi. Xorijlik talabalar qaysi stipendiyalarni olishi mumkinligini Xalqaro hamkorlik boʻlimidan ham albatta soʻrang.

column1: I got an academic excellence scholarship.
The academic excellence scholarship is 30 percent of tuition.
You need 12 or more credits last semester and a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
column2: Oʻtgan semestrda 12 yoki undan koʻp kredit olgan va oʻrtacha balingiz 3,0 yoki undan yuqori boʻlishi kerak.

column1: Who is the top student in our department?
The department's top student gets 65 percent of tuition as a scholarship.
column2: Kafedraning eng aʼlochi talabasi kontraktning 65 foizini stipendiya sifatida oladi.

column1: My friend came first in the department this semester.
column2: Doʻstim bu semestrda kafedrada birinchi oʻrinni oldi.

column1: How much is tuition for one semester?
A scholarship can't be more than your tuition.
column2: Stipendiya oʻqish toʻlovidan koʻp boʻlishi mumkin emas.

column1: With a scholarship, the tuition on your bill goes down.
column2: Stipendiya olsangiz, hisob-varaqdagi oʻqish toʻlovi kamayadi.

column1: The scholarship is written on the bill.
Check the bill and pay the fees within the period.
column2: Hisob-varaqni koʻrib, toʻlovni muddat ichida amalga oshiring.

column1: I collected points in the StarT program.
They give a 3,000-won scholarship for each point.
column2: Har bir ball uchun 3 000 vondan stipendiya berishadi.

column1: The more points you have, the bigger the scholarship.
column2: Ballar qancha koʻp boʻlsa, stipendiya ham shuncha katta.

column1: Ambassadors get a scholarship for their work.
Student council officers can get a scholarship too.
column2: Talabalar kengashi aʼzolari ham stipendiya olishi mumkin.

column2: Men Myanmadan kelgan Aungman. Chonju universiteti talabasiman.

column1: I'm Dilnoza from Uzbekistan. I'm studying business.
column2: Men Oʻzbekistondan kelgan Dilnozaman. Biznes boshqaruvini oʻrganyapman.

column1: I have worked at a cafe.
I've worked in a restaurant in my country.
I haven't worked in Korea, but I can learn fast.
column2: Koreyada ishlamaganman, lekin tez oʻrgana olaman.

column1: If I get permission, I can start next week.
column2: Ruxsat olsam, keyingi haftadan boshlay olaman.

column1: I can start in July when vacation begins.
My Korean isn't good yet, but I'll work hard.
column2: Koreys tilim hali yaxshi emas, lekin astoydil ishlayman.

column1: If you hire me, I'll really work hard.
column2: Meni ishga olsangiz, chindan ham astoydil ishlayman.

column1: I look forward to working with you
I look forward to working with you.
Boss, I look forward to working with you.
It's my first time and I don't know much, but please guide me.
column2: Birinchi marta va koʻp narsani bilmayman, iltimos, yoʻl-yoʻriq koʻrsatib turing.

column1: I'm Aung from Myanmar. I'm a second-year student at Jeonju University.
column2: Men Myanmadan kelgan Aungman. Chonju universitetining 2-kurs talabasiman.

column1: Yes, I've worked at a cafe in Myanmar.
I can start as soon as I get permission. I'll work hard.
column2: Ruxsat olishim bilan ishni boshlay olaman. Astoydil ishlayman.

column1: Part-time jobs also need a written work contract. Learn the words on a contract.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish uchun ham yozma mehnat shartnomasi kerak. Shartnomadagi soʻzlarni oʻrganing.

column1: Check the period, place, duties, hours and wage, then sign the contract.
column2: Muddat, joy, vazifalar, ish vaqti va ish haqini tekshiring, keyin shartnomani imzolang.

column1: Even for a part-time job, the employer must make a written contract and give you a copy.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish boʻlsa ham, ish beruvchi yozma shartnoma tuzishi va sizga bir nusxasini berishi shart.

column1: Check that the wage, hours, days off and payday are on the contract.
column2: Ish haqi, ish vaqti, dam olish kunlari va maosh kuni shartnomada yozilganini tekshiring.

column1: You also need the contract to apply for part-time work permission.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ishga ruxsat olish uchun ham shartnoma kerak.

column1: Boss, when do we write the contract?
Get a copy of the contract and keep it safe.
column2: Shartnomaning bir nusxasini olib, yaxshi saqlang.

column1: How long is the contract period?
The contract runs from March to June.
Check that the contract period matches your permission period.
column2: Shartnoma muddati ruxsat muddatingizga mos kelishini tekshiring.

column1: The workplace is a cafe in Hyoja-dong.
You can only work at the workplace on your permission.
column2: Faqat ruxsatnomangizda koʻrsatilgan ish joyida ishlay olasiz.

column1: The duties are working the register and arranging goods.
column2: Vazifalar — kassada ishlash va mahsulotlarni terish.

column1: The duties on the contract are different from the real work.
column2: Shartnomadagi vazifalar haqiqiy ishdan farq qiladi.

column1: I read it all and signed.
If there's something you don't understand, ask before you sign.
column2: Tushunmagan narsangiz boʻlsa, imzolashdan oldin soʻrang.

column1: If you work five hours, you must get a break.
column2: Besh soat ishlasangiz, tanaffus berilishi shart.

column1: John, this is the work contract. Please read it.
column2: Jon, bu mehnat shartnomasi. Oʻqib chiqing.

column1: The hours are Saturday and Sunday, ten to four?
column2: Ish vaqti shanba va yakshanba, oʻndan toʻrtgachami?

column1: Yes, and the break is 30 minutes.
Right. Sign here. You keep one copy.
column2: Toʻgʻri. Shu yerga imzo qoʻying. Bir nusxasi sizda qoladi.

column1: Part-time pay is counted by the hour. Also learn about the minimum wage and weekly holiday pay.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish haqi soatbay hisoblanadi. Eng kam ish haqi va haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi haqida ham bilib oling.

column1: Your wage must be at least the minimum wage, and 15+ hours a week gives weekly holiday pay.
column2: Ish haqingiz kamida eng kam ish haqiga teng boʻlishi kerak, haftasiga 15+ soat ishlasangiz, haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi beriladi.

column1: The 2026 minimum wage is 10,320 won per hour (Ministry of Employment and Labor notice). It changes every January.
column2: 2026-yilda eng kam ish haqi soatiga 10,320 von (Bandlik va mehnat vazirligi eʼloni). U har yili yanvarda oʻzgaradi.

column1: If your scheduled hours are 15 or more a week and you come on all scheduled days, you are entitled to weekly holiday pay (주휴수당).
column2: Rejalashtirilgan ish soatlaringiz haftasiga 15 yoki undan koʻp boʻlsa va barcha belgilangan kunlarda ishga kelsangiz, haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi (주휴수당) olish huquqiga egasiz.

column1: International students have the same rights to minimum wage and weekly holiday pay as Korean workers.
column2: Chet ellik talabalar ham eng kam ish haqi va haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi boʻyicha koreys ishchilari bilan teng huquqli.

column1: The 2026 minimum wage is 10,320 won an hour.
column2: 2026-yilda eng kam ish haqi soatiga 10,320 von.

column1: International students must not be paid less than the minimum wage either.
column2: Chet ellik talabalarga ham eng kam ish haqidan kam toʻlanmasligi kerak.

column1: I bought books with my part-time pay.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish haqimga kitob sotib oldim.

column1: I think this month's pay was calculated wrong.
column2: Menimcha, bu oygi ish haqim notoʻgʻri hisoblangan.
Haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi nima?

column1: If you work 15 hours or more a week, you can get weekly holiday pay.
column2: Haftasiga 15 soat yoki undan koʻp ishlasangiz, haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovini olishingiz mumkin.

column1: If you come on all your scheduled days, you get weekly holiday pay.
column2: Barcha belgilangan kunlarda ishga kelsangiz, haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovi beriladi.
Tungi ish kechki soat 10 dan boshlanadi.

column1: During the semester, night shifts can be hard on your studies.
column2: Semestr davomida tungi smena oʻqishingizga xalal berishi mumkin.

column1: You calculate it as hourly wage times hours.
column2: Soatbay ish haqini soatlar soniga koʻpaytirib hisoblaysiz.

column1: You can calculate weekly holiday pay with an app.
column2: Haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovini ilova orqali hisoblash mumkin.

column1: It's extra pay if you work 15 hours or more a week.
column2: Haftasiga 15 soat yoki undan koʻp ishlasangiz, qoʻshimcha beriladigan pul.

column1: Then you can get it. What's your hourly wage?
column2: Unda olasiz. Soatbay ish haqingiz qancha?

column1: That's the 2026 minimum wage. Check the weekly holiday pay on your pay slip too.
column2: Bu 2026-yilgi eng kam ish haqi. Ish haqi varaqangizdan haftalik dam olish kuni toʻlovini ham tekshiring.

column1: Part-time pay usually goes into your bank account. Learn words about payday and pay slips.
column2: Qoʻshimcha ish haqi odatda bank hisobingizga tushadi. Maosh kuni va ish haqi varaqasi haqidagi soʻzlarni oʻrganing.

column1: On payday the money goes into your account; check it with the pay slip.
column2: Maosh kuni pul hisobingizga tushadi; uni ish haqi varaqasi bilan tekshiring.

column1: By law, wages must be paid at least once a month on a fixed day.
column2: Qonunga koʻra, ish haqi oyiga kamida bir marta, belgilangan kunda toʻlanishi kerak.

column1: Employers must give you a pay slip. Check the hours and amounts.
column2: Ish beruvchi sizga ish haqi varaqasini berishi shart. Soatlar va summalarni tekshiring.

column1: Write down your work days and hours in a notebook or on your phone.
column2: Ish kunlaringiz va soatlaringizni daftar yoki telefoningizga yozib boring.

column1: Payday is the 10th of every month.
Payday has passed, but the money hasn't come in yet.
column2: Maosh kuni oʻtdi, lekin pul hali tushmadi.

column1: You can open an account at a bank near school.
column2: Universitet yaqinidagi bankda hisob ochishingiz mumkin.

column1: Bring your residence card and passport when opening an account.
column2: Hisob ochayotganda ID karta va pasportingizni olib boring.

column1: Please tell me your account number.
I sent my account number by text.
If the account number is wrong, you can't get paid.
column2: Hisob raqami notoʻgʻri boʻlsa, pul ololmaysiz.

column1: My pay was deposited in my account.
Boss, I don't think the payment has come in yet.
The pay slip shows the hours worked.
column2: Ish haqi varaqasida ishlangan soatlar koʻrsatilgan.

column1: Check the hourly wage and holiday pay on the pay slip.
column2: Ish haqi varaqasidan soatbay ish haqi va dam olish kuni toʻlovini tekshiring.

column1: A little tax was taken out of my pay.
If you don't know why tax was taken, ask the boss.
column2: Nega soliq ushlanganini bilmasangiz, xoʻjayindan soʻrang.

column1: Boss, when is payday this month?
column2: Xoʻjayin, bu oy maosh kuni qachon?

column1: The 10th of every month. Did you give me your account number?
Not yet. I'll send it by text.
OK. I'll deposit it and give you a pay slip too.
column2: Yaxshi. Pulni oʻtkazaman va ish haqi varaqasini ham beraman.

column1: Convenience store jobs are popular with students. Learn the words used there.
column2: Doʻkonchada qoʻshimcha ishlash talabalar orasida mashhur. U yerda ishlatiladigan soʻzlarni oʻrganing.

column1: At a convenience store you work the counter, stock shelves, check expiry dates and change shifts.
column2: Doʻkonchada kassada ishlaysiz, javonlarni toʻldirasiz, yaroqlilik muddatini tekshirasiz va smena almashasiz.

column1: There are many convenience stores near campus, so it's easy to work after class.
column2: Kampus yaqinida doʻkonchalar koʻp, shuning uchun darsdan keyin ishlash qulay.

column1: Night shifts can be tiring during the semester. Also think about your hour limit.
column2: Semestr davomida tungi smena charchatishi mumkin. Soat chegarangizni ham hisobga oling.

column1: At shift change, check the cash and cigarette count together.
column2: Smena almashganda naqd pul va sigaretlar sonini birga tekshiring.

column1: There are many customers at the counter.
Please refill the bags next to the counter.
When new goods arrive, you have to stock them.
column2: Yangi mahsulot kelsa, javonga terishingiz kerak.

column1: Put the items with the shortest expiry date at the front.
column2: Yaroqlilik muddati eng qisqa mahsulotlarni oldinga qoʻying.

column1: This milk is past its expiry date.
column2: Bu sutning yaroqlilik muddati oʻtib ketgan.

column1: At night I check the expiry dates on the triangle gimbap and sort them.
column2: Kechasi uchburchak kimbaplarning yaroqlilik muddatini koʻrib, saralayman.

column1: I'll see if there's stock in the storeroom.
I counted the stock and reported to the boss.
When we change shifts, we count the money together.
The next worker came late, so I couldn't change shifts.
column2: Keyingi ishchi kech keldi, shuning uchun smena almasha olmadim.

column1: I'd like to send a parcel.
You can send parcels at the convenience store.
I weigh the parcel box and enter it in the machine.
Aung, please start by stocking the drinks today.
column2: Aung, bugun avval ichimliklarni javonga terib qoʻying.

column1: OK. I put the short expiry ones in front, right?
column2: Xoʻp. Yaroqlilik muddati qisqalarini oldinga qoʻyaman, toʻgʻrimi?

column1: Right. Do we have cola in stock?
There are two boxes in the storeroom.
Good. You change shifts with Jinha at ten.
column2: Yaxshi. Soat oʻnda Jinha bilan smena almashasiz.

column1: Learn what to say to customers at the convenience store register.
column2: Doʻkoncha kassasida xaridorlarga nima deyishni oʻrganing.

column1: At the register you ask about bags, cards, receipts and points.
column2: Kassada paket, karta, chek va ballar haqida soʻraysiz.

column1: Use polite forms like -세요 and -드릴까요? with customers.
column2: Xaridorlarga -세요 va -드릴까요? kabi hurmat shakllarini ishlating.

column1: In Korea you can buy alcohol and cigarettes from the year you turn 19. Always check ID.
column2: Koreyada 19 yoshga toʻladigan yildan boshlab spirtli ichimlik va sigaret sotib olish mumkin. Har doim hujjatni tekshiring.

column1: If an unfamiliar payment comes up, say 잠시만요 and ask a senior coworker.
column2: Notanish toʻlov usuli chiqsa, 잠시만요 deb, tajribali hamkasbingizdan soʻrang.

column1: Do you need a bag? It's 100 won.
You have a lot of things. Do you need a big bag?
column2: Narsalaringiz koʻp ekan. Katta paket kerakmi?

column1: The card didn't work. Please insert it again.
column2: Karta oʻtmadi. Yana bir bor qoʻying.

column1: Shall I throw away the receipt?
You need the receipt to exchange it, so I'll give it to you.
column2: Almashtirish uchun chek kerak, shuning uchun sizga beraman.

column1: Would you like to collect points?
Do you have a points card?
I'll add points with your phone number.
Sorry, but please show me your ID.
You must check ID before selling alcohol and cigarettes.
column2: Spirtli ichimlik va sigaretni hujjatni tekshirib, keyin sotish kerak.

column1: Shall I heat it up for you?
Shall I heat the lunch box?
The microwave is over there. Heat it for about a minute.
column2: Mikrotoʻlqinli pech ana u yerda. Bir daqiqacha isiting.

column1: OK. Do you need a bag?
No, it's fine. I'll pay by card.
column2: Yoʻq, kerak emas. Karta bilan toʻlayman.

column1: Please insert your card. Would you like a receipt?
Learn what to say when a customer is looking for something.
column2: Xaridor biror narsa qidirayotganda nima deyishni oʻrganing.

column1: Tell customers where items are, when they're sold out and what's on offer.
column2: Xaridorlarga mahsulot qayerdaligi, tugaganligi va qanday aksiya borligini ayting.

column1: Common offers: 1+1 (buy one get one) and 2+1 (buy two get one).
column2: Koʻp uchraydigan aksiyalar: 1+1 (bittasini olsangiz, bittasi bepul) va 2+1 (ikkitasini olsangiz, bittasi bepul).

column1: If the customer is a foreigner, you can help in English. That's a strength.
column2: Xaridor chet ellik boʻlsa, ingliz tilida yordam bera olasiz. Bu sizning ustunligingiz.

column1: Excuse me, are you looking for something?
If you're looking for something, please let me know.
Milk is at the very bottom of that fridge.
column2: Sut ana u muzlatgichning eng pastida.

column1: Sorry, that milk is sold out right now.
column2: Kechirasiz, u sut hozir tugab qolgan.

column1: It's sold out now, but more comes in tomorrow morning.
column2: Hozir tugagan, lekin ertaga ertalab yana keladi.

column1: This drink is buy one get one free.
column2: Bu ichimlikka bittasini olsangiz, bittasi bepul aksiyasi bor.

column1: If you buy two, you get one more free.
It's 1+1, so please bring one more.
column2: Bu 1+1, shuning uchun yana bittasini olib keling.

column1: If it's the same price, you can bring another flavor.
column2: Narxi bir xil boʻlsa, boshqa taʼmlisini olib kelsangiz ham boʻladi.

column1: Excuse me, where is the milk?
It's in that fridge over there.
Sorry, it's sold out right now. It comes in tomorrow.
column2: Kechirasiz, hozir tugab qolgan. Ertaga keladi.

column1: That's buy one get one free. Please bring one more.
column2: Unga bittasini olsangiz, bittasi bepul aksiyasi bor. Yana bittasini olib keling.

column1: To work at a cafe you need to know the menu words.
column2: Kafeda ishlash uchun menyudagi soʻzlarni bilishingiz kerak.

column1: You can talk about cafe drinks, ice, sizes and extra shots.
column2: Kafe ichimliklari, muz, oʻlcham va qoʻshimcha shot haqida gapira olasiz.

column1: 따뜻한 거 means hot and 차가운 거 or 아이스 means iced.
column2: 따뜻한 거 — issiq, 차가운 거 yoki 아이스 — muzli degani.

column1: Take a photo of the menu and memorize it to learn fast.
column2: Tez oʻrganish uchun menyuni rasmga olib, yod oling.

column1: If a customer asks about allergies, tell them the exact ingredients.
column2: Xaridor allergiya haqida soʻrasa, tarkibni aniq ayting.

column1: For an americano, pull the shot first and add water.
column2: Amerikano uchun avval shot tayyorlanadi, keyin suv qoʻshiladi.

column1: You make a latte by steaming milk.
A latte with soy milk costs 500 won more.
We ran out of ice, so I checked the ice machine.
column2: Muz tugab qoldi, shuning uchun muz mashinasini tekshirdim.

column1: Mark extra-shot orders on the cup.
column2: Qoʻshimcha shotli buyurtmalarni stakanga belgilab qoʻying.

column1: If you change the size, the price changes.
Take the dessert out of the fridge and put it on a plate.
Maria, it's your first day, right? Let's start with the menu.
column2: Mariya, bugun birinchi kuningiz, toʻgʻrimi? Menyudan boshlaymiz.

column1: OK. An americano is shots and water, right?
column2: Xoʻp. Amerikano — shot va suv, toʻgʻrimi?

column1: How much is an extra shot?
500 won. Desserts are in the fridge.
Learn the phrases for taking orders at a cafe.
column2: Kafeda buyurtma qabul qilishda ishlatiladigan iboralarni oʻrganing.

column1: At a cafe, ask the drink, hot or iced, for here or to go, and give the buzzer.
column2: Kafeda ichimlikni, issiq yoki muzliligini, shu yerdami yoki olib ketishmi, soʻrang va chaqiruv qurilmasini bering.

column1: Many cafes use mugs instead of disposable cups for customers staying in.
column2: Koʻp kafelar joyida oʻtirgan xaridorlarga bir martalik stakan oʻrniga krujka beradi.

column1: Repeat the order back to the customer to avoid mistakes.
column2: Xato boʻlmasligi uchun buyurtmani xaridorga qaytarib ayting.

column1: Many shops use kiosks. Help customers who find them difficult.
column2: Koʻp doʻkonlarda kiosk orqali buyurtma beriladi. Qiynalgan xaridorlarga yordam bering.

column1: Hello, may I take your order?
Look at the menu and take your time ordering.
Would you like it hot or iced?
Would you like the latte hot?
I'll make it iced. Normal ice?
column2: Muzli qilib beraman. Muz odatdagidek boʻlsinmi?

column1: If you're drinking in the store, I'll give it to you in a mug.
Here's your buzzer. Come when it rings.
The buzzer rings when your drink is ready, so have a seat and wait.
column2: Ichimligingiz tayyor boʻlganda qurilma jiringlaydi, oʻtirib kuting.

column1: Customer number 35, your drink is ready.
Your drink is ready. It's hot, so be careful.
It's busy, so it'll take a bit long. Please wait a moment.
column2: Mijozlar koʻp, shuning uchun biroz vaqt oladi. Biroz kutib turing.

column1: I'll bring the cake out. Please wait a moment.
column2: Tortni olib chiqaman. Biroz kutib turing.

column1: OK, one iced latte to go. Come when the buzzer rings.
column2: Xoʻp, bitta muzli latte olib ketish uchun. Chaqiruv qurilmasi jiringlasa, keling.

column1: At closing time you clean and tidy up. Learn the words for closing.
column2: Kafe yopilish vaqtida tozalash va tartibga keltirish qilinadi. Yopilishga oid soʻzlarni oʻrganing.

column1: At closing you wash dishes, clean the machine, sort recycling and tidy up.
column2: Yopilishda idish yuvasiz, mashinani tozalaysiz, chiqindilarni saralaysiz va tartibga keltirasiz.

column1: Closing work is working time. You should be paid for the time you work after closing.
column2: Yopilish ishlari ham ish vaqti hisoblanadi. Yopilgandan keyin ishlagan vaqtingiz uchun ham haq olishingiz kerak.

column1: Separate food waste, general waste and recycling.
column2: Oziq-ovqat chiqindisi, umumiy chiqindi va qayta ishlanadigan chiqindini alohida tashlang.

column1: Take a photo of the closing checklist; it's handy.
column2: Yopilish roʻyxatini rasmga olib qoʻying, qulay boʻladi.

column1: Before closing, write down how many cakes are left.
column2: Yopilishdan oldin nechta tort qolganini yozib qoʻying.

column1: Please wash the mugs right away.
On busy days the dishes keep piling up.
column2: Mijoz koʻp kunlari idishlar toʻplanib ketaveradi.

column1: I turned off the coffee machine.
The coffee machine is hot, so wear gloves.
Wash the cloth and hang it up.
We use separate cloths for tables and for the bar.
column2: Stollar va bar uchun alohida lattalar ishlatamiz.

column1: Rinse plastic cups and put them in recycling.
column2: Plastik stakanlarni chayib, qayta ishlashga tashlang.

column1: In Jeonju, the days and times for recycling are fixed.
column2: Chonjuda chiqindilarni saralab tashlash kunlari va vaqti belgilangan.

column1: Please arrange the cups by size.
Tidy the ingredients and leave a note for the next person.
column2: Keyingi odam uchun masalliqlarni tartibga keltirib, eslatma qoldiring.

column1: Tom, let's do the closing together today.
OK. I'll start with the dishes.
Good. I'll clean the coffee machine.
Where do we put the recycling?
Behind the shop. When you're done, please wash the cloths too.
column2: Doʻkonning orqasiga. Tugatgach, lattalarni ham yuvib qoʻying.

column1: Learn phrases for greeting guests in a restaurant.
column2: Restoranda mehmonlarni kutib olish iboralarini oʻrganing.

column1: Greet guests, ask how many and about reservations, then show them to a table.
column2: Mehmonlar bilan salomlashing, necha kishi ekani va bron haqida soʻrang, keyin stolga kuzatib qoʻying.

column1: Say 어서 오세요 clearly when guests come in.
column2: Mehmonlar kirganda 어서 오세요 deb aniq ayting.

column1: 분 is the polite word for 사람; ask guests 몇 분이세요?
column2: 분 — 사람 soʻzining hurmat shakli; mehmonlardan 몇 분이세요? deb soʻrang.

column1: Many restaurants bring water and a wet towel first.
column2: Koʻp restoranlar avval suv va nam sochiq olib keladi.

column1: For dishes not on the menu, I'll ask the boss.
column2: Menyuda yoʻq taomlar haqida xoʻjayindan soʻrayman.

column1: Welcome. We have a few seats right now.
column2: Xush kelibsiz. Hozir bir nechta boʻsh joy bor.

column1: How many? If you're four, the inner seats are good.
column2: Necha kishisiz? Toʻrt kishi boʻlsangiz, ichkaridagi joylar yaxshi.

column1: We're cleaning, so please sit here in a moment.
column2: Hozir tozalayapmiz, biroz keyin shu yerga oʻtiring.

column1: Do you have a reservation? What's your name?
There are many reservations today, so you'll have to wait 30 minutes.
column2: Bugun bronlar koʻp, shuning uchun 30 daqiqa kutishingizga toʻgʻri keladi.

column1: I'll clear the table. Please wait a moment.
Please write your name on the waiting list and wait a moment.
column2: Kutish roʻyxatiga ismingizni yozib, biroz kuting.

column1: That's fine. Please sit here. Here's the menu.
column2: Mayli. Bu yerga oʻtiring. Mana menyu.
